title: R2. Gate code-doc execution (signer allowlist)
description: From architecture-review.md §8 R2 (P0). Orchestrator and ComputeRunner refuse to compile a source doc whose introducing commit isn't signed by a configured identity. Full sandboxing is a project; the allowlist is a weekend. Converts 'any write anywhere = RCE' into 'key compromise = RCE'.
design:
Converged design — docs/trust-and-attenuation.md (§2 Gate B).

PLACEMENT: gate lives INSIDE SourceDoc.compile — the narrow waist BOTH callers share (ComputeRunner AND Orchestrator; the Orchestrator reads latest_commit itself and skips SourceDoc.read, so a read-helper gate would miss it). compile fetches the introducing commit and refuses pre-compile unless Trust.authorized?(commit,:execute,scope). Reuses R1's seam.

SECOND EXECUTE INGRESS: the Orchestrator walks EVERY dir's __processes.json, so process-declaration must also be execute-gated, and the :sandbox_exec $secret:KEY resolution must require :execute (a distinct :secrets caveat is a phase-3 refinement). Federated write today = RCE + secret exfiltration, not just RCE.

SOUNDNESS — head-signature ALONE is UNSOUND (write-time laundering): the edit flow is reconstruct-full-doc -> mutate -> encode_update(FULL state) -> commit, so a trusted :execute-holder editing a code doc pulls an earlier untrusted-but-:write contributor's injected bytes under their own trusted head signature. Sound rule:
 (a) AUTHORITATIVE: every commit contributing to the code doc since the trusted baseline must be signed by an :execute-holder; per-doc watermark cache keeps the steady-state walk cheap. Only check sound even if a doc is reclassified as code after write.
 (b) DEFENSE-IN-DEPTH / fast path: Gate A requires :execute (not just :write) to WRITE a code doc (decidable via content-type/schema-entry) so untrusted bytes never land. (b) alone has a hole (doc later referenced as source_uuid), so (a) is the floor; (b) makes (a)'s walk trivial in the common case.

LOAD-BEARING INVARIANT: code docs store full-state updates per commit (encode_update full state). A delta-writing path touching a code doc already breaks reconstruct_snapshot, so name and ideally assert the invariant. NOTE: capability gates 'may run', not 'what running can do' — full BEAM/OS privilege remains until phase-4 sandboxing.
close_reason: R2 COMPLETE (per boss-clod relay 2026-06-10). Implemented by commonplace-trust in 3 commits on branch trust-attenuation in /home/jes/commonplace-trust (HEAD f8f70c0): (1) Gate B in SourceDoc.compile — contributor-chain walk, laundering-proof, cache-hit-safe (refuses pre-compile unless Trust.authorized?(commit,:execute,scope), per the CX-tdkq.2 design seam); (2) __processes.json declaration gate (:sandbox_exec + $secret protection; revocation stops running procs); (3) deterministic LRU stamps (fixed a pre-existing flake — hardens the R8c compile-cache LRU from CX-tdkq.8). Full suite ~1460 green, warnings-as-errors clean. NOTE: code lives on the trust-attenuation branch, NOT yet merged to commonplace main (68436ab) — bead closed for work-complete; the code merge is a separate step jes/boss coordinate.

title: R1. Draw the trust boundary in code, not docs
description: From architecture-review.md §8 R1 (P0). Wire Signing.verify_commit/1 into the import path behind a per-workspace policy knob (accept_unsigned: true|false), and route identity docs through SiblingMerger so the key store converges. Functions all exist — integration, not invention. Until then, add a one-line trust banner to README/serve startup: all peers and all code docs are fully trusted.
design:
Converged design — docs/trust-and-attenuation.md on commonplace-plan (§2 Gate A, §4, §7).

THE SEAM: R1 introduces Trust.authorized?(commit, verb, scope) :: :ok | {:error,_}. Phase-1 body = flat per-workspace trusted-identity allowlist. BOTH gates (import + execute) call ONLY this boundary, so phase-3 (capability chain) swaps the body without touching gates. This is the load-bearing structural decision.

GATE A placement: compose the signature check into the DEFAULT validation chain inside handle_validated_import (verify_id -> Trust.authorized?(commit,:write,scope) -> Namespace validator). Do NOT ride the pluggable validator_for opts seam — a caller passing validator:stub bypasses it (already bypasses namespace today); opts stays a test-only seam. accept_unsigned:true|false per-workspace knob (default-open now, default-closed once federation is live).

PREREQUISITE (gate is MOOT without it): Document.Server handle_info({:remote_commit,...}) (server.ex:292) ignores import_commit's return and applies update + set_latest regardless. Route it through the gate and RESPECT the verdict. Also fix the verify_commit/2 nil-signature crash (unsigned guard is only on the /1 head). Plus route identity docs through SiblingMerger so the keystore converges.

ANCHOR: trust anchor = workspace-LOCAL config (root key material + the knob), NOT synced identity docs — __identities__ public_keys are peer-writable with zero auth, so they cannot anchor trust. Framing for the README banner: a BEAM cluster is a single trust domain (any cookie-holder can RPC create_commit); federation is a NEW ingress seam and import_commit+sigcheck is the only door.
close_reason: R1 COMPLETE (per boss-clod relay 2026-06-10). Implemented by commonplace-trust in 5 commits on branch trust-attenuation in the worktree /home/jes/commonplace-trust (diff main..trust-attenuation): (1) nil-sig guard, (2) Trust.authorized?/3 seam (the load-bearing boundary both gates call — see CX-tdkq.1 design), (3) Gate A wired into the import default chain, (4) Document.Server remote_commit bypass fix, (5) identity-doc SiblingMerger convergence. Core suite ~1452 green + 102 MCP, warnings-as-errors clean. NOTE: code lives on the trust-attenuation branch (not yet merged to commonplace main at 32de283); bead closed for the work-complete, the code merge is a separate step jes/boss coordinate. Unblocks downstream trust beads that depend on R1.

title: Federation Phase C: commit-exchange envelope over Phoenix Channels (two local workspaces)
description: Thin (~500-800 LOC) commit-exchange over the existing commonplace_web Phoenix endpoint between two LOCAL separate-rooted workspaces. Envelope = commit + capability_proof (leaf cert CID) + inlined cert chain (availability). Receiving side feeds import_commit (the only door, unchanged). PULL-FIRST: CID-diff catch-up reusing NodeSync.catch_up (swap GenServer.call→HTTP); push (Channel broadcast) later. Thin transport auth (channel-join/HMAC, online "may you publish") kept DISTINCT from the import gate (offline "does this land"). Full agent round-trip: agent mints key → human cap-delegates scoped cert → agent signs+publishes commit → peer strict Gate A verifies sig+chain+author-binding → lands. ⚠️ include a per-peer rate-limit/scope on the pending_imports queue (a hostile peer flooding :awaiting_capability commits would fill the 1024 cap — federation-specific DoS; ref R11/CX-tdkq.11). Capstone: live two-workspace demo (accepted within grant; forged/over-broad/stolen-chain/expired/cross-epoch-unsigned all rejected over the real Channel path).
close_reason: PHASE C COMPLETE — commit-exchange federation between two separate-rooted local workspaces over a REAL HTTP socket (branch federate-for-real). C(i) Envelope wire format (a5e3acd): versioned JSON wrapper, base64(term_to_binary) payloads via binary_to_term([:safe]) — D12 fix (naive JSON breaks Commit.verify_id on atom-keyed metadata); certs inlined for availability; Envelope.for_commit walks the proof chain leaf→root. C(ii) HTTP endpoints on commonplace_web (34fc030): GET /federation/docs/:uuid/cids, POST .../commits, POST /federation/import — bearer-token plug (default-off ⇒ 403 when no peers configured; constant-time compare), cert id+sig verify BEFORE store, import through UNCHANGED import_commit, + the in-scope DoS guard FederationPeerBudget (fixed-window per-peer deferral counter 429s an :awaiting_capability flooder BEFORE pending_imports — bounds per-peer contribution to the global 1024 cap, ref R11). C(iii) PullClient (4283a57): CID-diff catch-up (NodeSync.catch_up shape, Req HTTP, transport injectable), commits via import_with_translation (same ingress as cluster: Gate A + node-signed cross-epoch translation + R11 pending queue unchanged), supervised only when :federation_pull peers configured. C(iv) ACCEPTANCE (dd1d0ac): two separate-rooted stores, REAL TCP (Bandit ephemeral port, real router+parsers), delegated agent commit federates A→B and lands ONLY because its chain verifies against the locally-pinned root at strict Gate A; wrong token 403s at the door. VERIFIED core 1548/0, web 70/0, mcp 106/0, warnings-clean. ⚠️ TRANSPORT DEVIATION: bead title says 'Phoenix Channels' but implemented as plain HTTP PULL — commonplace-plan's confirmed pull-first lean (msg 5091); Channels push layers on later if latency wants it. Dep: req added to apps/commonplace/mix.exs (already in umbrella lock via bots). Code on federate-for-real, NOT yet merged to main. Unblocks CX-orfw.2 (Phase D).

title: Trust phase 2.5: sign system-minted commits (snapshots + merges) with a node identity — strict-mode deployability
description:
Surfaced by R2. Ref docs/trust-and-attenuation.md [OPEN] I + §5 phase 2.5. R1+R2 enforce trust on USER commits, but two SYSTEM actors mint commits with no accountable signer, which breaks strict mode (accept_unsigned:false):
- Lazy-snapshot worker: snapshots sign only via the global SecretStore fallback (usually unsigned). An auto-snapshot landing on a code doc is a CONTRIBUTOR; the Gate B walk hits the unsigned snapshot baseline and DENIES → permanently bricks the code doc's executability in strict mode.
- Merge commits: CrossEpochMerge → Commit.new, never signed. A federated merge arrives unsigned → Gate A rejects it in strict mode → strict federation can't accept any merge.
Root cause is one thing: system-minted commits have no accountable signer. Resolution (lean): sign snapshots AND merges with a NODE IDENTITY (the node already has a local node_id), and have strict workspaces PIN node keys in trust.json alongside user keys — accountable signer without trusting peers. Weaker alternatives: exempt-but-verify snapshots (likely unsound — exempting re-opens laundering); disable auto-snapshot for code docs in strict workspaces (removes the Gate-B walk's commit_log-limit bound). This is THE gate on strict-mode rollout — flat-allowlist enforcement (R1/R2) is not usable in strict mode until this lands.
design: Snapshot worker + CrossEpochMerge each need a node SigningContext sourced from local config (node identity). trust.json grows an optional node-keys pin for strict workspaces. Sequence-wise this is the natural step that makes R1/R2 actually deployable in strict mode, ahead of phase-3 attenuation.
close_reason: Phase 2.5 COMPLETE — node-identity signing of system-minted commits (snapshots + merges) so R1/R2 are deployable in strict mode. Implemented by commonplace-trust on branch trust-attenuation (NodeIdentity per-workspace node signing identity; Trust auto-trusts the local node identity; node-sign at the write chokepoints — snapshot worker + CrossEpochMerge), MERGED to commonplace main at 34de418 (the R1+R2+2.5 trust tier is now on main, not just a branch). LIVE PROOF GREEN: 14/14 by-hand strict-mode gate checks passed (forgery, laundering, pwned-shell-out all refused live with real error returns); drift tests 342+50 = 0 failures. Per boss-clod relay 2026-06-10. Unblocks the phase-2.5 follow-ups CX-tdkq.25 (always-node-sign-system-kind) + CX-tdkq.26 (translator unsigned :regular).

title: Supervise Process.Orchestrator on boot (federation-gated)
description: Split from CX-tdkq.3 (R3). Putting Process.Orchestrator (the __processes.json/SmartDoc 'malleable software' engine) into the general Commonplace.Application supervision tree would auto-execute arbitrary substrate-declared code — including :sandbox_exec OS processes — on every boot, in every embedder (web app included), not just under `commonplace serve`. That is a trust-boundary EXPANSION, not a supervision detail: it belongs with the federation decision. BLOCKED on R1 (CX-tdkq.1 verify-on-import) + R2 (CX-tdkq.2 signer allowlist) — once code-doc execution is gated, supervising the Orchestrator on boot becomes safe. Today it's a bare unsupervised start_link in cli/serve.ex:54 (a crash there is unrecoverable). Scope when unblocked: named singleton (avoid double-run with serve), workspace-gated child, reconcile/remove serve.ex's manual start, decide which boot contexts should run declared processes.

title: R6. Backpressure and loop-safety for the reactive layer
description: From architecture-review.md §8 R6 (P1). Coalesce recomputes (drain the mailbox, compute once against latest state — read side already tolerates this), run computes async with a timeout, and add a cheap loop-breaker: a ViewCompute ignores commits whose update originated from its own writes, plus a depth/rate fuse that trips a view recomputing >N times/sec. Malleable software means users will wire cycles eventually (§5.5).
close_reason: R6 landed (926abbf): async single-flight + coalesce (burst→≤2 computes), async compute with timeout-kill + telemetry (hanging compute_fn no longer blocks the GenServer), and a sliding-window rate fuse that halts a runaway reactive cycle (the general loop-breaker catching single- and multi-view cycles). 3 deterministic tests, 1412 suite green. The 'ignore own-write echoes' efficiency refinement (needs commit-origin metadata through CommandRouter) split to a tracked follow-up — not safety-critical, the fuse covers loop-safety.

title: R4. Relieve the CommitStore
description: From architecture-review.md §8 R4 (P1; do-now-regardless). Three independent steps in order of cheapness: (a) serve reads outside the GenServer — CubDB snapshots support concurrent readers [START HERE]; (b) the already-acknowledged single-flight SnapshotWorker, replacing the debounce; (c) shard write serialization by doc-UUID hash across N coordinator processes — per-doc atomicity is the only invariant needing a serial point, and it's per-doc. The CommitStore singleton is the system's throughput ceiling (§5.2).

REMAINING: (b) single-flight SnapshotWorker replacing debounce; (c) shard write serialization by doc-UUID hash across N coordinators [large — changes the single serial point; may warrant its own design/decision].
close_reason: R4 do-now parts delivered: (a) reads served outside the GenServer via caller-side CubDB handle [c92f69f, +4 latent :not_found bug fixes]; (b) single-flight SnapshotWorker replacing the ETS debounce [a42edba]. Both fully tested, 1406 suite green. title: MUD: verb-output API needs docs (or convenience module)
description:
Workspace bot wrote a kindle.elx verb, compiled cleanly, but couldn't find the API to emit text back to the player or room. The convention (call Commonplace.MUD.World.tell/2 and broadcast_room/2,3 directly) works, but is not documented in moduledoc, not surfaced in the @verb editor's preamble, and not aliased in the verb's runtime ctx. The bow-cloak demo in tests works because the test author already knew World.broadcast_room — first-time authors don't.

Fix options (any one is sufficient):
- Verbs.elx moduledoc / @verb editor pre-fill should show a one-line example.
- Add Commonplace.MUD.Output module with tell(ctx, msg) / broadcast(ctx, msg) wrappers that pull player_uuid / current_room_uuid out of ctx, so verbs can call Output.tell(ctx, "...") without wiring args.
- Both.

Highest impact gap from the workspace build session — without a discoverable output path, in-world verbs are useless for malleability. Linked to CX-v55j as a P3-followup polish bead.
close_reason: Shipped at 6667e06. 6 new tests cover Output.tell/broadcast isolation, @dump here, look me, multi-word @dig+@name, verb_error single-copy each per actor/bystander.

title: MCP escript stale — predates M3-M7; workspace can't invoke_view_action against new shape
description:
apps/commonplace_mcp/commonplace_mcp escript dates Apr 25, before M3-M7 chat-substrate work shipped. Workspace claude (commonplaceclaude session) loads the escript at session start and uses it via the commonplace MCP tools. Stale escript means workspace's invoke_view_action calls hit the pre-M3 view-XML shape (no <arg from='..'/> children, no ArgResolver substrate path) and fail.

Per project memory feedback_relay_status_to_clod_squad: Claude Code registers MCP at session start; serve must be up before launching commonplaceclaude. title: Gold.Chain.attest crashes when called with CommitStoreClient routing module
description:
RedLog auto_commit handler crashes with :no_process error because Gold.Chain.attest calls direct GenServer.call(store, ...) where store=CommitStoreClient (a stateless routing MODULE, not a registered GenServer process). RedLog default store is CommitStoreClient.

Stack trace from /tmp/commonplace-workspace-serve.log:
** (stop) exited in: GenServer.call(Commonplace.Store.CommitStoreClient, {:latest_commit, ...}, 5000)
    ** (EXIT) no process: the process is not alive or there's no process currently associated with the given name
    (commonplace 0.1.0) lib/commonplace/gold/chain.ex:20: Commonplace.Gold.Chain.attest/2
    (commonplace 0.1.0) lib/commonplace/dataflow/red_log.ex:87: Commonplace.Dataflow.RedLog.maybe_attest/2

Impact: chat onramp GenServer terminates after each chat message commit. Onramp uses restart: :temporary so it stays dead — subsequent chat messages on the same room don't get audit-logged to _messages.log.

NOT a CommitStoreClient supervisor problem: CommitStoreClient is a stateless module. Gold.Chain incorrectly assumes 'store' is always a GenServer reference; needs normalization when given the routing module.

Fix shipped in this bead: Gold.Chain.normalize_store/1 substitutes CommitStoreClient → CommitStore (the actual local GenServer) for direct GenServer calls. Single-node attestation assumption acceptable for MVP; multi-node attestation routing is a substrate-followup if the use case surfaces.

title: Substrate: per-agent ed25519 key minting, binding, and SigningContext construction
description:
Substrate-tier infrastructure for per-agent signing keys.

WHY: Chat S2 (CX-o3r7) audit found that the signing call chain has plumbing for SigningContext but no actual per-agent keys to thread through it. Identity.register/4 today mints a presence-record YMap (name, type, first_seen, last_seen) but no keypair. Commit signing falls back to the global SecretStore (the human's key) or :unsigned. Without per-agent keys, every MCP-initiated commit either signs as the human (wrong attribution) or ships unsigned (no audit trail).

Per chat-room.md (commit 2c2ffb5 on commonplace-plan/main), v1 chat ships with placeholder signer_id 'mcp-agent@local'. This bead lands the substrate for swapping placeholder for real keys transparently — once it lands, V1/V2/V3 chat actions and the I1 verify helper start producing/verifying real signatures without code changes downstream.

Scope:
- Identity.register/4 (or sibling) mints an ed25519 keypair on first registration
- Private key storage (design decision in this bead — likely SecretStore keyed by identity_uuid; session-state alternative exists)
- presence_starter returns the binding suitable for SigningContext construction
- Lookup helper: Commonplace.Identity.signing_context_for_presence(presence_uuid)
- Key-rotation API surface (consumers of 'as-of' semantics in chat-room.md identity verification)
- Tests: key persistence across session restarts, key-rotation, lookup-after-rotation

- chat I1 (Commonplace.Chat.Identity.verify_message/2 helper)

title: Fork concurrency cap + timeout bump to prevent dist-Erlang heartbeat starvation
description:
Round 16 v1 revealed the actual day-killer: rapid fork retries pile up at CommandRouter, saturate serve's CommitStore, starve net_kernel's heartbeat, escript declares serve :nodedown after ~60s. Serve survived but lost dist link.

Diagnosis:
- CommandRouter.fork uses default 5s GenServer.call timeout
- Under load, individual fork takes 5-15s
- Escript times out → safe_invoke returns in-band error → workspace retries
- Retry queues behind the still-running first fork
- 3-4 concurrent forks pile on, all schedulers pinned, dist heartbeat misses, :nodedown

Fix (two parts, narrow):
1. Server-side dedup: CommandRouter tracks in-flight forks by source_uuid. Duplicate request returns {:error, :fork_in_progress} immediately — escript surfaces as in-band MCP error so agent can wait or surface to user. Eliminates pile-on.
2. Client-side timeout bump: escript's CommandRouter.fork wrapper uses 30s timeout instead of GenServer default 5s. Gives a single fork enough runway to complete without spurious in-band-timeout that triggers retry.

Acceptance:
- Concurrent forks of same source: second returns :fork_in_progress
- Concurrent forks of different sources: both succeed
- After first fork completes, repeat fork of same source succeeds  
- Workspace stress-test (rapid-fire fork loop) doesn't trigger :nodedown
- All existing fork tests pass
notes: Parent: CX-0nkq queue-contention triage. Round 16 v1 revealed cat-of-fork-of-fork was a red herring — actual killer was fork retry storm starving dist-Erlang.
close_reason: Verified across workspace MCP smoke rounds 13-17 — fork retry storm gone, MCP session resilient, reflog overhead eliminated. CX-0nkq's user-visible symptoms all addressed by these three sub-fixes.

title: MCP session dies on tools/list, resources/list, resources/read crashes
description:
anubis_server.ex handle_request only wraps tools/call in safe_tool_call (the CX-0nkq crash isolation). The other three branches — tools/list, resources/list, resources/read — propagate :exit straight to anubis's session GenServer, which tears down the stdio transport.

Reproduced (round 13, post CX-71ej): with serve quiet at 3.4% CPU, batch 2 produced 'all tools gone' on workspace's MCP. Most plausible: one tools/list call hit a transient CommitStore call timeout (CRDT tools schema read), :exit propagated, session died.

Fix: wrap tools/list, resources/list, resources/read in the same try/catch :exit/:error/:throw shape as safe_tool_call, returning an in-band MCP error response instead of letting the exit propagate.

Acceptance:
- Tools.list() raising or exiting returns a tools/list error response (or a degraded-but-non-empty list) instead of killing the session
- Resources/list and resources/read symmetric
- Existing MCP test suite passes
- Workspace round-13-batch-2 repro: session survives, tools still listed
notes: Parent: CX-0nkq narrow-fix follow-on. After CX-71ej shipped, the symptom changed from per-tool timeouts to session-level deaths, exposing the unprotected handle_request branches.
close_reason: Verified across workspace MCP smoke rounds 13-17 — fork retry storm gone, MCP session resilient, reflog overhead eliminated. CX-0nkq's user-visible symptoms all addressed by these three sub-fixes.

title: CX-c2bx: file as bead — :global overlapping-partition kicks short-lived nodes
description:
OTP 25+ defaults kernel.prevent_overlapping_partitions to true. Each MCP escript invocation (and each commonplace CLI command) starts a fresh short-lived BEAM node that joins the cluster, RPCs to serve, then exits. The :global heuristic mistakes this for a network partition and forcibly disconnects the node, surfacing as MCP 'Connection closed' errors.

**Diagnosed from serve log line:**
  'global' at node :commonplace_<hash>@commonplace requested disconnect from node :commonplace_mcp_<rand>@commonplace in order to prevent overlapping partitions

**Reproduced** during workspace MCP smoke testing 2026-04-25 (clod-squad msg #2911) after CX-3ine landed. CX-3ine reduced the visible CPU symptom (94% → 53%) but the disconnect persisted.

**Fix shipped** at 7dd725c: set kernel.prevent_overlapping_partitions = false BEFORE Node.start in three sites:
- apps/commonplace_mcp/lib/commonplace_mcp.ex (connect/1)
- apps/commonplace_cli/lib/commonplace/cli/serve.ex (start_named_node/1)
- apps/commonplace_cli/lib/commonplace/cli.ex (try_connect_to_serve/1)

Safe because no :global.register_name/2 calls exist anywhere in the codebase. The protection guards against actual partitioned clusters where the same global name might be claimed on both sides; not our use case.

**Closing condition:** workspace MCP smoke survives a full round (multiple tools, multiple sessions) without a 'Connection closed' disconnect.
close_reason: Verified across rounds 9-10: 'requested disconnect' warning gone, multiple MCP nodes joined cleanly without :global kicking them. Fix at 7dd725c+eadbeed: kernel.prevent_overlapping_partitions=false set before Node.start in MCP escript connect/1 + CLI serve start_named_node/1 + CLI try_connect_to_serve/1.

title: Sync.Agent resurrects reaped presence files from disk → CPU spin
description:
After Commonplace.Presence.Reaper removes a stale presence entry from the workspace root schema, the on-disk presence file (e.g. claude-code-6e2.bot) remains. On the next 1s SyncLoop tick, Watcher.detect_changes/4 flags it as :created and apply_create/3 re-adds it to the root schema with a fresh UUID. Each reap interval produces a fresh outbound commit storm that fans out via PubSub to DocCache invalidations, Orchestrator dispatch (full root-doc reconstruction per commit), and any wired ViewCompute/SmartDoc subscribers. Manifests as ~94% sustained CPU after the log line 'Presence reaper removed N stale entries'.

Diagnosed by commonplace-plan during workspace MCP smoke testing 2026-04-25 (clod-squad msg 2906).

**Fix:** filter honorific extensions (.bot/.exe/.usr/.who) out of disk_entries in Sync.Watcher.detect_changes/4. Honorific files are owned by the running actor process; Sync.Agent must not auto-create schema entries for them. Equivalent to the existing .commonplace-shadow skip in the same function.

**Why filter in Watcher (not Reaper):**
- Wider correctness: presence files are agent-owned across the board (Presence.Server.terminate, MCP shutdown, crash cleanup). Fixing only the reaper leaves the same resurrection bug for every other presence-removing path.
- Cleaner ownership invariant: 'the disk file is a materialization of the schema entry, EXCEPT for honorific extensions which are owned by the running actor process'.
- Smaller diff: one filter at one site (Watcher.detect_changes) vs. tracking down every Presence.remove caller.

**Followup to consider:**
- Honorific files marked :deleted should also be filtered (so a manual rm foo.bot doesn't tear down the schema entry behind a running actor's back). Out of scope for the immediate ship; file as a separate bead if desired.

**Test:** apps/commonplace/test/commonplace/sync/watcher_test.exs gained 'ignores honorific presence files on disk (CX-zb3p)' covering all four extensions + a regular file.
close_reason: Verified across rounds 8-10: serve CPU dropped from 94% sustained to ~53-67% (still has CX-0nkq-grade activity but no longer pegging from reaper-resurrection). No more 1Hz commit storm post-reap. Fix at 3eb9d0d: Watcher.detect_changes/4 filters honorific extensions (.bot/.exe/.usr/.who) out of disk_entries via Schema.honorific_extension?/1.

title: CommitStore overload + MCP tool crash propagation under fork
description:
**Reproduced** during workspace MCP smoke test (clod-squad msg 2849, 2026-04-25):

The MCP  tool tears down the stdio transport with -32000 'Connection closed'. Server log shows CommitStore GenServer.call({:commit_log, doc_uuid, [limit: 10000]}, 5000) → :timeout, plus parallel timeout in Sync.Agent.maybe_write_doc on {:latest_commit, ...}. Stack: DocBuilder.reconstruct_doc → Snapshotter → SnapshotTrigger.attempt_snapshot. Preceded by ~80 back-to-back Reflog checkpoint lines.

**Hypothesis:** CommitStore is single-mailbox; fork triggers lazy snapshot rebuild that fights for the same GenServer process. 5s call timeout is too short for big histories under contention. The exit propagates up through anubis's session GenServer and tears the transport down because nothing wraps the dispatch path.

**Three layers of fix** (per workspace's recommendation):

(a) **Raise CommitStore call timeout above 5s for big histories.** Easy. Masks the issue but prevents most user-visible failures. Could be configurable per-call (commit_log can be slow).

(b) **Move snapshot build off CommitStore mailbox.** Bigger surgery — split SnapshotTrigger / Snapshotter into a separate process that reads from CommitStore via a non-blocking projection. Solves the underlying overload.

(c) **MCP tolerates CommitStore timeouts.** Catch :exit in the tool dispatch path, return in-band MCP tool error. Already shipped in 88324f6→TBD as a hot-fix in apps/commonplace_mcp/lib/commonplace_mcp/anubis_server.ex's safe_tool_call/3 wrapper. Telemetry: [:commonplace, :mcp, :tool_call, :crashed].

**Status:** (c) shipped immediately so subsequent fork attempts return a tool error instead of killing the session. (a) and (b) remain open in this bead.

**Bonus question to investigate:** the ~80 back-to-back Reflog checkpoints during fork are suspicious. Why are they firing at that rate? Possibly a watcher subscribing to commit events and fanning out per-commit instead of debouncing. Look at Commonplace.Reflog.Snapshot trigger paths.

Workspace's bead CX-q9aj has the full failure context as observed from the client side.
notes:
**Investigation findings** (2026-04-25):

**Why so many snapshots / Reflog checkpoints:**

1. SyncLoop (apps/commonplace/lib/commonplace/sync/sync_loop.ex) fires Sync.Agent.sync_once every 1000ms (default).
2. Sync.Agent.sync_once (apps/commonplace/lib/commonplace/sync/agent.ex:84) UNCONDITIONALLY calls Commonplace.Reflog.Snapshot.checkpoint per cycle. This is documented as load-bearing for CX-86t2's race fix (async checkpoint races with concurrent root writers).
3. Reflog.Snapshot.checkpoint walks the FULL data tree and writes per-dir reflog entries — work scales with tree size, not commits-since-last-checkpoint.
4. Result: 1 checkpoint/sec PER Sync.Agent instance, regardless of whether anything actually changed. Under fork (which runs for many seconds and adds tree depth), the checkpoints accumulate and slow further as the tree grows.

**Why snapshot rebuild stalls CommitStore mailbox:**

1. DocBuilder.reconstruct_doc has a maybe_lazy_snapshot hook (apps/commonplace/lib/commonplace/tree/doc_builder.ex:46) that already wraps SnapshotTrigger.maybe_snapshot in Task.start.
2. The Task is async from DocBuilder's perspective BUT calls CommitStore.commit_log inside its build (Snapshotter.build_snapshot → reconstruct_source → DocBuilder.reconstruct_doc → CommitStore.commit_log).
3. Under load, MANY snapshot Tasks pile up — all waiting on the same CommitStore GenServer mailbox. The 5s GenServer.call timeout fires, :exit propagates.

**Architectural fix (b) proposal:**

Single-flight snapshot worker. A dedicated singleton GenServer (Commonplace.SnapshotWorker) that:
- Accepts maybe_snapshot(doc_uuid) requests via cast (non-blocking)
- Maintains an in-flight set keyed by doc_uuid
- Dedups: if a snapshot for X is already running, drop the new request (the eventual snapshot will reflect all commits up to its build moment)
- Performs the build inside its own process; CommitStore.commit_log calls go through normally but are serialized at the snapshot worker level so concurrent snapshot Tasks don't pile up at CommitStore

Replaces the Task.start in DocBuilder.maybe_lazy_snapshot. Same external semantics (eventual snapshot), bounded mailbox pressure.

**Reflog flood fix (orthogonal but cheap):**

Make Reflog.Snapshot.checkpoint idempotent when nothing changed:
- Track last-checkpoint commit_id per (root_uuid, owner)
- Before doing the recursive walk, check if root's :latest matches the stored value; if yes, no-op
- Preserves CX-86t2's race-fix property (still synchronous in the sync_once path) but eliminates the actual work when there's nothing new

**Status:**
- (c) crash-isolation already shipped at e677acb
- (a) raise CommitStore timeout: NOT proceeding per jes preference (papers over the issue)
- (b) single-flight snapshot worker: design above; implementation in progress
- Reflog idempotency: filed as separate scope below — depends on Reflog.Snapshot getting per-tree checkpoint cursor
close_reason: Resolved via three narrow sub-fixes: CX-71ej (idempotent reflog checkpoint per-dir cursor — eliminated ~13k unnecessary CommitStore calls per checkpoint, CPU 60-94% → 3.4%), CX-re6b (safe_invoke wrapper around all handle_request branches + Logger redirect to stderr + cat size cap), CX-kqz3 (async fork via Task + per-source in-flight dedup + 30s call timeout — broke the retry storm that was causing dist-Erlang heartbeat starvation). User-visible symptoms (fork timeout, MCP session deaths, :nodedown false-positives) all confirmed gone via workspace MCP smoke rounds 13-17.

title: Canonicalize merge (parent_id, merge_parents) by CID ordering
description:
Prereq for CX-69d7 E2E deterministic-merge convergence tests (option (d) pattern).

Current behavior: Merger.merge/4 (lib/commonplace/store/merger.ex:48) and downstream CrossEpochMerge / MergeSnapshotter emit merge commits with parent_id = L_arg and merge_parents = [R_arg] — i.e. the arg order is load-bearing. Two peers invoking merge on the same (L, R) pair in OPPOSITE order produce byte-different commits:

  peer A: merge(L, R) → parent=L, merge_parents=[R] → CID_A
  peer B: merge(R, L) → parent=R, merge_parents=[L] → CID_B ≠ CID_A

This breaks the deterministic-anyone property (CX-umz parallel) for merges: two peers with the same persisted siblings + same chosen strategy cannot produce byte-identical merge commits without coordinating arg order.

Proposed fix: at Merger.merge/4 entry, canonicalize (l, r) by CID ordering (e.g. parent = the lexicographically smaller CID, merge_parent = the larger). Forward canonicalized args to the chosen strategy. All downstream consumers already treat parent_id as "the chain we came from" — flipping which side is parent is semantically equivalent for the Yjs V1 update byte equality invariants that merge relies on.

Scope:
- Add canonicalization at Merger.merge/4 entry (or move the existing routing logic so canonicalization happens before strategy dispatch)
- Defensive: also canonicalize at the primitive module level (CrossEpochMerge, MergeSnapshotter) so direct callers get the invariant
- Test: merge(L, R) and merge(R, L) on same inputs produce byte-identical commits (same id, same update, same parent_id, same merge_parents)
- Test: existing merge semantics unchanged (no regression on merger_test.exs / merge_policy_test.exs / cross_epoch_merge tests)

Defer/out-of-scope:
- The "first-parent rule" for cross-epoch namespace selection is scoped to build 7 and tracked separately (per plan-bot msg 2026-04-18: merkle-tracked-yjs.md §L348). This bead is strictly about CID ordering for the CAS/deterministic-anyone property at build-<6 level.

Acceptance:
- Canonicalization tests green
- Full commonplace regression green
- CX-69d7 can write two-peer convergence tests that invoke merge with opposite arg order on each peer and observe byte-identical result
close_reason: Shipped 32fe6f7 — Merger.canonical_pair/2 utility, handler opts in. Scope narrowed from bead's original Merger-level canonicalization (would break SiblingMerger's parent=:latest CAS invariant); caller-opt-in is safer and still gives the handler the determinism CX-69d7 needs. Cross-peer determinism test in handler_test verifies byte-identical commit ids across swapped-{latest, other_ref} peers. 9/9 handler tests / 10 seeds, 437/0 broader regression. Persistence-on-other-peer is the autonomy gap tracked in CX-8k1v (jes-call).

title: NodeSync hook: invoke LateEditAutoTranslator on incoming commits
description:
Phase 2 cohort #3.A.2 (per commonplace-plan msg 2282). Pairs with CX-atk3's primitive — primitive-first-hook-second pattern (CX-4e2g + CX-tvyb/fab5/fkvc/2ok0/592q).

Scope:
- In NodeSync.catch_up (or equivalent import path), for each incoming commit call LateEditAutoTranslator.maybe_auto_translate/3
- On {:ok, :translated, c} or {:ok, :fallback, c} → import the translated commit (replaces the original import of the cross-epoch commit)
- On {:ok, :no_translation_needed} → import the original commit as-is (existing behavior)
- On {:ok, :skipped, reason} → import the original and emit [:commonplace, :late_edit, :auto_skip_stored] so divergence is visible rather than silent (baseline improvement — Doc.Server still sees a stored-but-untranslated commit, but telemetry names the case)
- Default fallback: true per design

Acceptance: two-peer test where peer A writes after peer B snapshotted → A's edits auto-translate into B's namespace on sync, resulting doc byte-identical on both peers.

Deps: CX-atk3 (primitive), CX-4e2g + CX-4qn1 upstream gate. Sits in cohort #3 dep graph ahead of CX-69d7 (integration test needs this wired).
close_reason: NodeSync.import_with_translation/3 wraps CommitStoreClient.import_commit with the CX-atk3 primitive. Aligned commits pass through unchanged; stale cross-epoch commits are replaced by translated versions; skipped case emits [:commonplace, :late_edit, :auto_skip_stored] telemetry for observability. catch_up routes through the new function. 6 tests GREEN, regression clean (1 pre-existing flaky agent-sync test unrelated). Commit c710eb3.

title: Sync-agent late-edit auto-translation on incoming cross-epoch edits
description:
Phase 2 cohort #3.A (per jes routing msg 2269, commonplace-plan msg 2270). Wires up Build 6's late-edit translation machinery inside the sync agent — the 'make cross-epoch peers actually sync' bead.

Mechanism ready (Builds 1-7 + CX-fbs6/gwz/l7j done); this is wiring/integration.

Scope:
- On incoming edit commit via sync protocol, detect if commit's snapshot_parent != current HEAD's snapshot_parent for the target doc
- If mismatch: invoke Translator.translate_edit/4 (primary byte-deterministic path) BEFORE attempting apply
- If pre-flight returns :untranslatable: opt-in positional-rebase fallback via translate_edit_with_snapshot/3
  - Design decision: fallback default ON or OFF for sync agent? Lean ON with telemetry so divergences are visible
- Emit [:commonplace, :late_edit, :auto_translated], [:auto_fallback], [:auto_skipped] telemetry

Acceptance: two-peer test where peer A writes after peer B snapshotted → A's edits auto-translate into B's namespace on sync (byte-identical convergence)

Rationale: without this, cross-epoch peers effectively can't sync — late edits from older snapshots fail to apply. Build 6 built the mechanism; this bead connects it to the sync path.

Blocked by: CX-4e2g, CX-4qn1 (must execute in order per jes routing).
close_reason: Primitive landed (e240344): maybe_auto_translate/3 does alignment check → translate_edit (primary, byte-deterministic) → translate_edit_with_snapshot + pre_doc fallback (opt-in, default ON per sync-agent policy) → :skipped with telemetry. 7/7 RED→GREEN, focused regression 62/0. title: Snapshot-trigger primitive: mandatory-threshold check
description:
Context quotes:

"I think I want it done heuristically, like after enough edits to be interesting, but ideally during a lull, but forcefully at some threshold. Maybe the automatic mandatory threshold is the higher priority, and heuristic is a nice to have." — jes, 2026-04-18

"Deterministic-anyone snapshotting (CX-umz) means multiple hooks can race safely; concurrent snapshots at the same parent dedup via CID. No coordination required."

Scope:

- Reads configured thresholds (per-doc-type config: state-vector entry count, chain-length-since-last-snapshot, etc.)
- If any threshold crossed → call CommitStore.snapshot/2
- If not crossed → no-op
- Idempotent and safe to call concurrently from multiple hook sites
- Zero-coordination: relies on deterministic-anyone CID dedup

Acceptance: unit tests proving (a) no-op when below threshold, (b) writes snapshot when above, (c) concurrent calls from two processes produce one dedup'd snapshot commit
close_reason: Landed in 72d23c3: Commonplace.SnapshotTrigger.maybe_snapshot/3 primitive + CommitStore.write_snapshot_cas/5 CAS write primitive + Snapshotter.build_snapshot/3 extraction. 14 dedicated tests + 283/0 regression across snapshot_trigger + entire store subsuite. Concurrency: deterministic-anyone (CX-umz) collapses same-parent calls; CAS on :latest rejects stale-parent calls as :parent_moved → :below_threshold. Chain walk stops at :snapshot and :genesis boundaries.

title: Automatic mandatory snapshot threshold
description:
Hard snapshot trigger that always fires when a doc crosses a configured limit. From jes 2026-04-18: 'I think I want it done heuristically, like after enough edits to be interesting, but ideally during a lull, but forcefully at some threshold. Maybe the automatic mandatory threshold is the higher priority, and heuristic is a nice to have.'

Scope:
- Hard trigger that always fires when a doc crosses a configured limit
- Candidate metrics: state-vector entry count OR chain length since last snapshot (or both, OR'd)
- Configurable per-doc-type (presence aggressive, regular relaxed/off) — matches docs/snapshot-compaction.md 'likely per-doc-type, not global'
- Deterministic, predictable, always fires — no heuristic delay
- Hook point: sync agent (Phase 2 territory) — when it materializes or persists a doc, check thresholds and trigger CommitStore.snapshot/2 if crossed
- Must use existing CommitStore.snapshot/2 mechanism (shipped in CX-umz); do not reinvent

title: Validate imported commits before trusting snapshot metadata
description: CX-u7p round 6 codex flagged that DocBuilder.reconstruct_doc/2 treats any commit with metadata.kind == :snapshot as an authoritative history cut point, but remote commits are accepted verbatim by CommitStore.import_commit/2 and NodeSync.catch_up without recomputing the content address or verifying signatures. A buggy or hostile peer could retag an ordinary delta as %{kind: :snapshot} and make reconstruction skip all earlier history (or drive the reset branch in Document.Server) — the round-2 metadata-in-content-address fix protects locally-created commits but does not validate imported ones. Need to reject imported commits whose computed id does not match, or whose signature does not verify, before replay semantics honor the metadata.
close_reason: Id-verification gate added to import_commit/3 BEFORE the namespace validator runs. Commit.verify_id/1 recomputes the content address (sha256 of parent_id || update || canonical_metadata || canonical_merge_parents) and compares to the claimed id; mismatch → [:commonplace, :commit, :rejected, :id_mismatch] telemetry + {:error, {:id_mismatch, computed, claimed}}. Closes the hostile-retag gap where a peer could flip metadata.kind to :snapshot and drive DocBuilder to skip history, or forge parent_id/update/merge_parents. 15 new TDD tests (verify_id primitive + import integration + telemetry + ordering). Drive-by fix: 5 sites in server_sync_test.exs that hand-forged sha256(update) alone now use Commit.new/5 — exactly the forge pattern the gate catches. Commit 6aba270. Full suite 1417 green.

title: Sibling-commit merge for concurrent CommitStore writes (multi-writer correctness)
description:
## Problem

CommitStore.create_chained_commit/3 plus the :latest pointer model cannot
preserve concurrent writes across multiple BEAM nodes. Every writer today
follows this pattern:

    {:ok, commit} = CommitStoreClient.latest_commit(store, uuid)
    doc = apply_update(Doc.new(...), commit.update)
    doc = mutate(doc)
    CommitStoreClient.create_chained_commit(store, uuid, encode_update(doc))

and readers use latest_commit (optionally DocBuilder.reconstruct_snapshot/2)
which walks from the :latest pointer only.

Two nodes racing on the same UUID can both observe the same parent commit,
both produce a full-snapshot update, and both successfully call
create_chained_commit -- yielding two SIBLING commits chained to the same
parent. Whichever :latest pointer write lands second becomes the entire
visible state, so the first node's concurrent write is silently lost at the
commit-chain layer even though the in-memory CRDT merge would have
preserved both.

## Relationship to CX-6g6

CX-6g6 round 1 (commit 318af70) fixed the in-memory prerequisite: identity
writes now derive client_id from {node(), uuid}, so two concurrent
updates from different nodes carry distinct (client_id, clock) pairs and
would MERGE correctly if they ever reached the same Yelixer.Doc via
apply_update/2. Codex round 2 correctly observed that this is only a
PREREQUISITE -- the CommitStore write/read path still collapses siblings at
the :latest pointer level.

CX-6g6 is therefore a prerequisite for this bead: without distinct client
ids, even a fixed commit-chain layer would still drop one side on CRDT
merge. With distinct client ids in place, this bead can solve the sibling
problem and preserve both writes end-to-end.

## Affected surface

Every doc type that uses create_chained_commit + reads via :latest /
reconstruct_snapshot:

- Identity docs (Commonplace.Presence.Identity: touch_last_seen,
  add_public_key, register's last_seen update)
- Schema docs (Commonplace.Tree.Schema mutations: add_file, add_directory,
  remove_entry -- every directory writer)
- Presence docs that happen to be multi-written (conceptually single-writer
  today, but no structural guarantee)
- Any future shared doc that lands on the same pattern

## Fix direction sketches

Not prescriptive -- design work is part of this bead:

(a) Chase-the-chain with linearization. Before writing, detect that
    :latest has moved under us; pull the sibling's update, merge in
    memory, re-encode as an additional chained commit on top of the new
    :latest. Requires CAS on the :latest pointer.

(b) Merge siblings at :latest-write time. Commits become multi-parent
    when a race is detected; the :latest pointer advances to a
    deterministic merge commit that carries both parents. Requires
    commit-envelope changes to support >1 parent.

(c) Explicit multi-parent commits with deterministic merge. Model
    every commit as potentially multi-parent, with a deterministic merge
    rule (hash-ordered parents, content-addressed merge commit). Aligns
    with the Merkle-CRDT framing in the design docs.

## Blocker status

Marked as blocker for: true multi-writer identity docs in production.
Today identity docs work in practice because writes are rare and usually
serialized through one node at a time; this bead is about making them
correct under genuine concurrency.

title: Stabilize client_id for Presence writers (root cause of state-vector bloat)
description: Commonplace.Presence.heartbeat/2 and update_status/3 call Yelixer.Doc.new() without passing client_id:, so each heartbeat mints a fresh random client_id and persists it into the state vector on re-encode. Root cause of the 14,360 client_ids observed on claude-code-2ca.bot (see CX-3ty). Fix: pass a stable client_id derived from the presence UUID (e.g. :erlang.phash2(uuid, 0xFFFF_FFFF)) so repeated writes from the same or different BEAM processes reuse the same client_id. This stops the bloat at the source; compaction (CX-3ty follow-up) only addresses existing bloat. Also audit other callers of Yelixer.Doc.new/1 that rebuild-then-re-encode — Schema mutations are another likely offender. See docs/superpowers/specs/2026-04-16-presence-compaction-design.md for context.

title: CommitStore publishes on commits: but UI subscribes on blue: — topic mismatch
description: Found 2026-04-09 during live wiki demo. WikiLive and TreeLive subscribe to blue:UUID via CPPubSub.subscribe_blue and handle {:commit, uuid, commit_id, meta} messages, but CommitStore.handle_call({:create_commit, ...}) broadcasts on commits:UUID via raw Phoenix.PubSub. The UI never receives live updates from CommandRouter-initiated writes (MCP, CLI). Must refresh the browser to see changes. Quick fix: add a second broadcast on blue:UUID from CommitStore. Deeper refactor: unify the dataflow PubSub conventions — CPPubSub.broadcast wraps messages as {topic, msg}, raw Phoenix.PubSub does not, and the existing wiki_live handler expects the bare form. Long-term, all channel producers should go through CPPubSub and all consumers should agree on whether messages are wrapped.
close_reason: Fixed in two commits: ccb7358 added CommitStore broadcast on blue:UUID (UI subscribers now receive commit events from CommandRouter-initiated writes), then 148ceaa fixed a latent BadBooleanError in WikiLive.handle_info (used strict `and` on a UUID string instead of `&&`). Live demo verified end-to-end: MCP write → CommitStore → PubSub → WikiLive re-render → browser updates with no refresh and no crash. Follow-up refactor to unify blue/commits topic duality left as open work.

title: Zigzag (signed varint) encoding bug: encode_sint(-1) produces wrong value
description: Property tests discovered that encode_sint(-1) produces <<3>> which decode_sint decodes as -2 instead of -1. The standard zigzag formula (n << 1) XOR (n >> 63) should yield 1 for -1, but the current implementation bsl(-n, 1) |> bor(1) yields 3. This affects any negative integer content values in CRDT updates. Discovered by CX-e2x property tests.
notes: Part of epic CX-hco (Yelixer CRDT Hardening). Discovered by CX-e2x property tests.
close_reason: Fixed: encode_sint now uses standard zigzag formula (n << 1) ^ -1. Property tests updated to cover negative integers. Commit 90d965d.

title: Fix YMap.to_map non-deterministic iteration order
description: YMap.to_map/2 iterates store.clients (Erlang map — non-deterministic order), so the 'last one wins' reduce gives different results depending on iteration order. When full-state snapshots are replayed via chain replay, this produces inconsistent CRDT state. Root cause of the reconstruct_snapshot workaround in merge.ex. Fix: use YATA sequence order (rightmost-in-sequence wins) instead of arbitrary Enum.reduce order, matching yrs map conflict resolution semantics.
notes: Part of epic CX-hco (Yelixer CRDT Hardening)
close_reason: Fixed: to_map/to_json/find_current_item now use YATA sequence order via BlockStore.get_sequence. 4 new determinism tests. Commit 266205d.

title: CubDB corrupts on unclean shutdown

B) Distributed Erlang: CLI commands connect to running serve node and call CommitStore remotely. Fallback to direct CubDB only when serve isn't running, protected by file lock to prevent concurrent access.

title: Gate B execute-baseline must be Gate-B-clean (snapshot/merge/translation absorption laundering)
description: Found grounding move-#1's translation-execute flag — a PRE-EXISTING class, a hole in the original R2 review. Gate B's contributor walk (trust.ex walk_contributors) halts :ok at the first snapshot whose SIGNER holds :execute — but post-2.5 that signer is the NODE (verb-agnostic auto-trust), and SnapshotWorker mints a snapshot from doc state regardless of whether the chain was Gate-B-clean. So a node-signed snapshot launders un-:execute-authorized contributions into an execute-TERMINAL baseline (same for node-signed merges — which also makes the stale Gate B moduledoc 'merges unsigned → strict denies converged code docs' FALSE; CX-tdkq.26 fixes that moduledoc; a .26 node-signed translation is a faster instance). Latent until phase-3 (its only input is a :write-without-:execute contributor on a code doc, which the verb-agnostic flat allowlist can't express; phase-3 certs are the first to express it). FIX: a snapshot/merge advances the EXECUTE baseline only if the chain was Gate-B-clean when minted (SnapshotWorker runs the walk + stamps it; un-clean snapshots store fine but don't halt the execute walk). NOT move-#1-blocking (the v1 delegation policy — no :write-without-:execute certs on code docs — closes the input). REJECTED route: an original-author field on the commit is unsound (attacker-writable → a :write holder stamps an :execute-holder's uuid and launders their own code). Ref docs/trust-and-attenuation.md §2 + docs/federation.md §4. [Converged: relayed independently by commonplace-trust ('vs write-only contributors') + commonplace-plan ('must be Gate-B-clean') — same bead, deduped into one.]

When a referenced cert isn't in the store yet → {:error, :awaiting_capability} → reuse R11 pending_imports/maybe_queue_pending (distinct from a hard untrusted-reject; fixpoint-retries when the cert lands). title: Trust phase 3d: authorized? phase-3 body + commit-author binding
description: Swap authorized?'s body (gates UNCHANGED). (1) Degenerate fast-path: commit signer ∈ pinned trusted_identities → :ok (implicit unattenuated 1-link root; preserves R1/R2 + hot path). title: Trust phase 3c: verify_chain — leaf→root cert-DAG verifier
description: verify_chain(leaf_cid, anchor_keys, store) :: {:ok, %{verbs,scope,caveats}} | {:error, reason}. Pure reduce_while leaf→root, mirroring authorized_to_execute?. Per link: verify_id + verify_sig against issuer.pubkey; full-pubkey key-link (child.issuer.pubkey == parent.audience.pubkey, EXACT 32 bytes); not expired (utc_now); DELEGATION GATE (every non-leaf cert must grant :delegate; leaf needn't); monotonic narrowing (child.verbs ⊆ parent.verbs, scope ⊆ via MapSet.subset?, caveats tighten). Terminate at a root cert whose issuer.pubkey == the pinned FULL pubkey for that identity in trusted_identities. Returns the intersected EFFECTIVE capability.

title: Trust phase 3a: Capability cert value type (Commonplace.Trust.Capability)
description: Commonplace.Trust.Capability struct {issuer:{identity_uuid,pubkey}, audience:{identity_uuid,pubkey}, claim:{verbs, scope, caveats:{not_before,not_after}}, proof: parent_cid|nil, sig}. Mirrors Store.Commit. CID = sha256 over the canonical assertion EXCLUDING sig (sig-over-CID, same as commits). Canonical encoding serializes scope + verbs as SORTED LISTS (not MapSet — internal order isn't a stable wire/CID contract) so two nodes minting the same cert converge on the same CID; caveats map under term_to_binary(:deterministic). KEY-BOUND: issuer/audience pin FULL 32-byte pubkeys (the signer_id fingerprint is 32-bit = ~2^32 second-preimage forgery target, never the binding). new/sign/verify_id/verify_sig, reusing Crypto.Signing.

title: Trust: cross-epoch translator mints unsigned :regular commits — strict-mode gap
description: Surfaced during Phase 2.5. The cross-epoch TRANSLATOR (store/translator.ex) re-expresses a user edit across epochs as a :regular commit; the original signature can't survive (bytes change) and NO user is in the loop, so the translated commit is unsigned-:regular. Phase 2.5 deliberately scoped it out (it node-signs only :snapshot/:merge kinds). Unlike fork (which has a user actor who can thread a signing context), translation has no signer available — so "needs user key" isn't satisfiable. If a translated :regular commit ever crosses a strict Gate A independently (synced to a strict peer), it would be REJECTED with no clean fix today. FIRST STEP: confirm the translated commits' sync path — are they absorbed into the node-signed :merge commit (then no gap), or do they sync as standalone :regular commits (then a real strict-mode gap)? If the latter: candidate fixes = node-sign translated commits (the translator IS a system actor), or mark them a system kind. Sharper edge than fork; worth nailing before strict federation.
design: Federation move-#1 Phase-A prereq. Federation crosses epochs (auto-snapshot advances them), so cross-epoch translation (node_sync import_with_translation → translator mints :regular, no signer) WILL hit a strict peer's Gate A → :unsigned reject. FIX (DECIDED): the RECEIVING node signs its own translations with its NodeIdentity (auto-trusted locally, the 2.5 pattern — translation is the receiver's own system action); impl in Translator.translate_edit_with_snapshot. .26 ALSO fixes the now-stale Gate B moduledoc ('merge commits minted unsigned → conservative deny' — false post-2.5). RESOLUTION (commonplace-trust grounded): .26 does NOT create the execute-laundering class — that's the separate snapshot/merge/translation-absorption bead CX-tdkq.27; the move-#1 v1 delegation policy (no :write-without-:execute certs on code docs) is the interim guard for the laundering input. DROPPED as unsound: the earlier 'Gate B checks the ORIGINAL pre-translation signer' candidate — original-author metadata is attacker-writable (laundering vector).
close_reason: Phase-A DONE (commit fc97465, branch federate-for-real). Translated commits node-signed at mint via shared node_sign/1 in Translator.translate_edit_with_snapshot, covering BOTH the primary DM path and the positional fallback (receiving node is the system actor — 2.5 pattern). 4 new tests incl. strict Gate A acceptance + id-determinism (signature outside the content address). Also fixed the stale Gate B moduledoc ('merges unsigned → conservative deny' — false post-2.5); the laundering class is tracked in CX-tdkq.27. RESIDUAL: a translated commit re-syncing to a THIRD strict node carries node-B's signature — that node must trust node B (the documented multi-node cross-pinning gap from NodeIdentity), not new exposure. Core suite 1519/0. NOT yet merged to main.

title: SandboxExecRunner test teardown must kill spawned OS children
description: SandboxExecRunner tests leak orphaned OS child processes: a `sleep 3600` stderr-relay bash (the wrapper SandboxExecRunner spawns) survives the test suite, reparents to ppid 1, and holds the test runner's output pipe open → CI/automation hangs waiting on EOF. Also leaves /tmp/cp_sandbox_* dirs. Cost ~30 min of diagnosis during R1. Fix: SandboxExecRunner test teardown must kill spawned children (and clean /tmp/cp_sandbox_*). Not part of the trust work — surfaced alongside it.

title: Trust phase 3: subtree-scope resolution via write-gated schema walk (Wrinkle H)
description:
Phase-3 sub-problem of attenuable capabilities (docs/trust-and-attenuation.md §4, Wrinkle H). Subtree-scoped capabilities (scope = subtree rooted at a stable UUID) require deciding "is doc D contained in subtree R?". Containment lives in schema docs (dir->entry->child-UUID), which are ordinary peer-writable synced CRDTs (Schema.add_file/add_directory chain commits like any doc; Orchestrator.collect_processes_recursive walks the tree THROUGH schema). So a peer trusted to write subtree R could RE-PARENT a target doc D into R to pull D under a scope they hold — a live attack on any path- or subtree-resolved scope.
Resolution: resolve subtree containment against schema state RESTRICTED to commits that themselves pass Trust.authorized?(:write) for that scope. Scope-resolution and the write-gate become mutually recursive but WELL-FOUNDED — the recursion bottoms out at the ROOT schema, which is locally anchored (root_uuid in local config, not synced). Same shape as the existing Namespace.walk (namespace.ex), which already resolves clientID membership against a genesis/snapshot trust root; Wrinkle H applies that trust-rooted-walk pattern to schema STRUCTURE instead of clientIDs — precedent, not net-new mechanism. Does NOT bite R1/R2 (doc-scoped, {:doc, uuid}, no tree walk). Couples scope-resolution to Gate A, hence its own bead.
design: Reuse Namespace.walk's trust-rooted-membership pattern with base case = local root_uuid; only schema commits passing authorized?(:write) for the parent scope contribute to containment. Scope already anchored on stable UUID. Open: resolve containment eagerly (cache a trusted-containment view) vs lazily per check.

title: Trust phase 3: attenuable capability cert docs + chain-walk verifier (UCAN-shaped)
description:
Phase 3 of trust+attenuation (docs/trust-and-attenuation.md §4). Generalize the flat allowlist into UCAN-shaped attenuable capabilities, WITHOUT touching the gates (only the Trust.authorized? body changes):
(i) A self-certifying capability CERT DOC type: {issuer, audience, claim:{verbs, scope, caveats}, proof: CID-of-parent-cert, sig: Ed25519(issuer)} — forming a delegation DAG rooting at a LOCALLY-anchored root key.
(ii) Swap Trust.authorized?'s body from allowlist-lookup to chain-walk: resolve signer -> walk the proof chain to a local anchor, enforcing monotone narrowing (child verbs ⊆ parent, scope ⊆ parent, expiry only tightens) and that the leaf grants {verb, scope}.
(iii) Federation envelope references the authorizing chain by CID (optionally inlines the cert docs); reuse pending_imports (R11/CX-tdkq.11) to defer commits awaiting their certs (:awaiting_capability, fixpoint-retry) as the ordering fallback.
(iv) Peer-workspace trust expressed as a root-issued cert (jes-root delegates {verbs:[:write], scope:/federated/peer-x subtree, not_after:T} to peer-X-root-identity) rather than config — auditable, attenuable, revocable.
Verbs {:write, :execute, :delegate}; scope anchored on STABLE UUIDs (not mutable tree paths — path-scoped caps are gameable). Builds on identity-and-signatures.md (Ed25519, shipped) + authorization.md (the biscuit/UCAN family this instantiates).
design: Design the cert format so a future unification with the white/MQTT macaroon layer is a re-encoding, not a re-think (doc open-question E). Keep caveats simple (expiry) but extensible toward Datalog if the black-channel condition engine (CX-1ji) ever needs expressive conditions — matches authorization.md's deliberately-deferred-Datalog stance. This bead is large and will likely split into sub-beads (cert-doc type, chain verifier, envelope refs, peer-trust cert) once it's the active front.
close_reason: PHASE 3 COMPLETE — UCAN-shaped attenuable capability cert-DAG. All six sub-beads done + reviewed-green: 22a cert value type (Commonplace.Trust.Capability, CID-excludes-sig, full-pubkey binding), 22b CubDB content-addressed store, 22c verify_chain (leaf→root walk: key-link + :delegate gate + monotone narrowing + expiry + local-anchor root + effective-intersection + cycle guard), 22d authorized? cert-path + ⭐commit-author binding (preserves R1/R2 fast-path), 22e proof-in-metadata + R11 pending-queue [+ a security fix re-running FULL trust+namespace on retry, hardening CX-tdkq.11], 22f issuance API + e2e + CLI. Gates UNCHANGED — only authorized?'s body swapped (the load-bearing seam from R1). Core 1460 + CLI 68 + cap-parse 6 GREEN, warnings-clean. On trust-attenuation (tip 18affe3), NOT yet merged to commonplace main — merge pending jes's sequencing call. Per boss-clod relay 2026-06-11. (CX-tdkq.23 Wrinkle-H subtree-scope + .21/.25/.26 trust follow-ups remain separate/open.)

title: Trust phase 1.5: revocation RESIDUALS (purge loaded modules + bound the gap)
description:
Phase 1.5 of trust+attenuation (docs/trust-and-attenuation.md §5). Revoking trust (removing a signer from the allowlist, or later superseding a capability cert) is paper-only unless the already-realized consequences are evicted:
(1) SourceDoc compiles are cached in ETS keyed by CONTENT-HASH — an already-compiled module from a now-untrusted signer stays runnable. Fix: fold the trust verdict (a trust-config generation/epoch) into the cache key, OR flush the SourceDoc cache on trust-config change.
(2) Orchestrator processes already spawned from a now-untrusted source keep running. Fix: a reconcile step that stops processes whose source is no longer Trust.authorized?(:execute).
This is where revocation gets teeth; without it, removing trust changes nothing already in motion.
design:
Cache-key-includes-verdict beats flush-on-change (no global flush), but the verdict can change without content change, so the key must incorporate the trust-config generation/epoch, not just content-hash. The reconcile-stop should hook the same place the Orchestrator already reconciles process specs.

── Re-scoped post-R2 (2026-06-10) ──
The BULK of original phase-1.5 is subsumed by construction: R2's Gate B runs on EVERY SourceDoc.compile incl. cache hits (so a revoked signer's cached module is denied at next compile — no cache-key change needed, superseding the cache-key approach above), and the __processes.json declaration gate shrinks the declared config so the Orchestrator reconcile loop stops a running process whose declaration lost trust (tested: "revoking trust stops an already-running process on the next reconcile"). RESIDUAL scope only: (i) :code.purge already-LOADED module objects on revocation (belt-and-braces — nothing invokes them via the substrate post-denial, but they linger in the BEAM); (ii) bound the revocation→stop LATENCY (reconcile interval, default 5s — decide acceptable or tighten); (iii) close the Orchestrator handle_blue dispatch firing in the reconcile gap. Hence P2, not P1.

title: Unify commits:/blue: topic duality + wire remote snapshot/2 (R10 gated seams)
description: Two R10 (CX-tdkq.10) seams that change a wire/storage contract — GATED per the split criterion. (1) Unify the commits:/blue: PubSub topic duality (CX-4im, closed: its fix added a blue: broadcast alongside commits: but explicitly left unifying the two topics as open work — that's a broadcast-contract change affecting every subscriber). (2) Wire remote snapshot/2 through CommitStoreClient (currently local-only per commit_store_client.ex; making it remote-routable is a transport-contract change). Both touch contracts used across nodes/subscribers — design the unified topic + the remote snapshot protocol before changing.

title: Cold-storage GC of superseded snapshots (R8a) — append-only deletion decision
description: The headline retention fix R8 (CX-tdkq.8) defers — GATED, structural. Reclaim store space by DELETING snapshot commits superseded by a higher-watermark snapshot. This directly contradicts the system's core invariant: 'CommitStore is append-only — data is never deleted' (CLAUDE.md, Store.GC moduledoc). The design DELIBERATELY deferred cold-storage GC. Deleting commits is dangerous + cross-cutting: (1) late-edit/cross-epoch translation reads derivation maps that REFERENCE old commits (Translator/Snapshotter/MergeAdopter) — deleting a superseded snapshot could orphan a derivation chain a peer's late edit still needs; (2) catch-up sync diffs CID sets across nodes — a deleted commit on one node looks like divergence; (3) the Merkle-DAG content-addressing assumes commits are immutable+present. Needs a design decision (cold-storage tier vs hard delete? watermark safety margin? interaction with cross-epoch translation + multi-node CID diff?) before ANY deletion. R8 parts (b) orphan archive/export [GC.archive_orphans, additive, done] and (c) compile-cache cap [done] landed; this is the remaining structural piece. Same gating pattern as R4c/R7.

title: Bursar-backed cluster singleton ownership + wiring (R7 impl)
description: The actual implementation R7 (CX-tdkq.7) defers to — gated on a jes design decision (raised by boss-clod 2026-06-10). R7's ENTIRE value is cluster-wide at-most-one; single-node at-most-one is already guaranteed by the supervision tree (one child = one instance). Two blockers: (1) DESIGN — the Bursar is a per-node local GenServer behind PubSub fan-out; making it a correct cluster-wide lock authority needs a decision: (a) run on one designated node (SPOF + minority degrades), (b) :global Bursar (one name to handle, CRDT-backed state aids recovery, still a :global), or (c) consensus-backed grants. Wiring the :global singletons (TickBot/MoveServer/Bot) to a per-node Bursar would trade :global's DETECTED name-conflict for SILENT cross-partition double-granting = regression. (2) WIRING PREREQ — neither the Bursar nor Scheduler.Agent is started in production today (built-but-unwired, only in tests); 'dogfood the green channel for real' requires wiring them into the app first. Scope once unblocked: resolve cluster-authority model, wire Bursar (supervised) + scheduler into the app, then replace TickBot/MoveServer/Bot :global ownership with Bursar leases (acquire+TTL+renew, lose-lease→stand-down). MoveServer's own moduledoc calls itself a 'v0 stand-in for the green channel' — it's the natural first real consumer.
close_reason: Redundant with CX-tdkq.7 — R7 has no do-now portion, so CX-tdkq.7 itself is the gated bead (no parent-with-done-part to split from, unlike R4→R4c). Consolidated: see CX-tdkq.7.

title: ViewCompute self-write origin-ignore (commit-origin metadata)
description: Refinement split from CX-tdkq.6 (R6). The review's R6 names two loop-breakers: (1) 'a ViewCompute ignores commits whose update originated from its own writes' and (2) a rate fuse. R6 landed the rate fuse (commit 926abbf) — the GENERAL loop-safety net that catches every cycle (single-view source==target and multi-view alike), so loop-safety is covered. (1) is an efficiency refinement (avoid one wasted recompute per self-write in the source==target case) that needs commit-ORIGIN metadata: CommandRouter.write currently hardcodes %{} commit metadata (command_router.ex:415) and doesn't return the commit id, so a ViewCompute can't tell its own write's echo from a genuine external edit. Scope: thread an :origin tag from write opts → create_chained_commit metadata → the {:commit, uuid, id, meta} PubSub broadcast; ViewCompute tags its writes and skips incoming commits whose meta origin == self. Cross-cutting (touches the write/commit/broadcast path used by MCP/CLI/everything) — deferred as its own bead rather than bolted onto R6. Not safety-critical: the rate fuse already prevents runaway.

title: CX-α: structural replay of nested map/array sub-types in yelixer snapshots
description: The 'real fix' R5 (CX-tdkq.5) defers to. Yelixer.Doc.snapshot_update/1 does NOT structurally replay CRDT sub-types nested inside maps/arrays — replay_named_type/3 short-circuits on the '__sub:' prefix, so a nested YMap/YArray loses its internal CRDT state on snapshot/compaction (apps/yelixer/lib/yelixer/doc.ex). The whole data model currently works around this via JSON-encoded blobs (accepting LWW), now an enforced rule + guard (see docs/plans/2026-06-10-nested-crdt-data-model-rule.md and Snapshotter.build_payload/2). This bead is the substrate fix: replay nested map/array sub-types structurally the same way XML sub-types already are (replay_xml_* helpers), restoring field-level concurrent merge for nested structures. ⚠️ Non-trivial CRDT-core change — a 'next structural investment', NOT do-now. When it lands, the R5 guard becomes a no-op and can be relaxed. This is the symbolic 'CX-α' referenced throughout the architecture review §5.3/§8 R5 and in yelixer's chat_shape_smoke_test.

title: R11. Handle out-of-order imports
description: From architecture-review.md §8 R11 (P2). A small pending-commit queue that retries namespace validation after subsequent imports land (or sorts catch-up batches topologically before import) removes the order-sensitivity noted in §6.1.
close_reason: R11 done (5944fe5): out-of-order imports no longer drop legitimate commits. import_commit holds a namespace-rejected commit in a small pending queue (capped 1024) and retries the queue to a fixpoint after every successful import, so a dependency arriving later (or a whole C→B→A chain) gets accepted with no ordering required of peers. Transparent to node_sync (initial reply/telemetry unchanged + new :deferred event). 3 tests incl. fixpoint cascade, 1423 suite green.
