title: Outliner MVP iv: _view.xml action declarations + ViewActionDispatch wiring (MCP surface)
description:
Action-declaration / MCP-dispatch surface for the outliner (epic CX-dqjs). Ref: docs/outliner.md §5. Mirrors chat: XML declares actions; LiveView (iii) renders. Both converge on the same structured mutations (MVP i).

_view.xml declares <action> elements with <arg> resolution (ArgResolver): edit_text, new_item, indent_item, outdent_item, reorder_item, toggle_collapse, delete_item. Wire ViewActionDispatch do_dispatch clauses routing each to the Commonplace.Outline.* mutation layer (MVP i), so an AGENT can restructure an outline over MCP, not just a human via the LiveView.
design: This is the action-discovery + MCP surface, NOT the human-render surface (that's iii). Same two-layer split as chat-room: declared <action>s feed MCP dynamic tools + ArgResolver; the LiveView feeds humans. Reuse the existing ViewActionDispatch/ArgResolver machinery — add clauses, don't fork it.
acceptance_criteria: An MCP/dynamic-tool caller can invoke indent_item/outdent_item/reorder_item/toggle_collapse/edit_text/new_item/delete_item against an outline and the _outline doc updates identically to the LiveView path. Action declarations parse; ArgResolver fills args. Tests cover dispatch -> mutation for each action.

title: Outliner MVP iii: OutlineLive LiveView — render tree + keybinds
description:
Human-facing LiveView for the outliner (epic CX-dqjs). Ref: docs/outliner.md §5. Follows the chat v1 precedent (feature-specific LiveView since ViewCompute is string->string with no generic structured-source primitive yet).

OutlineLive:
- Mounts /outline/:name; walks the workspace schema to resolve the _outline doc uuid.
- Reads the flat <item> bag, reconstructs the tree (MVP ii), renders nested <ul>/<li> with collapse toggles and per-item contenteditable bullets.
- Subscribes to commits:{outline_uuid} for live re-render.
- Dispatches keybinds to the structured mutations (MVP i):
  Enter=new sibling, Tab=indent (set parent=preceding sibling), Shift-Tab=outdent (set parent=parent's parent), Alt-Up/Alt-Down=reorder (set order between neighbors), Ctrl-.=toggle collapse, Backspace-on-empty/Del=delete.
design: Indent/outdent are PURELY attribute edits — the element never moves in the fragment, only its parent/order change. New-sibling/new-child mint a fresh id and an order key between neighbors (MVP i between()). Collapse is a shared attribute in MVP (per-viewer collapse is follow-up). Keep render = reconstruct(MVP ii) -> nested HTML; re-render on every commit.
acceptance_criteria: Visit /outline/:name; see nested bullets; Tab/Shift-Tab reparent; Enter adds a sibling; Alt-Up/Down reorder; Ctrl-. collapses/expands; editing a bullet persists and live-updates a second open session. Wallaby/feature test for the core keybind flow.

title: Outliner MVP ii: tree reconstruction + defensive cycle/orphan handling
description:
Pure reconstruction function for the outliner (epic CX-dqjs). Ref: docs/outliner.md §4-5.

Given the flat <item> bag from _outline (from MVP i), reconstruct the nested tree for rendering:
- Group items by 'parent'; within each parent, sort by (order, id) — node id is the STABLE TIEBREAKER so concurrent inserts at the same fractional position can't interleave ambiguously.
- Roots are items with parent=''.
- DEFENSIVE CYCLE/ORPHAN HANDLING: any item not reachable from a root (a parent-cycle, e.g. concurrent X->Y & Y->X; or a parent pointing at a deleted/missing id) is RE-ROOTED to top-level for display. No data loss — items + text intact; only the displayed attachment point is defaulted. Implement as a reachability walk during reconstruction.
design: This is the MVP stand-in for full Kleppmann cycle-safe move (follow-up CX-<kleppmann>). LWW-parent handles concurrent reparent-to-different-parents cleanly (no dup); the ONLY pathology it can't resolve is a concurrent 2-cycle, which orphan-to-root renders safely without losing data. Pure function, no side effects — easy to unit-test exhaustively.
acceptance_criteria: Pure fn: flat items -> nested tree. Tests: normal nesting; (order,id) tiebreak on equal order; 2-node parent cycle -> both orphaned-to-root, no crash, no data loss; parent pointing at missing id -> orphaned. No mutations performed (read-only).
notes: Round-2 cold-read decision (docs/outliner.md §4): orphan-to-root is COSMETIC / render-only — reconstruction NEVER writes parent='' back to the doc; stored parent stays as-is, only the rendered tree defaults the attachment point. Pure function on every render; replicas converge on commit-receipt; no write-storm. Output shape: build %{id => item} index, group by parent, sort each group by (order,id), attach children -> nested node structure.

title: Outliner MVP i: _outline xml doc shape + structured-XML mutation layer
description:
Foundation bead for the outliner (epic CX-dqjs). Define the _outline document shape and the mutation layer everything else builds on. Ref: docs/outliner.md §2-3 on commonplace-plan/main.

DOC SHAPE: _outline is an xml-typed doc (YXmlFragment). Content is a FLAT list of <item> elements, each a direct child of the fragment root:
  <item id parent order collapsed>TEXT-as-xml_text-child</item>
- id: short stable node identity, minted once, never reused.
- parent: id of parent item; '' (empty) = top-level. Reparent edits THIS attribute.
- order: fractional-index sibling-order key.
- collapsed: 'true'|'false' (shared in MVP).
- text: an xml_text CHILD (char-CRDT), NOT an attribute.

MUTATION LAYER (a Commonplace.Outline.* module): insert_item, set_parent, set_order, set_collapsed, edit_text(insert/delete), delete_item — all via the structured Commonplace.Yelixer.Types.XMLElement / XMLText API (insert_child/delete_child/set_attribute + text ops), committed as CRDT updates on _outline.

Plus a fractional-index helper: generate a key BETWEEN two neighbor keys (base-62 string or equiv), and the (order,id) comparator used by reconstruction (ii).
design:
CRITICAL: mutate via the structured XMLElement/XMLText API, NOT CommandRouter.write(serialized-string). Myers smart-merge on a re-serialized XML string would destroy the xml_text char-CRDT identity and the attribute-register (LWW) semantics the whole model depends on. The one integration point to wire is the commit entrypoint for structured xml edits — the SAME path normal collaborative xml editing already uses. Verify that path early; it is the load-bearing assumption.

Reparent being a clean register edit (set_attribute on a never-destroyed flat element) is why concurrent subtree edits survive and subtrees cannot duplicate. Keep elements FLAT — never express nesting via real XML child nesting.
acceptance_criteria: Can create an _outline doc; insert/reparent/reorder/collapse/edit-text/delete items via the module; two concurrent edits to one item's text merge char-by-char; concurrent set_parent to different parents resolves to ONE parent with no duplicate (LWW). Unit tests cover each op + the fractional-index between() + (order,id) comparator.
notes: Round-2 cold-read pinned these decisions (see docs/outliner.md §2,§4): (1) commit path = persist the structured op's Yjs update via CommitStoreClient/Document.Server update path, NOT CommandRouter string smart-merge — confirming the exact entrypoint is THIS bead's first task / load-bearing assumption. (2) item text = the <item>'s bare text content as one xml_text CRDT node (not a wrapper tag). (3) fractional-index between(left_key,right_key) minter + (order,id) comparator both live here; minting reads neighbor keys and mints between, no coordination, tiebreaker handles equal-key collision.

title: [EPIC] Outliner — Workflowy/org-mode tree on the flat-bag-of-xml-items model
description:
Workflowy/org-mode-style collapsible bullet-tree feature for Commonplace. Design doc: docs/outliner.md on commonplace-plan/main (this agent, commonplace-plan, owns the design; commonplace code agent owns implementation).

NORTH-STAR DATA MODEL — 'flat bag of xml items' (folds A1+A2, dominates both + multidoc):
A single xml-typed doc (_outline) whose content is a FLAT list of <item id parent order collapsed> elements — all direct children of the YXmlFragment root — where the TREE is expressed by the 'parent' ATTRIBUTE, not by XML nesting, and each item's text is an xml_text CHILD.

Why it dominates (verified against code):
- char-merge FREE (xml_text is a char-CRDT) — many independent char-merge text values in one doc, no per-bullet sub-docs. This is MVP-FREE, not a fast-follow.
- reparent = set_attribute(item,'parent',new_id) — an LWW register on a FLAT element that is NEVER destroyed. So concurrent subtree edits survive and the subtree cannot duplicate (A1's fatal delete+reinsert flaw is gone).
- reorder = fractional-index 'order' attr, sorted (order,id) with node-id tiebreaker.
- one doc — no multidoc per-bullet tax (and multidoc's Tree.Merge is merge-correct, NOT move-correct, so it doesn't even fix move).

MOST-CORRECT AND RIGHT-FOUNDATION COINCIDE: the flat bag is both the simplest MVP and the skeleton of the fully-correct end-state. The hard pieces are ADDITIVE upgrades on this exact model, never a migration away from it.

CRITICAL IMPLEMENTATION CONSTRAINT: mutations MUST use the structured XMLElement/XMLText API committed as CRDT updates — NEVER CommandRouter.write(serialized-string), whose Myers smart-merge would discard xml_text char-CRDT identity and attribute-register semantics that the whole model depends on.

Rendering reuses the chat-room pattern: _outline is the source; v1 ships an outliner-specific OutlineLive (same precedent as chat v1, since ViewCompute is string->string with no generic structured-source primitive yet); _view.xml declares <action>s as the MCP/action-discovery surface.

Scope: 4 MVP sub-beads (i doc+mutation layer, ii tree reconstruction+defensive cycle, iii OutlineLive, iv _view.xml actions+dispatch) + 4 additive follow-ups (Kleppmann move, node-id transclusion/mirrors, zoom, per-viewer collapse). The generic structured-source renderer is chat's existing shared substrate follow-up, not duplicated here.

title: squad-alerts MCP server (cross-ref: HERMES-6e1u)
description:
Build ~/boss-clod/squad-alerts/ — fleet-wide push-alerts channel for Claude Code sessions, modeled on ~/boss-clod/clod-squad/.

Cross-references HERMES-6e1u (boss-clod tracker). Boss-clod handles the channel plugin (HERMES-7bx4), MCP config (HERMES-x5pn), workerclaude launch updates (HERMES-2o2g), and per-agent token provisioning (HERMES-i82b). E2E test (HERMES-2w2w) is joint. This bead is only the server.

Scope:
- server.ts ~300 LOC + db.ts ~150 LOC, Bun + SQLite WAL
- Schema: publishers (name, token_hash, created_at, revoked_at) + alerts (id, publisher, severity, source, title, body, target?, related_bead?, dedup_key?, reply_via?, created_at, delivered_at, suppressed_at) + silences (dedup_key, until_ts, set_by, created_at)

title: Auto-fallback to secondary model on Anthropic 529 / transient errors
description:
When Anthropic returns HTTP 529 (Overloaded), 503, or other retryable errors, the worker should fall back to a configured secondary model rather than terminate silently.

Default fallback: claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 (Haiku is faster + tends to have spare capacity when Sonnet is saturated, as confirmed in the 2026-05-15 live testing round).

Implementation sketch: in Worker.Loop.handle_response (or in Client.call), on {:error, {:http_status, 529, _}} retry once with the bot's :fallback_model (default Haiku). Per-bot override via bot.json fallback_model field. Telemetry event [:commonplace, :bots, :worker, :model_fell_back] so observability surfaces it.

Acceptance: tests prove retry-once on 529 with the right model, and bot.json fallback_model override is honored.
close_reason: Shipped on feat/bots-followups commit 44eea57. 6/6 new tests + 64/64 bots suite green. Worker swaps to fallback_model on 502/503/529; one retry; non-retryable codes pass through; bot.json override + telemetry event in place.

title: Worker outcomes in __bot_activity (completed/cap_hit/error)
description:
Currently __bot_activity only logs trigger decisions (fired/suppressed/skipped). Worker outcomes are surfaced via :telemetry only — invisible in the substrate.

Reserved decisions per the Activity moduledoc:
- 'completed' (worker exited with :end_turn)
- 'cap_hit' (worker hit calls/output_tokens/wall_clock/max_tokens; include 'reason' field)
- 'error' (worker errored; include 'reason')

Implementation sketch: Dispatcher attaches a :telemetry handler at startup for [:commonplace, :bots, :worker, :finished]. Handler resolves the room's activity_uuid from state and calls Activity.append/3 with the outcome.

Acceptance: pumping a worker that hits each outcome surfaces an entry in __bot_activity with the right decision + reason.
close_reason: Shipped on feat/bots-followups commit 3b52cdc. 3/3 new tests + 58/58 bots suite green. Dispatcher attaches a telemetry handler for [:commonplace, :bots, :worker, :finished] and appends a substrate entry for each outcome.

title: v0 chat-room bot build: entity-as-doc, ephemeral cave-diver workers

title: Beads-on-Commonplace P1 — issue/comment/edge/label/import + CLI shim
description:
P1 of beads-on-Commonplace per spec at /home/jes/commonplace-plan/docs/beads-on-commonplace.md.

Scope (per spec §12 P1):
- Issue create / show / update / close (Commonplace.Bd.Issue)
- Comment add / edit / soft-delete (Commonplace.Bd.Comment)
- Dependency edge add / remove (Commonplace.Bd.Dep — single deps.json YMap)

Cycle-2 precision answers baked into design:
- Title is nested YText inside __issue.json's YMap (§3.2)
- Edge add+remove concurrent semantics: YMap LWW by Yjs (Lamport, clientID) (§5.4) — needs unit test fixture
- Importer view-suspend flag for bulk import; in P1 with no views, importer is a no-op for view recompute
- DocRef remap through ForkManifest at fork time (§13)

Demo bar: import a small JSONL fixture, run `commonplace bd create` natively, run `commonplace bd ready` (walk-based, no views in P1) and see the new issue alongside imported open issues.

Module layout (mirrors MUD shape under apps/commonplace/lib/commonplace/bd/):

- Workspace (tree ops: ensure /bd/, issues/, deps.json, labels/)
- IdMint (CX-bhul client-side mint with collision retry)

title: MUD: ad-hoc 'mix run' temp nodes orphan global singletons (MoveServer, TickBot)
description:
Running ad-hoc 'mix run /tmp/foo.exs' for diagnostic / hot-load scripts starts the :commonplace application locally on the temp node. Its supervision tree includes MoveServer and TickBot registered as :global. When the temp node joins the cluster, :global's name-conflict resolver kills one PID per registration (the loser is non-deterministic — sometimes serve's). When the temp node exits, its global PIDs die, and there's nobody left registered, leaving the singleton globally :undefined. Production users (workspace bot's MoveServer) then crash on GenServer.call.

Symptom on 2026-04-28: workspace's  movement crashed with 'no process' against {:global, MoveServer} after a diagnostic script left orphan registrations.

Fixes (any of):
1. Document: always use 'mix run --no-start' for temp/diagnostic scripts that talk to the cluster.
2. Make MoveServer/TickBot start_link no-op-on-already-globally-registered, with a 'follower' mode that doesn't terminate on conflict — :global :name_conflict_resolution_method or similar callback.
3. Move MUD singletons OFF :global onto a single dedicated registry (ETS-backed Registry) that lives only on the serve node, with explicit RPC for cluster-wide reach.
4. Add a healthcheck loop on serve's supervisor: if the global name resolves to a PID on a non-serve node OR is :undefined, restart locally.

(1) is documentation-only. (3)+(4) are structural. Worth picking one before the MUD has more users.

Linked to CX-l4yv (which proposes serve-hosted PlayerSession; same shape of concern).

title: MUD: Bot.spawn_session should host PlayerSession on serve, not the calling escript
description:
When the MCP escript calls Bot.send_input → spawn_session, GenServer.start runs on the calling node. With :global registration the session is reachable cluster-wide, but it physically lives on the escript's BEAM. Module updates (Output, Verbs fixes, etc.) only take if hot-loaded onto every escript node — restart-only scenarios like the 2026-04-28 Output-not-available crash.

Fix: spawn the PlayerSession on the serve node via :rpc.call(serve_node, GenServer, :start, [...]) (or use a dedicated DynamicSupervisor on serve and child_spec there). All bots become co-located on serve; module updates only need to be hot-loaded on serve to take effect everywhere.

Edge: serve might not be running (escript-only mode without daemon). Fallback: spawn locally if :rpc.call fails. Acceptable v1 limitation: bots without serve are degraded.

Filed as a structural follow-up to CX-yu2w; not blocking — hot-loading both escript nodes is the workaround for now.

title: MUD: verb_error appears 3x on raise (duplicate routing)
description:
When a user verb raises (e.g. workspace's kindle test), the player sees 3 instances of '(verb crashed: ...)'. Workspace hypothesized an inheritance chain (object → room → player) but it's actually duplicate-routing of a single firing:

1. emit_verb_error broadcasts :verb_error to the room (everyone including the actor's session sees it)
2. emit_verb_error tells the actor's player_uuid (actor's session sees it again)
3. dispatch returns {:error, '(verb crashed)'} from run_user_verb, which handle_verb_result renders to the actor (third copy)

Fix: emit_verb_error should broadcast with except: [actor_uuid] so bystanders see the verb_error event but the actor doesn't get the duplicate; drop the World.tell call; let the dispatch return value be the only actor-facing message. One social signal (broadcast minus actor), one personal signal (return error reply). Spec §6.2 will need a one-line update.

Linked to CX-v55j umbrella as P3-followup.
close_reason: Shipped at 6667e06. 6 new tests cover Output.tell/broadcast isolation, @dump here, look me, multi-word @dig+@name, verb_error single-copy each per actor/bystander.

title: MUD: @dig and @name parsers eat only first word of name argument
description:
Workspace bot ran '@dig north Old Stone Bridge' and got a room named 'Old' (not 'Old Stone Bridge'). Same shape on @name. @desc correctly takes multi-word text. Inconsistent.

Fix: change do_dig and do_rename clauses in apps/commonplace/lib/commonplace/mud/verbs.ex to take [direction | name_parts] (or [target | new_name_parts]) and Enum.join with ' '. @desc already does this with strip_first_word; the same pattern fits.

Cosmetic: workspace's accidental 'Old' room should be cleaned up by the user after the fix lands. (Or a follow-up @name takes care of it.)

Linked to CX-v55j umbrella as P1-followup.
close_reason: Shipped at 6667e06. 6 new tests cover Output.tell/broadcast isolation, @dump here, look me, multi-word @dig+@name, verb_error single-copy each per actor/bystander.

title: MUD MCP bridge — thin (mud_send + mud_read tools)
description:
Add MCP tools so workspace bots with MCP access can play the MUD without going through the CLI 'mud connect' path.

Approach: thin wrappers.
- mud_send(name, line) — find-or-spawn a PlayerSession for the bot identity; PlayerSession.input_sync; return events drained from an ETS buffer keyed by player UUID. PlayerSession's output_fn writes to that buffer instead of stdout.
- mud_read(name) — drain pending events without sending input (for ambient observation between commands).

PlayerSession needs minimal change: output_fn already pluggable. Add a small helper that returns/creates a buffer per bot identity and an ETS-backed output_fn factory. Sessions are kept alive across calls (registered by name in a Registry) so subscriptions persist.

Demo: workspace bot calls mud_send("bartleby", "look"); receives the room render. Then mud_send("bartleby", "north"); sees forest path. Then alice@CLI says hi; bartleby.poll picks it up.

~30 LoC of MUD-side code + tool wiring on the MCP server side.

Spec follow-up to /home/jes/commonplace-plan/docs/plans/2026-04-28-mud-v0.md (deferred MCP integration).
acceptance_criteria: Workspace bot with MCP access can: look around the bootstrap world, walk between rooms, say things that human CLI players hear, hear human-CLI utterances back via mud_read polling, take/drop/give objects, and author a verb via mud_send-driven editor mode.
close_reason: Thin MUD MCP bridge shipped at 1c4e23a. Two tools (mud_send/mud_read) + Commonplace.MUD.Bot session manager + buffered PlayerSession mode. 6 integration tests prove a bot can look/walk/say/take and hears human players' utterances back. CX-8wkb (fat alternative) remains open as the deferred option.

title: MUD v0 P3: in-world programming (@verb + dispatcher)
description:
Phase 3 of MUD v0. The malleable moment: players write Elixir verbs inside the game and the next caller runs the new code without server restart.

Spec: /home/jes/commonplace-plan/docs/plans/2026-04-28-mud-v0.md §6

Sub-tasks:
- Verb dispatcher: thin wrapper over Commonplace.Code.SourceDoc.compile/2 (already CID-cached in ETS via :source_doc_cache) + apply(module, :run, [ctx])
- @verb <target>:<name> line editor (LambdaMOO-style: print current, accept lines until '.' on own line, replace doc)
- Validate-on-save: run SourceDoc.compile + check :run/1 exported when @verb saves; surface compile errors immediately, not at next call
- Verb error handling: rescue exceptions from Verb.run/1, emit verb_error red event to room + tell triggering player, server keeps running
- Tick verb integration: tick.bot calls Verb.run(ctx) with player==nil for code-doc ticks

Depends on P1 (CX-01pc) and P2 (CX-???). Hot-reload comes free from SourceDoc's content-hash ETS cache — edit doc, hash changes, next call recompiles.
acceptance_criteria: Alice runs '@verb crown.obj:bow' and writes a verb body. Bob types 'bow crown' and sees Alice's prose play out in the room. Alice edits the verb body again; next 'bow crown' runs the new code. No server restart.
close_reason: P3 in-world programming shipped at 65f4255. VerbSource module + scope-ordered dispatch + @verb line editor + TickBot tick.elx priority. The §8 bow-crown demo is validated by integration test: alice writes a verb, bob triggers it, no restart. Hot-reload comes free from SourceDoc's CID-keyed ETS cache. 39/39 MUD tests green.

title: MUD v0 P2: tick loop
description:
Phase 2 of MUD v0. Single tick.bot actor wakes every 1000ms, walks the world tree, fires verbs/tick on rooms/objects with non-null tick_interval_ms.

title: M6 (iii): ViewCompute code_uuid subscription (third commit topic)
description:

title: [bug] ChatRoomLive composer accepts whitespace-only text and creates blank messages
description:
Bug-hunt finding (CX-1si4 via Wallaby).

Reproduction: open /chat/{room}/, fill composer with '   ' (3 spaces), click Post. Result: a message with text='   ' and the placeholder web-user.usr author is appended to _messages and rendered in the LiveView.

Expected: whitespace-only submits should be no-ops (same as empty submits, which ARE rejected today).

Root cause: ChatRoomLive.handle_event('post_message', %{'text' => text}, _) guards on text != "" but NOT String.trim(text) != "". Empty rejected; whitespace not.

Defense in depth: Chat.Actions.post_message could ALSO reject whitespace-only text. Currently accepts any non-empty binary.

Fix: ~3 lines — trim+empty-check in ChatRoomLive's handle_event guard, plus a require_opt-style guard in Chat.Actions for the action-layer half.

Acceptance: Wallaby bug-hunt test 'empty and whitespace-only submits don't create messages' passes. Chat.Actions.post_message tests for whitespace-only get an {:error, ...} return value.

Fixed in ChatRoomLive.handle_event + defense-in-depth require_non_blank guard added to Chat.Actions.post_message and edit_message. title: Substrate: invoke_view_action context auto-resolution (umbrella)
description:

title: Chat R1 — _messages.log red onramp + Commonplace.Chat.OnrampSupervisor
description:
Per-room red-channel onramp wiring.

New module: Commonplace.Chat.OnrampSupervisor (DynamicSupervisor)
- Children: Commonplace.Dataflow.RedLog onramp processes, one per chat room
- Keyed by room name
- API: ensure_started(room_name, log_uuid, magenta_topic), stop(room_name)

Each onramp subscribes to chat:{room}:events magenta topic and appends received messages to the room's _messages.log doc (RedLog YArray-of-JSON).

Lifecycle: room directory creation calls OnrampSupervisor.ensure_started; room teardown calls stop. The supervisor sits alongside other singleton services, NOT inside __processes.json (per docs/chat-room.md a5f3f5e per-room onramp supervision section).

Acceptance:
- post_message → magenta broadcast → onramp appends to _messages.log
- Two rooms get two independent onramps
- Onramp restart (process crash) recovers cleanly without losing messages already committed

title: Amortize reflog checkpoint via change-driven dirty-subtree invalidation
description:
CX-71ej shipped the idempotent half — when nothing changed, 0 writes per checkpoint. But change DETECTION still costs O(tree_reads): one latest_commit per file/dir per checkpoint. On a 10k-file tree, that's 10k reads/checkpoint regardless of activity. jes (msg #3800 via boss-clod relay) wants reflog 'idempotent AND amortized such that it's not expensive'.

Amortization design:
- Subscribe to CommitStore pubsub (commits topic)
- Maintain a dirty-uuid set in ETS, populated as commits land
- At checkpoint time, walk only the path from root to each dirty uuid (computed via Schema reverse-index OR by augmenting the per-dir cursor table with a parent-pointer)
- Cold start: dirty set is empty → must do full bootstrap walk once to populate cursor → then amortized
- Lifecycle: handle CommitStore restart (re-bootstrap), pubsub disconnect (re-bootstrap on reconnect)

Foundation:
- CX-71ej's :reflog_checkpoint_cursor ETS table is the scaffolding. Same key (reflog_dir_uuid). Add: dirty-bit set keyed by data_dir_uuid; pubsub subscriber that maps doc_uuid → enclosing data_dir(s) and marks them dirty.

Acceptance:
- Steady-state checkpoint cost is O(commits-since-last-checkpoint), not O(tree_size)
- Cold-start bootstrap is correct (no missing reflog entries)
- Pubsub reconnect re-bootstraps without losing entries
- All existing reflog tests still pass
notes: Parent: CX-0nkq queue-contention triage. Builds on CX-71ej's cursor table.
close_reason: Amortization shipped: telemetry-driven dirty-set + parent_index ETS tables; clean subtrees skip all reads via fast-path. New tests prove sub_b's data dir + leaf are not read after warming when only sub_a changes. Cold-start safety verified. All 1149 commonplace + 327 yelixer + 95 mcp + 57 cli tests pass; --warnings-as-errors clean.

title: Idempotent reflog checkpoint via per-dir cursor
description:
Per-dir cursor keyed {root_uuid, owner, data_dir_uuid} stores schema_cid + entry CIDs + last reflog_commit_id. snapshot_dir checks cursor; if all CIDs match, returns cached reflog_commit_id and skips both writes (schema_update and snapshot_update). Recurses into children regardless (for change detection), but recursion is cheap when child also cursor-hits.

Why: CX-0nkq queue contention. Reflog.Snapshot.checkpoint walks O(tree_size) per checkpoint and writes ~2k create_chained_commit per 1000-dir tree. Bead notes proposed checking root :latest only, but that fails because file edits don't bubble to root schema. Per-dir cursor preserves correctness while eliminating writes when subtrees are stable.

Acceptance:
- Two consecutive checkpoints on unchanged tree return the same reflog_commit_id (no new commits).
- After modifying one file, only the path from root to that file produces new reflog commits.
- All existing reflog tests pass.
notes: Parent: CX-0nkq narrow-fix #1 of 3
close_reason: Verified across workspace MCP smoke rounds 13-17 — fork retry storm gone, MCP session resilient, reflog overhead eliminated. CX-0nkq's user-visible symptoms all addressed by these three sub-fixes.

title: RedLog mailbox onramp: in-memory writes invisible to tail_red without commit
description:
Workspace MCP smoke test (round 3, 2026-04-25, clod-squad msg #2879) found that magenta sent on agents/claude-code never appears via tail_red on the corresponding mailbox UUID. tail_red returned 0 events / total 0 even when magenta had been broadcast.

**Root cause:**
- CX-92u's mailbox onramp (Commonplace.Dataflow.RedLog onramp GenServer) subscribes to the mailbox topic on init and appends each received magenta message to an in-memory YArray (apps/commonplace/lib/commonplace/dataflow/red_log.ex:117-120).
- The in-memory state is NOT persisted to the commit store until commit_onramp/1 is called explicitly.
- tail_red reads from the commit store via RedLog.load (apps/commonplace_mcp/lib/commonplace_mcp/tools/tail_red.ex:42), so it only sees committed events.
- For the per-agent mailbox, nothing in the system calls commit_onramp on the onramp pid — so the in-memory state never reaches the store.

**Fix shipped (smallest viable):** debounced auto-commit inside RedLog onramp. After each magenta receive, if no commit timer is pending, schedule send_after(:auto_commit, 250ms). Bursts coalesce; tail_red sees events within a quarter-second of arrival. Explicit commit_onramp/1 cancels any pending timer. See commit TBD on main.

**Filed even though shipped** so the design rationale is captured + future regressions have a reference. Closing once workspace confirms tail_red round-trips events.
notes: Filed during CX-0nkq smoke-test round 3. Auto-commit fix shipping in same patch.
close_reason: Verified live across rounds 5-10: send_magenta on agents/<name> reliably lands in tail_red within ~500ms. R8 + R9 pings both persisted to red despite their respective crashes — auto-commit timing fully proven robust. Fix at a45682b: RedLog onramp schedules Process.send_after :auto_commit 250ms after each receive (with sticky-reschedule policy to prevent timer-reset starvation under sustained load).

title: MCP write tool clobbers non-text docs (views, JSON, etc.)
description:
Workspace MCP smoke test (round 3, 2026-04-25, clod-squad msg #2879) reported: writing text via the MCP write tool to a doc whose content type is :view (or any non-text type) succeeds but converts the doc to plain text, destroying the original structure. invoke_view_action subsequently returns 'document content is not a view'.

**Root cause:**
- apps/commonplace_mcp/lib/commonplace_mcp/tools/write.ex calls Commonplace.CommandRouter.write/2.
- CommandRouter.write at apps/commonplace/lib/commonplace/command_router.ex:132 reconstructs the doc, reads ContentType.get_content (defaults '' for non-text content), Diff.apply_diff treats both old + new as text and emits insert/delete ops, encode_update + commit lands a text-shaped doc on the original UUID. Doc's content type is silently coerced to text on the next read.

**Fix options (need design call):**
1. write detects existing content type — if not :text, return {:error, :type_mismatch} with a message naming the actual type. Force flag (e.g. add 'force: true' to args) to opt in to destruction.
2. write preserves the existing content type when targeting a typed doc — Myers-diff on the appropriate string projection.
3. Type-specific write tools (write_text, write_json, write_view) so the surface is unambiguous.

My lean: (1) — the safest default. write SHOULD refuse to write text into a non-text doc unless the caller says they really mean it. (2) is doable but limited (some types like :view aren't string-shaped). (3) is more code surface but most explicit.

**Repro from workspace:**
1. Have any existing view doc (e.g. claude-code.bot — actually that's a presence/.bot, but same shape applies)
2. Call MCP write with that doc's UUID and arbitrary text
3. Subsequent invoke_view_action / cat returns plain text; the original structure is gone

**Filed during CX-0nkq smoke-test round 3.** Companion to CX-c4q9 (mailbox onramp commit timing) which is ready/shipped.
notes: P2: a default-destructive write tool is dangerous; agents could trash workspace state with a single tool call. Discuss design before fixing.
close_reason: Verified at API level (round 8): refuse path returned correct error message ('write refused: doc has content type :map, not :text. Pass force: true to override'); force=true path returned correct response shape ({forced: true, previous_type: 'map', new_bytes: ..., uuid: ...}). Fixes at 1d8e18f (default behavior + force flag) + 1e1949a (split write/2-3-4 to fix Elixir multi-default-arg ambiguity that was misbinding 3-arg calls).

title: presence_info returns all-NIL after CX-hf71 anubis port — possible regression
description:
Workspace MCP smoke test (round 2, 2026-04-25 ~06:13 UTC, clod-squad msg #2875) reported presence_info tool returning all-NIL fields with the exact summary string 'No presence info — server started without a presence_starter.' That string comes from PresenceInfo.summary/1 (apps/commonplace_mcp/lib/commonplace_mcp/tools/presence_info.ex:48) when context[:presence_uuid] is nil.

**Expected:** presence_info returns {presence_uuid, mailbox_uuid, mailbox_topic} with real UUIDs, populated by AnubisServer.init/2 from the injected presence_starter closure.

**Possible causes (need to triage):**
1. AnubisServer.init/2 not invoked — anubis only calls it after notifications/initialized. If client doesn't send that, init/2 never runs.
2. presence_starter closure called but PresenceServer.start_link returned {:error, ...}. AnubisServer.init silently falls through to unchanged frame in that case (anubis_server.ex:81-93 case clause). The error is invisible to the agent.
3. :persistent_term lookup of {AnubisServer, :presence_starter} returned nil because the escript main/0 didn't run AnubisServer.config before the Supervisor started the session.
4. Workspace's MCP escript launched before serve was ready, attached to a wrong/stale serve, etc.

**Diagnostic next steps:**
- Add Logger.warning at AnubisServer.init/2's else branch when starter returns non-:ok, naming the reason — turns silent fall-through into observable failure.
- Verify :persistent_term was set BEFORE first session init ran (race possible if Supervisor.start_link begins before config/1 returns?).
- Check serve logs from workspace's relaunch window for any PresenceServer.start_link error.

**Status:** filed during the CX-0nkq smoke-test round; presence_info worked in the FIRST round (clod-squad msg #2849: 'mailbox UUID e911dbcb-7ecf-500b-9181-6f8a2abcde7b on topic agents/claude-code'). So between round 1 and round 2 something regressed. Most likely candidate: serve restart cycle left state inconsistent, OR the bartleby-removal CRDT edit corrupted the workspace root in a way that breaks PresenceServer init.
close_reason: Diagnostic improvements (Logger.warning on nil / false / other branches of presence_starter result) already shipped in apps/commonplace_mcp/lib/commonplace_mcp/anubis_server.ex:93-129. The bead's 'Diagnostic next steps' list is fully implemented — silent fall-through is now observable. The single-instance regression itself can't be re-reproduced from current state; if it recurs the warnings will identify the failure branch immediately. Related to CX-k320 (closed this session, c31031e) which fixed context dispatch under fresh-VM module-not-yet-loaded conditions — could have masked as a presence_info NIL in some sessions.

title: Sync.Agent crash propagation: bartleby Port exit takes down :commonplace app
description:
**Reproduced** by workspace MCP smoke test (clod-squad msg 2841, 2026-04-25):

Sequence: bartleby Port exit_status 0 → Sync.Agent crash → Application exits :stopped → CommitStoreClient unresponsive → MCP transport dies.

This is a supervision-tree intensity violation: a USER-PROCESS exit (bartleby) cascades up through Sync.Agent into the :commonplace Application supervisor, taking down the whole BEAM. The user process should be isolated; its exit is normal lifecycle, not a system fault.

**Root cause to investigate:**
- Sync.Agent (apps/commonplace/lib/commonplace/sync/agent.ex) is started by Commonplace.Sync.SyncLoop.
- The user process (bartleby) is spawned by Commonplace.Process.Orchestrator.
- Why does bartleby's clean exit (exit_status 0) crash Sync.Agent? Possibilities: shared file lock; Port linked to Sync.Agent process; SyncLoop monitoring user-process and propagating :DOWN as a fatal exit.
- Why does Sync.Agent crashing reach the :commonplace Application? Sync.Agent is presumably under a per-user-process supervisor; max_restarts violation cascading up the tree?

**Workaround in place** (not a fix): /home/jes/commonplace/workspace/__processes.json was moved to /tmp/__processes.json.workspace.bak by boss-clod earlier (msg 2799). Without it, serve doesn't auto-spawn bartleby and the crash chain doesn't fire. Don't add bartleby back to __processes.json until this is fixed properly.

**Next step when picked up:**
1. Reproduce with bartleby restored, capture full BEAM crash dump (or sasl logs if enabled)
2. Trace the supervision tree from bartleby's Port up through Sync.Agent up through :commonplace
3. Add :temporary or rest_for_one boundary at the user-process level so user crashes don't escape the orchestrator's scope

Filed during workspace MCP relaunch effort (CX-y3q smoke test). Companion to CX-glc6 (now closed) and CX-q9aj (workspace's own findings bead, see boss-clod msg 2841).

title: Port hand-rolled MCP server to anubis_mcp
description:

title: CrossEpochMerge.merge(snap, translated_R) duplicates baseline content in merge.update
description:
Surfaced during CX-hmkz diagnosis (2026-04-19).

When CrossEpochMerge.merge is called with L=snapshot_commit and R=translated_regular_commit (both of the same effective namespace via empty L_chain/R_chain), the output merge commit's update bytes carry the baseline 'abc' content as part of the diff, not just the new edit (Y). Applied to D_L (= snap_l reconstructed), the result has DUPLICATED baseline:

  Direct apply: snap_l='Xabc' + merge.update → 'XabcYabc'

CX-k250's existing assertion only checks String.contains?(content, 'Y'), so this doesn't fail. Adding refute String.length(content) > 5 catches it.

Likely cause: encode_diff(D_R, sv_of_D_C) emits items including the baseline-re-author when D_R was reconstructed by replaying snap+translated (which re-applies snap's items to a fresh doc, with random fallback client). The encode_diff's filter logic doesn't know the baseline items are already present in L's chain.

Why CX-hmkz two-peer test passes despite this: in the production sync path, each peer's siblings are REGULAR commits chained to the common ancestor (not snapshot-vs-translated). CrossEpochMerge(r_commit, l_commit) for two regulars at same epoch produces correct ~10-byte merge updates without baseline duplication.

Repro:
  test/commonplace/store/cross_epoch_merge_test.exs:415 'fallback-translated sibling (CX-k250)' — change assertion to also check refute String.length(content) > 5

Fix scope: CrossEpochMerge primitive. Likely needs to filter encode_diff output to drop items whose ids are already covered by L's chain reconstruction, even when R_chain is empty. Or: change r_edits computation to not include re-applied snap items.

Not blocking for any current cohort — production path is unaffected.

Acceptance: CX-k250 unit test passes with stricter assertion (refute length > 5). And/or new test isolating CrossEpochMerge with snapshot L + translated R producing exactly-X-and-Y.
close_reason: Not a primitive bug — test fixture artifact. CX-k250 unit fixture pre-created the ContentType envelope under client=3 before applying c_snap, which Yjs encoded as a duplicate doc state. encode_diff(doc_r, base_sv) then emitted ALL of client=3's items (envelope keys + abc + Y), inflating translated.update from 10→71 bytes and CrossEpochMerge produced 'XabcYabc' on apply. Production builds doc_r the canonical way (start fresh, apply c_snap, insert) and never hits this. Fixed CX-k250 fixture to match the production shape; added refute String.length(content) > 5 regression assertion. Commit e8e6f70.

title: Two-peer E2E cross-epoch: reconstructed text drops L's edit after sibling-merger
description:
Surfaced during CX-k250 resolution attempt at the full two-peer E2E (2026-04-19).

**Scenario**: Two peers sharing a ContentType-envelope doc.
1. Both peers start with shared snapshot C ("abc")
2. Peer A chains L on top of C (inserts "X" at position 0) → "Xabc" (conceptually)
3. Peer A takes a second snapshot snap_l (new epoch, post-divergence)
4. Peer B chains R on top of C (inserts "Y" at position 3) — cross-epoch vs snap_l
5. Bidirectional sibling exchange via NodeSync.import_with_translation (translator fallback on peer A)
6. SiblingMerger.maybe_merge_siblings on both peers → each folds off-chain siblings into :latest
7. Reconstruct doc content on peer A via DocBuilder.reconstruct_doc → ContentType.get_content

**Expected**: text contains "abc", "X", "Y"
**Observed on peer A**: text = "abccY" (has Y but NO X, and a duplicated "c")

**Key observations**:
- CX-k250 verified the primitive (CrossEpochMerge + translator fallback) preserves the sibling edit at the unit level, with ContentType (see test/commonplace/store/cross_epoch_merge_test.exs:417).
- The unit-level scenario applies the merge commit directly onto snap_l's doc (single-level application). The two-peer E2E reconstructs via DocBuilder which walks the full chain including pre-snapshot commits.
- "abccY" suggests L's "X" insertion is being dropped AND some C-side state is being duplicated or mis-replayed. The "cc" is suspicious — could indicate that base "abc" is being applied twice somehow, or that snap_l's re-authored "abc" is being combined with pre-snapshot "abc" without snap_l's X re-authoring taking effect.

**Likely causes to investigate**:
1. DocBuilder.reconstruct_doc walks past snap_l back to pre-snap commits, re-applying C then L then snap_l then merge — potentially replaying C twice if snap_l short-circuits the pre-snap chain incorrectly
2. snap_l's `derivation_map` doesn't link L's X insertion to the post-snap namespace, so X is effectively dropped
3. The merge commit's parent_id vs the sibling-merger's expected chain state is inconsistent when applied through reconstruct_doc

**Repro path**:
1. Use ContentType.create(:text) envelope throughout (raw Text "t" hits the CX-k250 fixture artifact)
2. Follow the scenario above
3. Observe `ContentType.get_content(doc)` returns "abccY" instead of something containing X, Y, abc

**Scope**:
- Diagnose which layer drops X / duplicates c — likely DocBuilder.reconstruct_doc semantics around post-snapshot merge commits
- File sub-beads for any primitive gaps discovered
- Goal: CX-t47h E2E passes observable-level convergence on both peers after cross-epoch sync + sibling-merge

notes:
2026-04-19 Round 4 — FIX SHIPPED.

ROOT CAUSE (final): `LateEditAutoTranslator.maybe_auto_translate/3` ran the late-edit-translator path on ALL incoming commits regardless of kind. When an incoming commit is a snapshot (kind=:snapshot), the translator's primary path succeeds vacuously (snapshot items are self-referential, all refs are 'own'), and produces a TRANSLATED commit struct that's freshly stamped `kind: :regular, parent_id: target_snapshot_id`. The original snapshot is replaced by a regular commit on import — a different semantic. SiblingMerger then sees this 'translated snap_l' as a regular cross-epoch sibling, calls CrossEpochMerge against it, and gets back garbage bytes (because the translated 'regular' is actually a snapshot's full re-authored content masquerading as a delta).

FIX: gate `maybe_auto_translate/3` to only process `kind: :regular` commits. Snapshots, merges, and genesis commits are self-contained in the DAG and should be imported as-is. See apps/commonplace/lib/commonplace/late_edit_auto_translator.ex.

REGRESSION TEST: apps/commonplace/test/commonplace/sync/two_peer_merge_e2e_test.exs 'cross-epoch two-peer merge (CX-hmkz)' — produces "XabcY" on both peers (was "abccY" pre-fix). Sibling-merger interaction now correct.

Test suite: 1485 tests, 0 new failures (one pre-existing agent_test.exs:154 flake unrelated, confirmed by re-running with fix reverted).

FOLLOW-UP filed: separate primitive-level bug surfaced during diagnosis. CrossEpochMerge.merge(snap_l, translated_R) where translated_R is a fallback-positional-rebase commit produces a 71-byte merge update that, when applied to D_snap_l, yields content like "XabcYabc" — duplicates the baseline. CX-k250's existing assertion (`String.contains?(content, "Y")`) is too weak to catch this. The duplication is masked in the production (two-peer) path because each peer's siblings end up as REGULAR commits chained to the common ancestor (not snapshot-vs-translated), and that path produces the correct merge bytes. This bug only surfaces when a snapshot is on the L side of CrossEpochMerge with a translated regular as R sibling.
close_reason: LateEditAutoTranslator gated to kind=:regular commits. Two-peer cross-epoch E2E (CX-69d7 cross-epoch describe block) passes with 'XabcY' on both peers. Snapshots and merges are no longer rewritten into regulars during sync.

title: Bug: CrossEpochMerge emits empty update when merging a fallback-translated sibling
description:
Surfaced during CX-t47h diagnostic (cross_epoch_e2e_test.exs scratch).

Reproduction:
1. Two peers share snapshot C (contains "abc")
2. Peer A chains L on top of C (adds "X")
3. Peer B chains R on top of C (adds "Y") — same epoch as C
4. Peer A snapshots post-divergence → snap_l (new epoch, derived from L state)
5. Peer A imports R via NodeSync.import_with_translation(store_a, r)
6. Primary translation fails (pre-flight :untranslatable :case_b)
7. Fallback fires (auto_fallback telemetry emitted) — Translator.positional_fallback authors a rebased commit translated_R with:
     snapshot_parent = snap_l.id
     parent_id = snap_l.id
     update = positional rebase diff (non-zero bytes)
8. SiblingMerger.maybe_merge_siblings(store_a, uuid) finds translated_R as off-chain sibling
9. Merger.merge(snap_l.id, translated_R.id, :translate) returns a merge commit with:
     parent_id = snap_l.id
     merge_parents = [translated_R.id]
     update = <<0, 0>>  ← EMPTY
10. Reconstructed text on peer A = "abcX" — missing "Y"

Root cause hypothesis: CrossEpochMerge.merge assumes L and R are in DIFFERENT namespaces separated by snapshots. It walks SnapshotAncestry.common_ancestor, composes forward derivation maps for both chains, computes r_edits as encode_diff(D_R, sv_of_D_C), then translates r_edits via r_composed (R→C) and l_inverse (C→L).

For the fallback-translated case, translated_R.snapshot_parent = L.snapshot_parent = snap_l (they share namespace). SnapshotAncestry likely returns C = snap_l with empty L_chain and R_chain. Then:
- r_composed = {} (empty — no snapshots between C and R)
- l_inverse = {} (empty — no snapshots between C and L)
- r_edits should be encode_diff(D_translated_R, sv_of_D_snap_l) — which OUGHT to contain the Y insertion the fallback encoded

But the output is empty. Either:
- encode_diff is returning empty (maybe because the fallback-author client is already covered in snap_l's SV via some pathway)
- Pass-1 filter is removing the Y items
- Pass-2 translate is dropping them
- Or the algorithm has a latent bug when both chains are empty

Scope:
- Reproduce in a focused unit test under test/commonplace/store/cross_epoch_merge_test.exs or similar, isolating Merger.merge from SiblingMerger + the fallback path
- Diagnose: print r_edits, r_composed, pass-1 output, pass-2 output
- Fix at whichever layer drops Y
  - Likely fix: in CrossEpochMerge, short-circuit to a simple "both in same namespace" merge when both chains are empty — emit encode_diff(D_R, sv_of_D_L) directly without the translate passes
  - Or: verify the positional-fallback commit's SV interacts correctly with the translate pipeline

Acceptance:
- CrossEpochMerge.merge on (snap, fallback_translated_sibling) produces a merge commit whose update, applied on snap-doc, yields a doc containing BOTH snap's content and the fallback sibling's edit
- cross_epoch_e2e_test.exs (CX-t47h scratch test) passes with observable "Y" in reconstructed text on peer A

Blocks: CX-t47h follow-up completion (the E2E test depends on this primitive being correct).

Diagnostic test at apps/commonplace/test/commonplace/sync/cross_epoch_e2e_test.exs (currently left in-place as a repro harness). Can be cleaned up after the fix lands.
close_reason: Not a bug — test-fixture artifact. Root cause: the CX-t47h diagnostic fixture used raw Yelixer.Types.Text with a custom type name ('t'), which bypasses the ContentType envelope that Translator.positional_fallback→Rebase.rebase reads via ContentType.get_content. With nothing to read, Rebase sees pre==dirty==nil, short-circuits, and returns the target doc unchanged → empty translated update. Production sync always goes through ContentType — the empty-merge-update behavior does not occur there. Shipped 7e1cad6: regression test with the real ContentType envelope round-tripping through translator fallback + CrossEpochMerge — merge correctly carries the sibling's edit.

title: Cross-epoch two-peer merge E2E: translator-hook + sibling-merger interaction
description:
Follow-up to CX-69d7 (which ships the two-strategy + sibling-merger observable-convergence patterns, defers the cross-epoch case).

Context: The cross-epoch scenario in CX-69d7 prototypes revealed a subtle interaction between NodeSync.import_with_translation (CX-7cm1) and SiblingMerger.maybe_merge_siblings (CX-4qn1). Specifically:

- Peer A snapshots post-divergence → moves to new epoch
- Peer B has R chained off OLD snapshot_parent (cross-epoch w.r.t. A)
- Peer A imports R via import_with_translation → depending on translatability, R is either replaced by a translated commit (:translated), dropped (:fallback), or stored as-is with telemetry (:skipped)
- Peer A runs SiblingMerger.maybe_merge_siblings → finds the (possibly-translated) R as off-chain sibling → Merger.merge(snap_l, translated_R, :translate)
- Observable text on peer A is "abcX" — missing the "Y" edit from R

Likely causes to investigate:
1. The translator replaces R with a commit whose "Y" edit does not survive the translation (e.g. ref target item got rewritten to a no-op under the new epoch)
2. The merge picks up the ORIGINAL (untranslated) R via :skipped path; CrossEpochMerge then tries to translate at merge time and the :case_b :untranslatable failure from the earlier prototype happens silently inside SiblingMerger (which reports {:ok, :merged} regardless)
3. Merger.merge(snap_l, R, :translate) succeeds at the commit level but the resulting update bytes do not carry R edits across the epoch boundary

Scope:
- Trace import_with_translation outcome for the CX-69d7 cross-epoch fixture (which of :translated/:skipped/:fallback fires)
- Determine whether the issue is at translator-time or merge-time
- If it is a genuine gap (translator cannot preserve edits), file as a new primitive bead
- If it is a fixture issue (test setup wrong shape), adapt CX-69d7-style setup to exercise the real production path

Expected acceptance:
- A two-peer E2E test where peer A snapshots post-divergence, peer B has a pre-snapshot edit, sync + sibling-merger yields text containing both sides edits on both peers
- OR: a clear finding + follow-up beads for whichever primitive layer has the gap

Not a blocker on CX-69d7 per se — that bead ships with the same-epoch two-strategy coverage. This bead closes out the cross-epoch story.
notes:
Unblocked by CX-k250 close (not a bug — fixture artifact). CX-k250 regression test verifies the primitive (translator fallback → CrossEpochMerge) works correctly at the unit level with ContentType envelope.

Remaining work for full CX-t47h E2E acceptance: a two-peer E2E test where peer A snapshots post-divergence, both peers sync siblings bidirectionally, and SiblingMerger.maybe_merge_siblings on each peer yields observable convergence. A ContentType-fixture prototype surfaced a NEW issue on peer A — reconstructed text came out 'abccY' (missing L's 'X' edit) — likely in DocBuilder.reconstruct_doc's interaction with post-snapshot chained merges or in how snap_l's re-authored content composes with subsequent commits. Separate from CX-k250; warrants its own focused session.
close_reason: Acceptance satisfied by CX-hmkz regression test (commit f1fc9c8). The 'cross-epoch two-peer merge (CX-hmkz)' describe block in apps/commonplace/test/commonplace/sync/two_peer_merge_e2e_test.exs exercises exactly the acceptance scenario: peer A snapshots post-divergence, peer B's R is cross-epoch w.r.t. snap_l, bidirectional sibling exchange via NodeSync.import_with_translation + bilateral SiblingMerger.maybe_merge_siblings yields observable convergence — both peers reconstruct 'XabcY'. The cross-epoch story closes out cleanly with the CX-hmkz fix (gating maybe_auto_translate to :regular commits).

title: Distributed sibling-commit merge (post-import chain reassembly)
description:
Follow-up to CX-l7j. CX-l7j fixed in-process concurrent-writer races via GenServer mailbox serialization in create_chained_commit. A separate correctness concern remains: when import_commit accepts commits from remote peers, two peers that independently wrote chained off the same shared parent end up as siblings post-import. Linear readers walking from :latest see only one branch — commits aren't lost (import_commit persists them) but they're invisible to linear chain walks.

Root cause: post-import, peers see only one branch of sibling commits when walking linearly from :latest. CX-l7j's GenServer serialization can't help across process/node boundaries — the race is between peers' histories, not their mailbox slots.

Mechanism reuse: same-namespace sibling merge goes through Merger.merge(L, R, strategy: :translate) — the L_ns == R_ns path already tested in CX-dx22 (union-case collapse). The primitive exists; this bead is about triggering + policy.

Open policy questions:
- Trigger point: post-import hook inside handle_call({:import_commit, ...})? Sync.Agent periodic sweep? Explicit caller?
- Strategy default: :translate vs :merge_snapshot?
- User-visible surfacing: flag divergence state or auto-resolve silently?
- Auto-trigger vs opt-in?

These parallel the snapshot-policy discussion queued at CX-4e2g..CX-592q and should probably be decided together.

Priority: leave P2/P3 for jes to adjust. Not blocking CX-l7j's in-process fix — that's the P1 bug in the named-scope sense.
close_reason: Landed in ca7042c: Commonplace.SiblingMerger.maybe_merge_siblings/3 primitive + CommitStore.write_prebuilt_commit_cas/2 (generic CAS write for prebuilt commits) + CommitStore.all_commit_ids_for_doc/2 (all persisted vs chain-reachable). DAG reachability follows parent_id AND merge_parents so folded-in siblings stop counting as siblings — idempotence fixpoint. Default :translate strategy, :merge_snapshot override accepted. Scope: primitive only — wiring (post-import hook vs. sync-agent sweep vs. explicit) deferred to follow-up beads. 6 dedicated tests green + 283/0 regression across snapshot_trigger + entire store subsuite.
