For envelope-structure docs (ContentType.create + YText 'content'), Commonplace.Store.Snapshotter.build/1 produces a derivation map that pairs unrelated items. Example: source doc client 1 authors (1,0)=_type, (1,1)=_name, (1,2)="abc" (len 3). Snapshot replay (Yelixer.Doc.snapshot_update) iterates source.types in map-key order, which is not source insertion order — so the snapshot doc has items (1,0)="abc" (len 3), (1,3)=_name, (1,4)=_type. pair_ids then pairs by position: snap(1,0) ↔ src(1,0), pairing content with _type. Result: DM is garbage and any late-edit ref into the source's text item resolves to the wrong snap id. Late-edit pre-flight reports :case_b for envelope docs with text content even though semantically the edit is valid. Impact: translator primary path (CX-fefz / Build 6.5) produces spurious :case_b failures on envelope-structure docs — the fallback (CX-7sln) masks this in practice but the primary path is silently wrong. Fix direction: either (a) replay types in a deterministic order matching source item order (e.g., sort by earliest-item-clock) so position pairing is correct, or (b) pair by content identity (match snap items to source items by parent+parent_sub for map entries, by parent for text items). Note: CX-fefz's sub-clock expansion (commit snapshot items to clocks 2..4) is independently correct — this bug is prior to expansion at the pair_ids layer.
design: Reproduced locally in apps/commonplace/test/commonplace/store/translator_fallback_test.exs — the bare-text scenario (Text type 't') works because there's only one type so replay order is trivial; the envelope scenario (root map + content text) fails pre-flight naturally. Blocks correct primary-path translation for the real commonplace tree docs.
acceptance_criteria: Primary-path Translator.translate_edit succeeds on envelope-structure docs with text content. late_edit_preflight and translator_test suites extended to cover envelope scenario end-to-end without :case_b false positive.
close_reason: Fixed Snapshotter pair_ids bug by canonicalizing snapshot_update replay order to source-clock order. Envelope-structure docs (root YMap + named content) now translate correctly via primary DM path. Full commonplace store suite + yelixer suite green.

title: Namespace validator rejects late-edit translated commits introducing new item-authorship clients
description:
A late-edit translated commit (Build 6.5) has item ids from the translating peer's client (e.g. client 2) but refs pointing into the target snapshot's namespace (e.g. snapshot built from client 1). The current namespace validator (CX-ch5) runs MapSet.subset?(update_ids, namespace) where update_ids includes item-authorship clients; a translating peer that wasn't previously in the namespace is rejected with {:client_ids_outside_namespace, [peer_client_id]}. This blocks persistence of legitimately-translated late edits.

Observed while implementing CX-fefz (6.5) in apps/commonplace/test/commonplace/store/translator_test.exs — the CID-dedup integration test was dropped because it triggered this rejection. Byte-determinism test (same file) passes because it checks in-memory commit structs without persistence.

Fix direction (TBD): extend update_client_ids or the validator to split item-authorship clients (allowed to join) from ref/delete_set clients (must be in namespace). Alternative: mark translated commits with metadata.kind that bypasses namespace validation or has its own check that focuses only on translated refs (pre-flight already validated those).

Acceptance:
- Translated late-edit commit produced by Translator.translate_edit/4 can be imported via CommitStore.import_commit/2 even when the translating peer's client is new to the namespace.
- Re-enable the CID-dedup test in translator_test.exs.
- Existing namespace validator tests still pass.
close_reason: Role-split validator landed: authorship-vs-reference axis (namespace = initial snapshot clients ∪ authors-since; authorship EXTENDS, references MUST subset). Yelixer.Encoding.update_client_ids_by_role/1 helper; new :unknown_reference telemetry distinct from blanket :namespace_mismatch. CID-dedup-via-import tests for CX-fefz (translator), CX-fdjh (cross_epoch_merge), CX-dx22 (merge_snapshotter) landed in same commit per msg 2236 directive. 4 CX-ch5 tests retrofitted. Full suite 1402 green. Commit df8cac4.

title: 7.5 — Top-level merge router + red events
design: Thin dispatch over 7.3 and 7.4. Strategy choice is explicit at call site — future work can layer heuristics on top (e.g., 'if one side has >N commits since C, prefer merge-snapshot') but this bead does not include them.
acceptance_criteria:
- End-to-end test: both strategies produce valid merged commits with the expected metadata shapes.
- Red events observable.
- Strategy choice is caller-level; no automatic heuristics.
- Fallback flag routes untranslatable edges to positional rebase (6.6 reuse).
close_reason: Merger.merge(store, L, R, strategy:, opts) dispatches to CrossEpochMerge (:translate) or MergeSnapshotter (:merge_snapshot) with explicit caller-chosen strategy — no heuristics. Emits [:commonplace, :merge, :completed] and [:commonplace, :merge, :failed] red events. 7 tests green. Drive-by fix: CrossEpochMerge + MergeSnapshotter fetch_commit now matches :none (the actual CommitStore.get_commit return) instead of :not_found.

title: 7.4 — Merge-snapshot construction
description:
Produce a snapshot commit with snapshot_parents = [L, R] and a derivation map containing two entries (one per source namespace). The merge-snapshot establishes a fresh namespace that both sides derive from. snapshotter_version inherited from Build 5 (CX-umz) — no new field required.

Depends on 7.1, 7.2, 6.3. Blocks 7.5.
design:
Extend Snapshotter.build/1 to accept multiple parents. Internally:
- Reconstruct L's doc via DocBuilder replay.
- Reconstruct R's edits since common ancestor C (reuse 7.1 to find C), apply to L's doc — this is a 'replay R into L' operation that uses Build 6 translation (6.3) to commute R's edits through the L chain.
- Run snapshot_update/1 on the combined doc.
- The resulting DM has two entries: %{L => {new_id → old_id_in_L}, R => {new_id → old_id_in_R}}.

Hash formula unchanged — canonical_metadata handles the multi-parent shape via the existing snapshot_parents: [hash, ...] field.
acceptance_criteria:
- Multi-parent snapshot with DM covering both epochs.
- Byte-determinism across two peers producing the same merge-snapshot from same inputs.
- Late-edit translation works against merge-snapshots (the DM-with-multiple-entries case is already structurally supported by 6.2's outer-map inversion and 6.3's reference translation).
close_reason: MergeSnapshotter.build_merge_snapshot/3 produces multi-parent :snapshot commits with snapshot_parents=[L_ns,R_ns] and a two-entry DM covering both epochs. 5 tests green: shape, content, byte-determinism, late-edit L-only ref, late-edit C-content ref. CID-dedup-via-import determinism tests deferred to CX-fbs6 (validator cross-epoch escape hatch).

title: 7.3 — Translate-into-primary merge
description:
Given D_L (namespace L) and D_R (namespace R), produce a merge commit with parent_id = D_L.id, merge_parents = [D_R.id], metadata.snapshot_parent = L, and ops = R's edits since common ancestor C commuted into L's namespace.

Depends on 6.3, 6.4, 7.1, 7.2. Blocks 7.5.
design:
Algorithm:
1. {C, L_chain, R_chain} = common_ancestor(L, R) (7.1).
2. Invert each DM in R_chain via 6.2 → inverse_R_chain.
3. inverse_R_composed = compose_dms(inverse_R_chain) (7.2).
4. First translation pass: rewrite R's op references via inverse_R_composed (6.3) → ops in C's namespace.
5. L_composed = compose_dms(L_chain) (7.2).
6. Invert L_composed (6.2) → inverse_L_composed.
7. Second translation pass: rewrite ops from step 4 via inverse_L_composed (6.3) → ops in L's namespace.
8. Pre-flight validate (6.4); fail if any ref untranslatable.
9. Emit merge commit via CommitStore.create_commit with merge_parents.
acceptance_criteria:
- Integration test: two branches diverging after a snapshot, each adding edits, merge produces a commit containing both sides' effects in L's namespace.
- Byte-determinism across two peers performing the same merge.
- Failure modes (untranslatable-in-either-direction) surface via red events (reuse 6.5's :untranslatable event with phase: :r_to_c or phase: :c_to_l).
close_reason: Build 7.3: CrossEpochMerge.merge/3 implements two-pass translation (R→C forward compose, C→L inverse compose). Merge commit has parent_id=L_id, merge_parents=[R_id], snapshot_parent=L_ns. Empty-chain degenerate case short-circuits as identity. Emits [:commonplace, :late_edit, :untranslatable] with :phase metadata. Tests: byte-determinism, happy-path content preservation, R→C phase telemetry, intermediate-state adversarial DM injection. DEFERRED to CX-fbs6: CID-dedup-via-import tests — namespace validator rejects translated commits whose item-authorship clients are new to target namespace. 7.3 ships with in-memory byte-determinism on the merge commit struct; end-to-end store-accepts-merge tests land with CX-fbs6. Commit ff0e5a0.

title: 7.2 — compose_dms/1 chained-lookup helper
description:
Given a list of derivation maps [DM1, DM2, ..., DMn] where DMi maps namespace(Si-1) → namespace(Si), produce a single composed map mapping namespace(S0) → namespace(Sn) via chained lookup. Per docs/late-edits-and-derivation-map.md § Composability Constraint, composition uses only the DMs' own bytes — no snapshot data required.

Depends on 6.2. Blocks 7.3, 7.4.
design: Fold over the list with DM_composed[S0][new_id_in_Sn] = DM1[S0][DM2[S1][...DMn[Sn-1][new_id_in_Sn]]]. Forward composition only in this bead; inverse composition is obtained by inverting each DM via 6.2 first, then composing via the same fold.
acceptance_criteria:
- compose([]) = identity (empty).
- compose([DM]) = DM.
- compose([DM1, DM2]) = chained lookup as specified.
- Property test: composed result applied to an id matches sequential application across the same chain.
- Run on real snapshot chains produced by the snapshotter.
close_reason: Build 7.2 shipped as 56142e8. Namespace.compose_dms/1 folds [DM1..DMn] into a single composed map %{hash(S0) => %{new_in_Sn => old_in_S0}} via chained lookup. Mid-chain misses are dropped per spec. Tests: 2 doctests + 9 unit (empty, singleton, all-empty, two-DM simple, mid-chain-miss drop, no-matches, three-DM end-to-end, 4-deep composed-equals-sequential property, integration against real Snapshotter.build/1 across two hops). Uses only DM bytes — no snapshot contents needed.

title: 7.1 — Common-ancestor snapshot walk
description:
Given commits L and R, walk their snapshot_parent chains to find the shared snapshot C (lowest common ancestor in the snapshot DAG). Return {C, L_chain, R_chain} where each chain is the ordered list of snapshots traversed from C up to L/R's current namespace.

Blocks 7.3, 7.4.
design: Graph walk over snapshot_parent edges. MVP assumption: snapshot chains are linear (no merge-snapshots yet in play for this walk) — the walk terminates at the first shared snapshot. Extension to merge-snapshot-aware walks (when 7.4 introduces snapshot_parents list ≥ 2) filed as a follow-up if not naturally bundled.
acceptance_criteria:
Unit tests covering:
- (a) L and R share immediate snapshot (trivial)
- (b) L and R diverge through N snapshots
- (c) one side has more snapshots than the other
- (d) no common ancestor (separate docs — return error)
close_reason: Build 7.1 shipped as 0c73c82. Snapshot-DAG LCA walker: SnapshotAncestry.common_ancestor/3 (GenServer-backed) + common_ancestor_with_fetcher/3 (testable core). Returns {C, L_chain, R_chain} where chains are snapshots from just-after-C up to each input's namespace. 8 synthetic tests (cases a/b/c/d per spec + input variants incl. snapshot-as-input and :unknown_commit) + 2 integration tests against real CommitStore. MVP linear — multi-parent extension scoped for 7.4 follow-up.

title: 6.6 — Positional-rebase fallback dispatch (opt-in)
description:
Add opt-in flag fallback_to_positional: true to Translator.translate_edit/3. When pre-flight fails with :case_a or :case_b and the flag is set, dispatch to the existing positional-rebase module (CX-6a7). Default is false (fail loud). Emit [:commonplace, :late_edit, :fallback] red event on fallback.

Depends on 6.5.
design: Opt-in per-edit (not per-doc or per-peer). Fallback loses byte-determinism and reassigns authorship to the local peer — the documented tradeoff. Red event surfaces the invocation so it's observable and auditable.
acceptance_criteria:
- With flag set, :case_a / :case_b failures route to positional rebase and produce a valid commit (observable effect preserved).
- Red event emitted on fallback.
- With flag unset, behavior matches 6.5 (fail loud).
notes: Implemented positional-rebase fallback in Commonplace.Store.Translator.translate_edit_with_snapshot/3. Flag fallback_to_positional: true + pre_doc: %Yelixer.Doc{} opts dispatch to Commonplace.Document.Rebase.rebase/3 on pre-flight failure. Returns {:ok, commit} chained to target snapshot with the dirty effect preserved; emits [:commonplace, :late_edit, :fallback] with %{edit_hash, target_snapshot, reason, ref_id, commit_id}. Default false matches 6.5. Surfaced related bug CX-hzdc in the snapshotter (pair_ids mispairs envelope-doc DM entries when snapshot_update reorders types) — filed separately; fallback path masks it for now.
close_reason: Shipped CX-7sln (Build 6.6) in commit cc61833. Translator.translate_edit_with_snapshot/3 now accepts fallback_to_positional: true + pre_doc: opts; on pre-flight :case_a/:case_b, dispatches to Commonplace.Document.Rebase.rebase/3 and returns a commit chained to the target snapshot. Emits [:commonplace, :late_edit, :fallback] red event. Default false preserves 6.5 fail-loud. 4 new tests (envelope + bare scenarios, flag unset, flag set happy-path, telemetry, no-trigger on primary success). Filed CX-hzdc for snapshotter pair_ids bug surfaced during this work.

title: 6.5 — End-to-end translator pipeline with red events
description:
Compose 6.2 + 6.3 + 6.4 into a single entry point: Translator.translate_edit(edit, target_snapshot, opts) returning {:ok, translated_commit} or {:error, reason}. Emit red events on all outcomes:
- [:commonplace, :late_edit, :translated] — success
- [:commonplace, :late_edit, :untranslatable] — failure with %{reason: :case_a | :case_b, edit_hash, target_snapshot}

Does NOT dispatch to fallback — 6.6's scope.

Depends on 6.4. Blocks 6.6.
design: Wire through CommandRouter or CommitStore as appropriate (commonplace's call). Red events via [:commonplace, :late_edit, ...] telemetry prefix. Integration test showing full end-to-end translation producing a commit landing in the expected namespace.
acceptance_criteria:
- All three red events observable in telemetry tests.
- Integration test: edit authored against P gets translated into a commit whose ops live in S's namespace.
- Byte-determinism: two translating peers produce byte-identical commits.
close_reason: Build 6.5 shipped: Translator.translate_edit/4 at apps/commonplace/lib/commonplace/store/translator.ex. Composes 6.2 (inverse DM) + 6.3 (translator) + 6.4 (pre-flight) into a single entry point returning {:ok, %Commit{}} or {:error, reason}. Emits [:commonplace, :late_edit, :translated] with %{edit_hash, target_snapshot, commit_id} on success and [:commonplace, :late_edit, :untranslatable] with %{edit_hash, target_snapshot, reason, ref_id} on pre-flight failure. Also fixed sub-clock DM expansion at translator build time (snapshotter pairs only start-clocks; Yjs refs can point mid-item). 6 tests in apps/commonplace/test/commonplace/store/translator_test.exs cover success (shape + telemetry + S-namespace apply), :case_a/:case_b failures with ref_id, and byte-determinism. Full suite: 916 tests, 0 failures. Filed CX-fbs6 for namespace-validator gap (late-edit commits that introduce new authorship clients). Commit 8d1e450.

title: 6.4 — Pre-flight validator + atomic apply
description:
Before applying a translated batch to S, confirm every rewritten reference resolves to a live item in S. If any ref is missing, fail the whole batch atomically. Two failure reasons distinguished per docs/late-edits-and-derivation-map.md § 'Missing entries in the inverse':
- :case_a — E edits an item tombstoned-in-S
- :case_b — E's adjacent-insert origin was tombstoned before S

Depends on 6.2, 6.3. Blocks 6.5.
design: After 6.3 rewrites, validator walks translated refs and looks up each in the inverse DM + live-item set of S. Return {:ok, ops} or {:error, {:untranslatable, reason, ref_id}}. Atomic apply uses existing DocBuilder apply path.
acceptance_criteria:
- Property test: random edits parented on random snapshotted docs, with injected tombstones, producing expected case_a / case_b failures.
- Live edits pass through cleanly.
- Atomicity test: failed pre-flight leaves S unmodified.
close_reason: Build 6.4 shipped: LateEditPreflight.validate/2 + translate_and_validate/2 at apps/commonplace/lib/commonplace/store/late_edit_preflight.ex. Pre-flight walks every item ref (origin/right_origin/parent:id) and every delete_set clock, exempting E's own items, and short-circuits on first missing ref with {:error, {:untranslatable, :case_a | :case_b, id}}. case_a for target/delete refs; case_b for origin/right_origin. translate_and_validate guarantees atomic apply — translator never runs on a failed pre-flight. 12 tests in apps/commonplace/test/commonplace/store/late_edit_preflight_test.exs cover all cases incl. explicit atomicity test. Full commonplace suite: 910 tests, 0 failures. Commit 03f6682.

title: 6.3 — Rewrite Yjs op references via inverse DM
description:
Given an update binary E and an inverse DM, produce a new update binary E' where every op's (left-origin, right-origin, parent) reference has been translated. (clientID, clock) of each op's own identity is preserved unchanged — this is what gives byte-determinism across peers. This is the core load-bearing primitive of Build 6.

Depends on 6.1, 6.2. Blocks 6.4, 6.5, 7.3.
design:
New module (commonplace's call on name — Yelixer.Encoding.Translate or Commonplace.LateEdit.Translator). Depends on encoder determinism (6.1) and DM inversion (6.2). Algorithm:
1. Decode E via existing decoder.
2. For each item, translate origin_left, origin_right, parent via inverse_dm[ref] when present. Absent references are left untranslated; pre-flight (6.4) will catch them.
3. Preserve each item's own (clientID, clock) unchanged.
4. Re-encode via Yelixer.Encoding.encode_update/1.
acceptance_criteria:
- For every op type Yelixer supports, translation preserves (clientID, clock) and rewrites refs as specified.
- Property test: two independent callers passing the same (E, inverse_dm) produce byte-identical output.
- Round-trip test: translate(encode(ops), identity_map) == encode(ops).
- Unit tests for each reference type (left-origin, right-origin, parent).
close_reason: Build 6.3 shipped as 9ff3837. Commonplace.Store.LateEditTranslator.translate_update/2 — decodes E, flattens outer-keyed inverse DM, rewrites origin/right_origin/{:id,_} parent refs per item while preserving each item's own (clientID, clock), re-encodes via Yelixer.Encoding.encode_update/1 against a synthetic Doc/BlockStore. 15 tests: identity/round-trip, identity preservation, per-ref-type (left-origin, right-origin, {:id,_} parent, {:named,_} untouched), bare-nil-origin, outer-keyed multi-source lookup, multi-client, repeated-call byte-determinism, 2-stage translate, 50-iteration randomized determinism batch. Pre-flight 6.4 layers on top — 6.3 passes unknown refs through unchanged per spec.

title: 6.2 — Derivation-map inversion helper
description:
Add Commonplace.Store.Namespace.inverse_derivation_map/1 that flips {new_id → old_id} to {old_id → new_id}. Pure function, O(N). Input is a full DM (map of maps keyed by source_snapshot_hash); output inverts the inner map only, outer keys unchanged.

Blocks 6.3, 6.4, 7.3.
design: One-liner on Enum.map + Map.new. Doctest for documentation. No caching in this bead — inversion is cheap; callers may memoize per-batch if a hotpath appears.
acceptance_criteria: Function exists; doctest passes. Unit tests cover: (a) empty inner map; (b) single entry; (c) multi-source outer map (future-proofing for merge-snapshots in Build 7).
close_reason: Shipped as new commit. Pure inversion helper with 7 units + 3 doctests. Unblocks 6.3, 6.4, 7.2, 7.3.

title: 6.1 — Yelixer encoder byte-determinism property test
description:
Before any late-edit translation code ships, Yelixer.Encoding.encode_update/1 must be shown byte-deterministic given equal op sets. Mirrors the snapshot_update/1 determinism gate already landed in CX-umz.

Blocks 6.3.
design: Property test: generate random op lists, encode twice through the same function, assert equal bytes. Cover edge cases: empty op list, single op, all three reference types (left-origin, right-origin, parent), mixed clientIDs, ops touching every Yelixer-supported Y-type (YText, YMap, YArray, YXmlFragment/Element).
acceptance_criteria: Property test with ≥100 generated cases, all passing. Encoder determinism requirement documented in Yelixer.Encoding module docstring. If the test fails, the encoder fix is scoped in this bead — 6.3 cannot ship without encoder determinism.
close_reason: Shipped as 8c2ae46. Property test caught two real bugs: (1) apply_update/2 didn't merge decoded ds into doc.delete_set, (2) encode_delete_set/1 iterated map without sorting. Both fixed. 11 tests + 2 properties green across Text/YMap/Array/XMLFragment. 6.3 gate cleared.

title: Build 7 — Cross-epoch merge + merge-snapshots
description:
Implement multi-parent merges across namespace boundaries per docs/merkle-tracked-yjs.md § Cross-Epoch Merges. Two strategies:
- Translate-into-primary: commute R's edits backward through inverse DMs to common ancestor C, forward through DMs to L's namespace, emit merge commit.
- Merge-snapshot: establish a fresh namespace with snapshot_parents = [L, R], DM covering both source namespaces.

Builds on Build 6's translation machinery (6.3 reused end-to-end in 7.3). compose_dms/1 lands here only (no retrofit to 6 per jes).

Spec: /home/jes/commonplace-plan/docs/plans/2026-04-18-builds-6-7-beads.md (commit 3707fcb). Sub-beads: 7.1 → 7.2 → {7.3, 7.4} (parallel) → 7.5.
acceptance_criteria: All five sub-beads closed green. Integration test: two branches diverging after a snapshot, each adding edits, both merge strategies produce valid merged commits containing both sides' effects. Byte-determinism across peers performing the same merge.
close_reason: All 5 sub-beads (7.1-7.5) green. Integration test in merger_test.exs runs both :translate and :merge_snapshot on the same L/R scenario and verifies content preservation (abc + X + Y) for both strategies. Byte-determinism covered in per-sub-bead tests (CX-fdjh, CX-dx22). Three open tasks deferred to CX-fbs6 (namespace validator cross-epoch escape hatch) — CID-dedup-via-import for CX-fefz, CX-fdjh, CX-dx22.

title: Build 6 — Late-edit translation (primary path via derivation maps)
description:
Implement the primary late-edit path specified in docs/late-edits-and-derivation-map.md. An edit E authored against pre-snapshot commit P gets translated into S's namespace by preserving its (clientID, clock) and rewriting its references via an inverse derivation map. Byte-deterministic across peers, composable with CID dedup. CX-6a7 positional rebase is retained as opt-in fallback.

Ships horizonless per jes 2026-04-18 (composability-safe maps mean indefinitely-old stragglers translate cleanly). compose_dms/1 is NOT part of Build 6 — single-step inverse lookup suffices.

Spec: /home/jes/commonplace-plan/docs/plans/2026-04-18-builds-6-7-beads.md (commit 3707fcb). Sub-beads: 6.1 → 6.2 → 6.3 → 6.4 → 6.5 → 6.6.
acceptance_criteria: All six sub-beads closed green. End-to-end integration test: an edit authored against P, given a snapshot S produced from P, translates to a commit in S's namespace whose ops match the expected byte sequence. Two independent peers performing the same translation produce byte-identical commits (CID dedup holds).
close_reason: All 6 sub-beads (CX-w62, CX-2rd, CX-yvhs, CX-0ut2, CX-fefz, CX-7sln) closed green. E2E translator + byte-determinism test live at apps/commonplace/test/commonplace/store/translator_test.exs (commit 8d1e450).

title: Snapshot op + derivation map + deterministic-anyone hash (Build 5, CX-umz)
description:
Closes the CX-bgy umbrella. Deliver the actual namespace-epoch compaction: snapshot commits with deterministic encoding, derivation map, and snapshot_parents/snapshotter_version metadata.

Scope:
1. Snapshot creation entry point (MVP explicit trigger; reuse/extend create_snapshot_commit)
2. Canonical snapshot encoding (Yelixer snapshot_update deterministic across instances)
3. Derivation map construction {source_snapshot_hash -> {new_item_id -> old_item_id}}
4. Metadata shape: %{kind: :snapshot, snapshot_parents: [hash], derivation_map: map, snapshotter_version: 1}
5. Hash conformance: sha256((parent_id||<<>>) ∥ update ∥ canonical_metadata(metadata))
6. Namespace establishment: post-snapshot regular commits auto-stamp snapshot.id (CX-a04 should handle)

Gating precondition: Yelixer encode-determinism property test — two instances, same state, byte-identical.

Non-goals: late-edit translation, cross-epoch merge, multi-parent snapshots, DM composition impl, automatic cadence, DM eviction.

Required tests:
- Snapshot happy path
- Deterministic-anyone property (load-bearing)
- Hash conformance out-of-band
- Namespace bootstrap post-snapshot
- Derivation map coverage
- Composability property (hand-crafted)
- snapshotter_version in hash
- Empty / genesis-only doc
- Yelixer encode-determinism property
close_reason: Build 5 shipped as 0255b42. Snapshot op + deterministic-anyone hash + derivation map. Closes the CX-bgy umbrella. 16 snapshot_op tests + 5 yelixer determinism tests green.

title: Auto-stamp snapshot_parent on regular commits (Build 4)
description:
Analog to CX-m3x but for the namespace dimension. CommitStore.create_commit should auto-populate metadata.snapshot_parent = current_namespace(latest) when caller produces a regular commit without explicit snapshot_parent. Then tighten validator to reject regular commits missing snapshot_parent (post-umbrella).

Scope:
1. Auto-stamp snapshot_parent in create_commit for kind: :regular commits
2. Implement current_namespace(commit) helper (snapshot->commit.id, genesis->commit.id, else->metadata.snapshot_parent)
3. Tighten validator: flip bootstrap accept to reject malformed (post-umbrella). Preserve legacy %{} hatch.
4. Handle test-hash avalanche (analog to CX-m3x ~73 cascade).

Required tests:
- Auto-stamp happy path
- Snapshot-rooted doc
- Caller override
- Validator tightening (regular sans snapshot_parent rejected)
- Legacy pre-umbrella (%{} metadata still accepted)
close_reason: Shipped as commit e6f2608. Auto-stamp snapshot_parent on :regular commits via Namespace.current_namespace/1 helper (snapshot->commit.id, genesis->commit.id, regular/merge->inherited, legacy->nil). Validator tightened to reject :regular commits without snapshot_parent (:missing_snapshot_parent). Legacy %{} hatch preserved. 14 new tests all green; full commonplace (841) + yelixer (325) suites green. Cascade was zero since production code doesn't yet produce :regular commits — existing namespace tests already supplied snapshot_parent explicitly.

title: CX-ch5: Yelixer namespace primitive + validator swap (umbrella build 3)
description:
Deliver the real namespace-membership predicate and swap the CX-bv3
pass-through stub with it.

## Scope

1. Primitive in Yelixer (or Commonplace, whichever owns the namespace
   concept): `clientID_in_namespace?/3` or equivalent API. Answers:
   "does this clientID belong to the namespace rooted at this
   snapshot/genesis id?"

2. Replace CommitStore.default_namespace_validator/1 (currently a
   pass-through stub) with the real predicate. Regular commits whose
   update ops reference clientIDs outside the declared snapshot_parent's
   namespace get rejected with {:error, {:namespace_rejected, reason}}.

3. Namespace membership is "clientIDs observed in the namespace's
   commit chain" — walk from snapshot_parent back to the namespace
   root, aggregate state vectors of every regular commit plus the
   snapshot's own.

## Validator rules

- Legacy (metadata == %{}): accept (pre-umbrella hatch).
- kind: :genesis: accept (genesis is its own trust root).
- kind: :snapshot: accept (snapshot is a trust root).
- kind: :regular without :snapshot_parent: accept (current tests use
  this shape — regular-commit wiring with snapshot_parent is a later
  bead).
- kind: :regular with :snapshot_parent: validate clientIDs.

Bootstrap: the first regular commit after genesis introduces its own
clientID. Validator must accept this — namespace(genesis) == {} and
the new clientID is first-seen.

## Deliverables

- Predicate API + docs
- Validator swap
- Red event on rejection: commit_rejected_namespace_mismatch
- Tests: happy path, bootstrap, mismatch, validator-swap, legacy

## Dependencies

- Blocks: CX-bgy (umbrella)
- Blocked by: CX-m3x (wiring), CX-bv3 (hook), CX-fzi (genesis primitive) — all landed

## Open questions already resolved

- State-vector aggregation: on-demand walk for MVP (durable index
  deferred as optimization if perf demands it).
- Genesis namespace: empty — first regular commit bootstraps.

## Source

commonplace-plan directive, clod-squad #2171.

title: Snapshot op with derivation map + deterministic-anyone hashing (build 5)
description:
Replace current Yelixer.Doc.snapshot_update/1 with a namespace-establishing snapshot primitive that records a derivation map. This is the payoff build — makes late-edit translation (build 6) and cross-epoch merge (build 7) possible.

## Scope

### Yelixer work

#### Yelixer.Doc.snapshot_update/1 rewrite

Signature:
```
snapshot_update(source_doc) :: {update_bytes, derivation_map}
```

Behavior:
- Re-author source's observable state under a fresh peer (new u64 clientID, starting clock 0).
- Walk source items in **deterministic order** (fixed by type name alphabetically; within a type, by source item id ascending).
- For each source item, emit the corresponding new op into the fresh namespace, recording the mapping (new_item_id → old_item_id).
- Return the encoded update bytes + the derivation_map: `%{source_snapshot_hash => %{new_item_id => old_item_id}}`. Source hash is provided by the caller at the CommitStore layer.

Determinism requirements (load-bearing — CX-bv3's hash binds derivation_map into snapshot.id, so non-determinism → silent divergence):
- Fixed iteration order over types (alphabetical by name).
- Fixed iteration within types (ascending source item id).
- Deterministic derivation-map serialization (Erlang :deterministic term_to_binary handles this automatically via canonical_metadata, but map-build insertion order must be reproducible).
- Deterministic Yelixer encoder: encode_update/1 must produce byte-identical output given equal input ops. Fixed op ordering, deterministic varint/structural encoding, no wall-clock or randomness in the encoder.

#### Yelixer.Doc encoder determinism audit

Follow-up/verification: apps/yelixer/lib/yelixer/encoding.ex (encode_update/1). If non-deterministic paths exist, fix them here. Required for:
- Snapshot dedup (concurrent snapshotters collapse)
- Byte-determinism of late-edit translation (CX-6 scope, but prerequisite is this encoder property)

### CommitStore work

- CommitStore.create_snapshot_commit updated to:
  - Take source doc + source commit hash
  - Invoke Yelixer.Doc.snapshot_update/1
  - Build metadata = %{kind: :snapshot, snapshot_parents: [source.snapshot_parent], derivation_map: <map>}
  - Hash includes derivation_map via canonical_metadata (automatic given CX-bv3).
  - Write the snapshot commit.
- DocBuilder.reconstruct_doc / reconstruct_snapshot short-circuit at snapshot commits (existing behavior from CX-u7p — no change needed).

### CLI / trigger

- Per Q7 MVP: explicit trigger only. Add a minimal CommandRouter verb `commonplace snapshot <doc-uuid>` or equivalent that invokes create_snapshot_commit on the current doc state.
- No automatic Reaper-driven cadence in this bead.

### Migration

- Existing CX-u7p snapshots (presence docs) keep their current form. Pre-epoch legacy per docs/namespace-model.md § Migration.
- Post-umbrella snapshots carry derivation maps; pre-umbrella ones don't. Read path tolerates both.

## Out of scope

- Late-edit translation pipeline (build 6 — deferred).
- Cross-epoch merge / merge-snapshots (build 7 — deferred).
- Derivation-map side-table storage (inline per Q3; revisit after real data).
- Automatic snapshot cadence (Q7 explicit-only).
- Straggler horizon (Q9 deferred).

## Acceptance criteria

- snapshot_update produces byte-identical (update, derivation_map) from identical (source_doc, source_hash) on different BEAM instances.
- Snapshot commit id is deterministic: two peers compacting the same parent produce the same commit id (CID dedup works).
- derivation_map entry for each item in source maps correctly to the corresponding new item in the snapshot.
- DocBuilder.reconstruct_doc on the new snapshot produces the same observable state as the source (lossless re-authoring).
- XML content survives snapshot (regression test for CX-b2y's shipped fix).
- No automatic cadence: Reaper doesn't fire new-style snapshots without explicit trigger.

## Dependencies

- CX-bgy umbrella
- Blocked by CX-bv3 (metadata carries derivation_map, kind: :snapshot, snapshot_parents)
- Blocked by CX-fzi (snapshot_parents references genesis at the chain root)
- Blocked by CX-ch5 (Yelixer namespace boundary — snapshot establishes a new namespace that Commonplace must recognize)

## Design refs

- /home/jes/commonplace-plan/docs/merkle-tracked-yjs.md § Snapshot Semantics + § Derivation map + § Deterministic snapshots
- /home/jes/commonplace-plan/docs/late-edits-and-derivation-map.md § The Derivation Map + § Storage
- /home/jes/commonplace-plan/docs/snapshot-compaction.md (deterministic snapshotting, CID dedup)
- CX-u7p closure notes (current snapshot_update/1 behavior — baseline to replace)

Snapshotter.build/1 dropped to a thin wrapper (client_id determinization + snapshot_update call). All callers migrated (10 sites). Acceptance criteria met: byte-determinism across BEAM instances (new apps/yelixer/test/yelixer/snapshot_update_dm_test.exs + preserved snapshot_determinism_test.exs property test), snapshot commit id deterministic (Snapshotter metadata/write path unchanged), DM position-pair semantics identical to pre-refactor, XML round-trip preserved, no automatic cadence. title: Yelixer namespace boundary (envelope-carried) (build 3)
description:
Make Commonplace namespace-aware at the commit layer without changing Yjs wire format. Namespace is carried in commit envelope metadata (per jes's Q1 decision 2026-04-18); Yjs update bytes use plain u64 clientIDs unchanged.

## Scope

### Commonplace.Document.Server

- Track current namespace (snapshot_parent hash) as part of doc GenServer state.
- Advance current_namespace when:
  - A snapshot commit is received (advance to the snapshot's own hash — that IS the new namespace).
  - A commit is received whose snapshot_parent differs from current_namespace (i.e., we joined a different epoch).
- Expose current_namespace to the commit-creation path so CX-bv3's regular-commit writer can stamp metadata.snapshot_parent = current_namespace.

### CommitStore.import_commit validation

- On remote commit import, compare declared snapshot_parent against the namespace of ops' clientIDs.
- Uses Yelixer-side API `Yelixer.Doc.clientID_in_namespace?/3` (see Yelixer work below).
- Rejects with structured error on mismatch.

### Yelixer API addition

- `Yelixer.Doc.clientID_in_namespace?(doc, client_id, namespace_hash)` — checks whether a clientID was authored under the given namespace. Implementation: Yelixer tracks "which namespace introduced each clientID" at the Doc level (this is new state), populated when processing incoming commits that declare their namespace.
- No wire-format change to Yjs updates themselves. Namespace is a layer above.
- State vector representation at the Commonplace application layer becomes `(namespace, clientID) → clock`; Yjs internal state vector stays plain clientID-keyed.

### Sync path

- Phoenix PubSub commit broadcasts must carry snapshot_parent in the commit envelope (already handled by CX-bv3 metadata extension — verify end-to-end replication preserves it).

## Out of scope

- Yelixer internal refactor to prefix clientIDs (explicitly rejected — envelope approach).
- Snapshot op + derivation map construction (CX-e).

## Acceptance criteria

- New commits stamp metadata.snapshot_parent = current namespace.
- import_commit rejects a commit whose declared snapshot_parent disagrees with ops' namespace.
- Two-node replication test: commit created on node A with namespace N1, node B imports and sees matching namespace in its current_namespace tracker.
- No regressions in existing Document.Server or sync tests.

## Dependencies

- CX-bgy umbrella
- Blocked by CX-bv3 (needs snapshot_parent in the commit struct)
- Blocked by CX-fzi (needs genesis as the initial namespace)

## Design refs

- /home/jes/commonplace-plan/docs/namespace-model.md § Identification: Envelope, Not Prefix + § Consequences of envelope approach
- /home/jes/commonplace-plan/docs/merkle-tracked-yjs.md § Late Edits (references the namespace boundary this enforces)

Document.Server.:commit now tags writes as :kind :regular so CommitStore's CX-bv3 autostamp fires. Yelixer Doc-level clientID_in_namespace?/3 cache deferred to follow-up CX-4l7u — existing commit-walk validator (CX-bv3 + CX-fbs6) meets the rejection criteria; Doc-state cache becomes meaningful when CX-umz snapshot ops land. title: Stamp deterministic genesis snapshot at doc creation (build 2)
description:
Every new document creation stamps a synthetic genesis commit so namespace is never undefined. Write-side only per commonplace-plan confirmation 2026-04-18: existing docs retain pre-umbrella legacy shape (read-side interpretation only, no data rewrite).

## Scope

### Doc creation path

- On new document creation (Commonplace.Document.Server / commonplace CLI init / fork path), the first commit is a deterministic genesis:
  - parent_id = nil
  - update = <<>> (empty Yjs update)
  - metadata = %{kind: :genesis, doc_uuid: <uuid>}
  - hash = sha256(<<>> || <<>> || canonical_metadata(metadata))

Two peers independently creating "the same" document (same UUID) derive identical genesis ids — no coordination required.

### First user commit

- First real user commit on a new doc has:
  - parent_id = genesis.id
  - metadata.snapshot_parent = genesis.id
  - metadata.kind = :regular

### Read path (existing docs)

- Pre-umbrella commits keep metadata = %{} and their original hashes.
- DocBuilder.reconstruct_doc treats legacy commits as implicit-genesis-namespace per docs/namespace-model.md § Migration.
- No backfill pass. No migration of existing commits. Read-side interpretation only.

## Out of scope

- Any retroactive genesis for existing docs (explicitly declined — reopens identity questions).
- Yelixer namespace-tracking APIs (CX-c).
- Snapshot op (CX-e).

## Acceptance criteria

- New docs created via Document.Server + CLI stamp a genesis before any user commit.
- Genesis hash is deterministic from doc_uuid — test: two Doc.new(uuid) calls on different BEAM instances produce identical genesis.id.
- First user commit has parent_id = genesis.id and metadata.snapshot_parent = genesis.id.
- Existing docs load without modification; pre-umbrella commits keep their ids.

## Dependencies

- CX-bgy umbrella
- Blocked by the commit-struct + metadata-kind-enforcement bead (CX-a+d).

## Design refs

- /home/jes/commonplace-plan/docs/namespace-model.md § Genesis + § Migration: Pre-Epoch Legacy
- /home/jes/commonplace-plan/docs/merkle-tracked-yjs.md § Commit Structure (Genesis row)

title: Commit struct gains structural metadata; regular-commit-path validates namespace (build 1+3)
description:
Fold of CX-a + CX-d per commonplace-plan's recommendation: the commit struct change and the regular-commit-path validation touch the same module and are meaningless apart.

## Scope

Extend Commonplace.Store.Commit (apps/commonplace/lib/commonplace/store/commit.ex) with the fields required by the Merkle-tracked Yjs namespace model, and enforce namespace invariants on write + receive.

### Struct additions

- `merge_parents: [hash]` — additive, defaults to empty. `parent_id` stays as the primary-chain anchor; multi-parent merges live in `merge_parents`. (Multi-parent merge commits themselves are deferred to build 7.)

### Metadata-map shape (load-bearing)

Post-umbrella commits MUST carry an explicit `:kind` in metadata. Pre-umbrella legacy commits (`metadata = %{}`) keep their hashes (canonical_metadata(%{}) = <<>> reproduces the pre-CX-u7p formula).

- Regular: `%{kind: :regular, snapshot_parent: hash}`
- Snapshot: `%{kind: :snapshot, snapshot_parents: [hash, ...], derivation_map: map}` (filled in CX-e)
- Merge: `%{kind: :merge, snapshot_parent: hash}` (multi-parent deferred to build 7)
- Genesis: `%{kind: :genesis, doc_uuid: <uuid>}` (stamped in CX-b)

### Hash formula (no change)

Already established at store/commit.ex:71 by CX-u7p r2:
```
commit.id = sha256((parent_id || <<>>) || update || canonical_metadata(metadata))
canonical_metadata(%{}) = <<>>
canonical_metadata(m)   = :erlang.term_to_binary(m, [:deterministic])
```
Backward-compatible: all metadata-map additions (snapshot_parent, derivation_map) are folded into the hash via canonical_metadata without a formula change.

### Write path

- CommitStore.create_chained_commit / create_snapshot_commit: stamp metadata with explicit `:kind` and (for regular commits) `snapshot_parent = current_namespace`.
- current_namespace tracking lives in Commonplace.Document.Server (CX-c).
- Enforce: new commits without explicit `:kind` are rejected at create time.

### Receive path

- CommitStore.import_commit: validate declared `snapshot_parent` matches the namespace of ops' clientIDs. Validation helper is provided by Yelixer (CX-c exposes `clientID_in_namespace?/2`).
- Mismatched commits rejected with structured error.

## Out of scope

- Genesis stamping logic (CX-b)
- Yelixer namespace-check API (CX-c)
- Snapshot op + derivation map construction (CX-e)

## Acceptance criteria

- Existing historical commits with `metadata = %{}` retain their content addresses (regression fixtures pass).
- New regular commits fail creation without explicit `:kind`.
- import_commit rejects a commit whose declared snapshot_parent disagrees with ops' namespace.
- All existing tests pass (no regressions in CommitStore / DocBuilder / Merge).

## Design refs

- /home/jes/commonplace-plan/docs/namespace-model.md § Commit Shape + § Hash formula
- /home/jes/commonplace-plan/docs/merkle-tracked-yjs.md § Commit Structure

title: Merkle-tracked Yjs: namespace epochs + derivation maps (umbrella, builds 1-5)
description:
Umbrella for the Merkle-tracked Yjs model per jes's 2026-04-18 spec. Every commit lives in a namespace established by a snapshot; snapshots re-author observable state in a fresh Yjs ID space and carry a derivation map so late edits can translate byte-identically across namespace boundaries.

## MVP scope (this umbrella)

Builds 1-5 per docs/merkle-tracked-yjs.md:
- Commit struct with structural metadata + regular-commit path validation (CX-a+d combined)
- Deterministic genesis at doc creation (CX-b)
- ClientID namespacing — envelope-carried (CX-c)
- Snapshot op with derivation map + deterministic hash (CX-e)

## Out of scope (deferred)

- Build 6: late-edit rebase pipeline (primary derivation-map path + fallback to CX-6a7 positional rebase)
- Build 7: cross-epoch merges (commutation through inverse derivation maps)
- Merge-snapshots (snapshot_parents list ≥ 2)

## Design decisions (confirmed by jes)

- **Wire format: envelope.** Yjs update bytes use plain u64 clientIDs unchanged; namespace carried in commit metadata. Yelixer remains Yjs-wire-compatible.
- **Snapshot authority: deterministic-anyone.** Hash formula H(parent || update || canonical_metadata); snapshotter identity NOT in hash. Concurrent snapshots from same parent collapse by CID dedup.
- **CX-6a7 positional rebase retained** as fallback when derivation map is absent or incomplete (pre-epoch legacy snapshots, tombstone-boundary edge cases).

## Design docs

Located in commonplace-plan repo at commit 7dd6c6b or later:
- /home/jes/commonplace-plan/docs/merkle-tracked-yjs.md (top-level spec)
- /home/jes/commonplace-plan/docs/namespace-model.md (commit shape, hash formula, genesis, legacy)
- /home/jes/commonplace-plan/docs/late-edits-and-derivation-map.md (derivation map structure, translation algorithm, fallback)
- /home/jes/commonplace-plan/docs/snapshot-compaction.md (deterministic snapshotting, CID dedup)
- /home/jes/commonplace-plan/docs/positional-rebase.md (fallback mechanism, CX-6a7 shipped)

## Predecessors

- CX-u7p (capped, in-memory Yjs-ID rebase attempt — superseded)
- CX-6a7 (positional rebase shipped 2026-04-17; retained as fallback role)
- CX-e31 (snapshot-parents second Merkle tree — subsumed by this umbrella)
- CX-6y9 (snapshot_update XML content gap — fixed via CX-b2y, now part of Yelixer baseline)

title: Yelixer: XML delete_child + snapshot_update XML replay (unblock Phase 2 CX-9fy)
description:
Prerequisite for Commonplace CX-9fy (positional-rebase Phase 2, YXml).
Two gaps in Yelixer's XML support block CX-9fy from shipping:

## Gap 1: No delete_child primitive

`apps/yelixer/lib/yelixer/types/xml_fragment.ex` and
`apps/yelixer/lib/yelixer/types/xml_element.ex` expose `insert_child`
but no `delete_child`. Tree-path rebase needs "delete child at
path X" to replay structural deletions. Missing at every layer —
not just the public API.

**Add:**
- `XMLFragment.delete_child(doc, type_name, index, length \\ 1)`
- `XMLElement.delete_child(doc, type_name, index, length \\ 1)`

Pattern: mirror `Yelixer.Types.Array.delete/4`. The children sequence
is integrated via YATA (same as Array), keyed under
`#{type_name}::children`. Walk the sequence, mark items deleted, update
DeleteSet, return updated doc. Tombstones stay; child type registrations
stay (they're idempotent and re-used on future inserts with the same
id).

## Gap 2: snapshot_update doesn't replay XML content

`apps/yelixer/lib/yelixer/doc.ex:101-109` — XML types fall into the
catch-all branch that registers the name but skips content replay:

```elixir
_ ->
  {doc, _} = get_or_create_type(doc, name, effective_ref)
  doc
```

Comment says "XML support is currently a stub in commonplace; revisit
when it lands." Now landing (CX-9fy).

**Add:** `replay_xml_fragment/3`, `replay_xml_element/3`,
`replay_xml_text/3` that walk the source doc's XML tree and replay
structure + attributes + text content into the fresh doc. Pattern after
`replay_text` / `replay_map` / `replay_array`.

Also extend `infer_type_from_sequence/2` if needed so apply_update
correctly materializes XML top-level types (check — may already work
since XML items carry their own type_ref in `{:type, type_ref}`
content).

## Tests

- XMLFragment.delete_child removes children at index, respects length
- XMLElement.delete_child same
- Round-trip: create XML doc, snapshot_update, apply to fresh doc,
  verify to_string output is identical
- Round-trip with nested elements, attributes, text leaves
- Round-trip with deleted children (tombstones) — snapshot should drop
  the tombstones, observable shape preserved

## Out of scope

- Tree-path diff algorithm (lives in Commonplace Rebase.YXml)
- ContentType envelope `:xml` materializer (Commonplace side)
- content_type_ref(:xml) routing (Commonplace side; separate gap —
  currently points to `:xml` atom which isn't a valid XML type ref,
  should be `:xml_fragment`)

## Done when

- delete_child functions ship with tests
- snapshot_update XML replay works, round-trip tests pass
- CX-9fy unblocked: can compute tree-path diffs and apply them
close_reason: Shipped via worktree merge 4d8257f. XMLFragment/XMLElement.delete_child added; snapshot_update replays XML (fragment/element/text with attributes, tombstones dropped); wire format now carries XmlElement tag. 16 new tests, 0 regressions.

title: Positional-rebase phase 1: YText rebase + dispatcher scaffold + Document.Server integration
description:
Phase 1 of CX-6a7. Highest value + simplest implementation. Shippable on its own.

Per RFC (docs/positional-rebase.md §Per-Type Coordinate Systems / §Implementation Phasing):

Scope:
  * YText rebase primitive (~50 LOC): Myers diff over old_doc' and old_doc strings → sequence of {:insert, pos, text} / {:delete, pos, len} ops in char coordinates; replay as YText.insert/delete on new_doc.
  * Rebase dispatcher scaffold (~100 of the 200 dispatcher LOC): module that routes (old_doc, old_doc', new_doc, type) to the per-type rebase impl. Phase 1 only wires YText; stub/raise for other types until their phase lands.
  * Document.Server integration: transparent in handle_info({:remote_commit, snapshot}, state) — reset with snapshot, then rebase dirty ops. Telemetry via :telemetry.execute with snapshot_rebased(ops_count, dropped_count) red event.
  * Per-type property test: apply(old, edit) ∘ rebase(edit, new) ≡ apply(new, rebased_edit) in native shape.
  * Hand-crafted scenarios: typed-while-snapshot-arrived, concurrent-inserts-at-same-position tiebreak, rebase-absorbed (effect already present in new_doc).

Acceptance criteria:
  * YText dirty edits preserved across remote snapshot arrival
  * Property test passes for random (old_doc, dirty_edit, snapshot_update(old_doc)) triples
  * Non-YText docs: rebase raises a clear error (to be replaced by real impls in phases 2-4), no silent fallback to data loss
  * Regression: the capped CX-u7p test "snapshot-reset drops dirty edits" is inverted — dirty YText edits MUST now be preserved

Dependencies: CX-u7p landed (snapshot primitive). RFC requires design review pass before coding starts.

Out of scope: non-YText types (separate phase beads); YArray identity function registration (phase 4 concern); causally-stable barrier optimization (separate design).

Unblocks: CX-3ty follow-on (presence compaction can run without losing dirty presence writes).

A fresh-context agent opening this bead should read that file first; it defines the positional-rebase vocabulary (named mechanisms, per-type coordinate systems, tradeoffs, open questions) that this bead's scope references. close_reason: Phase 1 shipped: YText positional rebase + dispatcher + Document.Server integration. 353 tests pass. Umbrella CX-6a7 stays open for phases 2-4.

title: Positional-rebase dirty-edit preservation across snapshot boundaries (umbrella)
description:
Implement the observation-based positional-rebase design from commonplace-plan's RFC at /home/jes/commonplace-plan/docs/positional-rebase.md.

Problem: when a Document.Server holds uncommitted local edits and a remote snapshot arrives (via PubSub), `Yelixer.Doc.snapshot_update/1` rewrites every Yjs item ID under a fresh client clock. The dirty ops reference pre-snapshot IDs as their left-neighbors; those IDs no longer exist in the new doc, so Yjs holds them in a pending buffer waiting for IDs that will never arrive, silently dropping the edits.

Capped predecessor: CX-u7p shipped the snapshot primitive + reset-on-receive semantics (landed in main at 6bba291). The in-memory ID-rebase optimization was attempted across codex rounds r2-r6 and reverted at round 7 after four consecutive P1 structural findings — the approach is fundamentally misaligned with ID-rewriting snapshots.

Chosen approach (positional rebase): don't try to preserve Yjs IDs. Re-author dirty edits as fresh writes in the new doc using native-shape coordinates (char position, integer index, key, tree path). Algorithm:
  1. Apply dirty edit to old_doc → old_doc'
  2. Materialize old_doc and old_doc' in native shape
  3. Diff the shapes → high-level ops in native coordinates
  4. Replay ops against new_doc as fresh writes

The insight: `snapshot_update` preserves observable structure (positions/indices/keys/tree paths) even though IDs change. A dirty edit expressed in native coordinates passes through the snapshot boundary cleanly.

Phasing (per RFC, ordered by value × simplicity):
  1. YText rebase (~50 LOC) — highest value, covers most commonplace docs
  2. YXmlFragment rebase (~250 LOC) — views and structured docs
  3. YMap rebase (~80 LOC) — structured views and presence state blocks
  4. YArray rebase (~150 LOC) — lowest priority, most footguns (identity function)
  + Dispatcher + Document.Server integration + test matrix (~200 LOC)

Total: 500-700 LOC, ~1 week focused work per jes.

Acceptance criteria (umbrella-level):
  * Dirty edits are preserved across snapshot boundaries for all supported Y-types
  * Native-coordinate diff-and-replay implemented per-type
  * Rebase dispatcher routes correctly and handles nested Y-type recursion
  * Transparent integration in Document.Server handle_info on remote snapshot
  * Property-based tests per type + hand-crafted cross-type scenarios
  * All-or-nothing rebase failure semantics (no silent partial data loss)
  * Telemetry: red events for snapshot_rebased/rebase_absorbed

Open questions (tracked in RFC §Open Questions):
  - Identity function for YArray items: per-doc schema annotation (leaning) vs per-field vs global registry
  - All-or-nothing vs per-edit rebase on ambiguity (leaning: all-or-nothing, fail loud)
  - API shape: transparent in handle_info (leaning) vs explicit apply_remote_snapshot(..., rebase: true)

Phase 1 (YText) alone is shippable and unblocks CX-3ty's follow-on. Subsequent phases add incrementally.

Not a hotfix chain. This gets a real design pass, RFC review, and phased implementation — explicitly NOT the round-by-round codex pattern that capped CX-u7p.
notes: RFC location (cross-repo): /home/jes/commonplace-plan/docs/positional-rebase.md in the commonplace-plan repo — NOT in commonplace's docs/. A fresh-context agent opening this bead should read that file first; it defines the positional-rebase vocabulary (named mechanisms, per-type coordinate systems, tradeoffs, open questions) that this bead's scope references. Related: commonplace-plan's docs/snapshot-compaction.md defines the complementary sender-side snapshot semantics.
close_reason: All 4 phases shipped: CX-dqn (YText, 57affeb), CX-8nu (YMap, a489c53), CX-1cc (YArray, bad7ae3), CX-9fy (YXml, b82f2c7). Plus CX-bgq double-apply fix (2f72ba2), CX-b2y Yelixer XML prerequisites (4d8257f), and the :xml materializer (198cc84). Positional rebase now preserves dirty edits across remote snapshot boundaries for all four Y-types. 777 commonplace tests + 289 yelixer tests, all green. Open followups: CX-e31 (snapshot-parents second Merkle tree — architectural).

title: snapshot_update/1 discards XML-backed doc content
description: Codex round-3 finding on CX-u7p. Yelixer.Doc.snapshot_update/1 at apps/yelixer/lib/yelixer/doc.ex:101-107 re-registers non-text/map/array top-level types but does NOT copy their items. Snapshotting a doc with Yelixer.Types.XMLFragment produces an empty update. Once written via CommitStore.create_snapshot_commit and read via DocBuilder.reconstruct_doc (which now stops at snapshots), the pre-snapshot XML content becomes unreachable — data loss. Mitigating factor: XML-backed docs aren't currently the target of compaction (presence is YMap). Fix: extend snapshot_update/1 to copy XML fragment contents too. See codex review at /tmp/codex-CX-u7p-v3.txt.
close_reason: Superseded by CX-b2y (shipped in 4d8257f). snapshot_update/1 now replays XML content (fragment/element/text + attributes). Root cause at apps/yelixer/lib/yelixer/doc.ex:101-107 fixed — XML-backed docs now snapshot correctly.

title: Normalize string-keyed maps in Presence.set_attributes/3
description: In CX-4ba's new Presence.set_attributes/3 (apps/commonplace/lib/commonplace/presence.ex:215-224), the function pattern-matches atom keys (:owner, :cwd, :capabilities). When attributes arrive from params/JSON/RPC boundaries they're typically string-keyed (%{"owner" => ...}). Every entry falls through to the unknown-key clause, so set_attributes/3 silently writes an unchanged commit and none of the new metadata reaches the presence card. Fix: accept both atom and string keys (normalize). See codex review at /tmp/codex-CX-4ba-v2.txt.
close_reason: Normalized via small helper before the case statement; both atom-keyed and string-keyed attrs map to the same typed clauses. Test added covering the JSON / RPC string-keyed shape.

title: Resolve presence identity from stored content, not filename
description: In PresenceCard rendering (CX-4ba), wiki_live.ex:901-905 derives the presence name from `page_name` (the filename) for the `Identity.lookup/4` call. But `Presence.create/4` keeps the original actor name in the document even when the schema entry is collision-renamed (e.g. `claude-code-abc.bot`). In that case: (a) the card renders the suffixed filename as the actor's display name, and (b) Identity.lookup misses the cold identity registered under the unsuffixed name, so duplicate sessions never show identity metadata. Fix: load the presence doc first, read the `name` field from the stored content, use THAT for identity lookup. See codex review output at /tmp/codex-CX-4ba.txt and apps/commonplace_web/lib/commonplace_web_web/live/wiki_live.ex:901-905.
close_reason: Identity.lookup now derives the actor name from content[name] (the stored original) instead of the parsed filename, so collision-renamed presence files correctly resolve to the same cold identity as the original. Falls back to parsed filename for legacy docs without stored name. Test added covering two presence files for the same actor + one Identity record.

title: Include snapshot metadata in authenticated commit payload (content-address hash)
description: In the snapshot-append commit format (CX-u7p), metadata like `kind: :snapshot` is stored on the commit struct but EXCLUDED from `Commit.content_address/2`. This means: (a) a peer could retag an existing commit as a snapshot without changing its commit ID, and readers on DocBuilder.reconstruct_doc/2 would silently truncate history at that point; (b) when commit signing is enabled (ed25519), the snapshot marker is not covered by the signature. Fix: include metadata in content_address/2 so the marker is cryptographically bound. Callers will need a migration since existing commit IDs will change on first write — but for a not-yet-rolled-out snapshot primitive this is fine. See codex review output at /tmp/codex-CX-u7p.txt and apps/commonplace/lib/commonplace/store/commit.ex:8-13.
close_reason: Already fixed by CX-u7p r2 / CX-bv3. Commit.content_address (apps/commonplace/lib/commonplace/store/commit.ex:147-155) folds metadata via canonical_metadata/1 since the second round of CX-u7p, and Commit.verify_id is wired into CommitStore.import_commit as a gate. Test 'non-empty metadata changes the content address (CX-u7p r2)' at apps/commonplace/test/commonplace/store/commit_test.exs:70-76 directly covers the retag-as-snapshot scenario the bead described. Empty-metadata legacy commits keep their original hash via the canonical_metadata(%{}) → <<>> short-circuit (intentional backwards-compat hatch). When commit signing lands, the signature covers commit.id which now includes metadata.

title: Stabilize client_id for Sync.Watcher/RedLog writers (same bug class as CX-6g6)
description:
Found during CX-6g6 audit. Multiple modules call Yelixer.Doc.new() then apply_update + mutate + encode_update without passing client_id:. Each write mints a fresh random client_id that gets persisted into the state vector, same pathology that produced 14,360 clients on claude-code-2ca.bot (see CX-3ty).

Confirmed write-then-encode offenders (out of scope for CX-6g6, filed separately):
- apps/commonplace/lib/commonplace/sync/watcher.ex:215 (apply_modify: fresh Doc.new() every file modification — every .txt edit grows the state vector of that file's CRDT)
- apps/commonplace/lib/commonplace/sync/watcher.ex:187 (apply_create: fresh Doc.new() on create — single-shot, less bad, but still worth stabilizing)
- apps/commonplace/lib/commonplace/sync/watcher.ex:386 (needs re-check)
- apps/commonplace/lib/commonplace/sync/agent.ex:178, 193 (needs re-check)
- apps/commonplace/lib/commonplace/sync/entry_agent.ex:92, 147 (needs re-check)
- apps/commonplace/lib/commonplace/sync/dir_agent.ex:197 (needs re-check)
- apps/commonplace/lib/commonplace/sync/export.ex:61 (needs re-check)
- apps/commonplace/lib/commonplace/dataflow/red_log.ex:30 (load): every commit() call after load grows state vector
- apps/commonplace/lib/commonplace/green/bursar.ex:515, 553 (needs re-check)
- apps/commonplace/lib/commonplace/process/orchestrator.ex:393, 440, 577 (needs re-check)
- apps/commonplace/lib/commonplace/reflog/snapshot.ex:62 (needs re-check)

Fix pattern: same phash2-of-uuid stabilization used in CX-6g6 for Presence/Identity. Each caller should pass client_id: :erlang.phash2(doc_uuid, 0xFFFF_FFFF) to Yelixer.Doc.new/1 so all writers of a given doc share a stable client_id.

Acceptance: no writer in apps/commonplace/lib should call Yelixer.Doc.new() without an explicit client_id: unless the resulting doc is never persisted (read-only reconstruction for get_content, etc.). Add a test per fixed site like the CX-6g6 100-heartbeat test.
notes:
2026-04-19 partial-fix audit (Round 1).

FIXED in this pass:
- apps/commonplace/lib/commonplace/dataflow/red_log.ex: new/load → stable_client_id(uuid). Verified by 100-cycle state-vector test in test/commonplace/dataflow/red_log_test.exs (sv has exactly 1 client after 100 load→append→commit cycles).

KEY FINDING — two distinct writer patterns require different fixes:

PATTERN A (load + mutate, like Presence): load existing doc, mutate it,
encode_update, commit. Stable client_id alone fixes this — appended items
go under the stable client at incrementing clocks. RedLog matches this.
Sites that fit Pattern A:
- dataflow/red_log.ex (FIXED)

PATTERN B (replace whole doc): each write creates a fresh Doc.new(),
authors the entire content from scratch, encodes, commits. With stable
client_id this BREAKS — the second commit's items collide with the
first's at (stable_id, clock=0..N) and Yjs drops them as duplicates,
silently losing the new content. Demonstrated by a Watcher 100-modify
test: with stable client_id, content frozen at first commit's value
('v0' instead of 'v100').
Sites that fit Pattern B (need refactor to load+mutate, OR are
acceptable because reads use reconstruct_snapshot/latest-only):
- sync/watcher.ex apply_create (line 187), apply_modify (line 215)
- sync/agent.ex stale-write recovery (line 178)
- sync/entry_agent.ex sync_outbound (line 95)
- sync/dir_agent.ex create file (line 197)
- green/bursar.ex persist_state (line 515)
- reflog/snapshot.ex snapshot_dir reflog_doc (line 62)
- (probably) process/orchestrator.ex (lines 393, 440, 577) — not yet inspected

OFFENDERS OUT OF CX-pyi SCOPE (read-only, no encode_update):
- watcher.ex:386 (load_content), agent.ex:193 (extract_content),
  entry_agent.ex:171 (extract_content), export.ex:61 (load_content),
  bursar.ex:553 (initial create_state_doc — single-shot)

NEXT STEPS:
1. Pattern A sites (none remaining besides RedLog) — done.
2. Pattern B sites — file as a separate refactor bead. The fix is
   either: (a) restructure each write site to load existing state then
   apply incremental edits via the Yjs CRDT API, or (b) ensure these
   commits are tagged kind=:snapshot so DocBuilder.reconstruct_doc trims
   to them and accumulating bloat across the chain isn't an issue. (b)
   is a smaller change but only safe if every reader in the system uses
   trim-aware reconstruction.

Pattern B is bigger than CX-pyi as originally framed and probably
deserves its own design-driven cleanup pass.
close_reason: All in-scope writers refactored. RedLog (commit 604d3e2): load+mutate via stable client_id. sync/watcher, sync/entry_agent, sync/agent, sync/dir_agent, green/bursar persist_state (commit 9df5021): load+mutate via stable client_id + Document.Diff for text-content writers, stable id alone for one-shot creation paths. Watcher 100-modification test asserts SV stays at 1 client and content tracks the latest write. Sites SKIPPED with rationale: process/orchestrator.ex (3 sites — all read-only, no encode_update follows), reflog/snapshot.ex line 62 (only reader is reconstruct_snapshot, so chain bloat doesn't compound at read time; YMap-diffing for replace-pattern not justified).

title: Presence doc rendering: surface useful actor info on .bot/.usr/.exe/.who pages
description:
## Current state

Presence files (.bot/.usr/.exe/.who) are YMap CRDT documents created by `Commonplace.Presence.create/4` (apps/commonplace/lib/commonplace/presence.ex:50). The YMap has fields: `name`, `type`, `status`, `started_at`, `heartbeat`. A cold identity is also registered in `__identities__` with `first_seen`, `last_seen`, optional `public_keys` (apps/commonplace/lib/commonplace/presence/identity.ex).

When you browse to `/wiki/<name>.bot`, the WikiLive flow is:
- `load_page/2` calls `read_doc_content/1` (apps/commonplace_web/lib/commonplace_web_web/live/wiki_live.ex:733-738) which returns `ContentType.get_content(doc)`. For a `:map` content type that returns a plain Elixir map (apps/commonplace/lib/commonplace/document/content_type.ex:70-81 -> YMap.to_map).
- The page header at line 344-364 renders the filename (`name.bot`) and path. Edit/History buttons appear.
- The content branch at line 387-413: `ViewDetect.is_view?/1` returns false for a non-binary map (apps/commonplace/lib/commonplace/document/view_detect.ex:41), so the markdown branch runs. `render_wiki_content/2` only handles binary input (wiki_live.ex:533); the map falls through to `render_wiki_content(_, _), do: raw("")` at line 544.

**Net result: a `.bot` page renders just the filename header and an empty body.** No fields from the YMap reach HTML. Edit mode opens a Yjs editor on a map doc, which CodeMirror likely can't display meaningfully either.

## Gaps (what a user wants when looking at a bot)

- Identity: name, honorific, owner/who-launched-it, working dir / project
- Liveness: status badge, age of last heartbeat, uptime since started_at, green/yellow/red against the reaper's 30s stale threshold (apps/commonplace/lib/commonplace/presence/reaper.ex:16)
- Activity: current task, last action, recent commits authored by this signer
- Capabilities: tools/MCP servers, skills
- Cross-link to the cold identity in `__identities__` (first_seen, last_seen, public keys)

## Easy wins (already in YMap, just not surfaced)

- `name`, `type`, `status`, `started_at`, `heartbeat` — all present today
- `started_at` -> uptime; `heartbeat` -> "Xs ago" + liveness color via the reaper's `@default_stale_threshold` (30_000ms)

## New info needed (write paths don't exist yet)

- `current_task` / `activity` — bots would need to write this themselves (Presence.set_activity?). Server.ex (apps/commonplace/lib/commonplace/presence/server.ex) only writes status/heartbeat today.
- `owner` / launched-by — would need to thread through `Presence.create/4` and `Server.init/1`
- `cwd` / project — same; could pull from `System.cwd!()` at start
- `capabilities` / tools — bot-supplied
- `public_keys` are on the cold identity, not the hot presence — the page should cross-load and display them

## Cross-system opportunities

- **Identity** (presence/identity.ex): every hot presence has an `identity_uuid` (Server state); page should resolve cold-identity fields (`first_seen`, `last_seen`, `public_keys`) by name+type.
- **Signed commits** (commonplace/store/commit.ex:16, gold/attestation.ex, gold/chain.ex, crypto/signing.ex): commits have a `signer_id` field. The page can scan recent commits across the tree filtered by `signer_id == this actor's identity` to render an activity feed.
- **Reflog** (apps/commonplace/lib/commonplace/reflog/snapshot.ex): the `__reflog/<owner>/__snapshot` doc records tree-wide checkpoints per owner. If reflog "owner" maps to actor identity, a presence page could show the last N reflog snapshots for this owner and diffs.
- **Dataflow channels** (Commonplace.Dataflow.PubSub blue/magenta/red, used in wiki_live.ex:14): a presence page could subscribe to the actor's outbound channel for a live activity ticker (recent events from this signer).
- **Recent Changes** (wiki_live.ex:740-764) already walks the tree for commits — the same machinery, filtered by signer, gives a per-actor commit feed.
design:
## Detection + dispatch

In WikiLive.load_page/render, when the page name parses as a presence file (use `Presence.parse_honorific/1`), branch to a dedicated `render_presence_page` component instead of the markdown/view path. Don't change wiki rendering for non-presence docs.

## Layout

**Header strip** (top, always visible)
- Large name + honorific badge (.bot/.usr/.exe/.who) with a glyph
- Liveness pill: green if `now - heartbeat < 15s`, yellow `< 30s`, red `>= 30s` (mirror reaper threshold). Show "Xs ago" / "stale Xm ago".
- Status text from YMap `status`
- Uptime from `started_at` (humanized: "running 4m 13s")
- Owner / launched-by line (new field, ok to show "unknown" until populated)

**Identity panel** (right column)
- Cross-link to the cold identity: name+type -> Identity.lookup -> `first_seen`, `last_seen`, public keys (truncated, copy button)
- Working dir / project (new field)
- Capabilities list (new field, render as tag chips)

**Activity panel** (middle/left)
- "Current task" big text from a new `activity` field (empty state: "idle")
- Recent commits feed: scan tree commits, filter by `signer_id` matching this actor's identity. Reuse `collect_recent_changes/3` but key on signer instead of latest-per-doc. Show last ~20 with timestamp + path link.

**Reflog tail** (bottom, collapsible)
- If actor is a reflog owner, show last N `__reflog/<owner>/__snapshot` checkpoints with timestamp + short CID.

**Live updates**
- Subscribe via `CPPubSub.subscribe_blue(presence_uuid)` (already in load_page) so heartbeat/status writes refresh the page automatically.
- Also subscribe to the actor's signer feed (new helper) so the activity ticker updates without polling.

## Write paths that need to be added

1. `Commonplace.Presence.set_activity/3` (writes "activity" key on the YMap); call sites in actor harnesses (commonplaceclaude, MCP server) to push current task strings.
2. Extend `Presence.create/4` and `Presence.Server` opts to accept `owner`, `cwd`, `capabilities`; populate at start.
3. New helper `Commonplace.Store.CommitStoreClient.commits_by_signer/2` (or scan-and-filter) to feed the activity feed without re-walking the entire tree per render.
4. Optional: `Presence.Server` writes a per-actor signer-feed channel (red?) on every status/activity change so the LiveView can subscribe directly.

## Out of scope / follow-ups

- Editing presence docs in the Yjs editor (currently broken for maps) — disable the Edit button on presence pages or replace with a structured form.
- Linking presence -> tmux pane / process inspector.
- Per-actor permission/policy display once gold attestations land more broadly.
close_reason: Implemented in 529ce0a (worktree-agent-ab4eacc0). Adds PresenceCard function component with liveness pill (mirrors Reaper 30s threshold), activity/identity/owner/cwd/capabilities panels; wires WikiLive to detect .bot/.usr/.exe/.who via Presence.parse_honorific; adds Presence.set_activity/3 and Presence.set_attributes/3 (additive — no edits to create/heartbeat/update_status to avoid CX-6g6 collision). Per-signer commit feed deferred to follow-up. Tests: +9 presence, +6 presence_card render, all green.

title: Implement snapshot-append compaction primitive (CommitStore + Yelixer)
description:
Implement the (B) snapshot-append approach from docs/superpowers/specs/2026-04-16-presence-compaction-design.md. New primitives:

- CommitStore.create_snapshot_commit/4 (+ CommitStoreClient passthrough): writes a chained commit with metadata tagging it as a snapshot.
- Yelixer.Doc.snapshot_update/1: returns a self-contained update whose state vector contains a single client_id, encoding current materialized state.
- Commonplace.Presence.Compactor: given a presence UUID, rebuild + write snapshot commit. Idempotent.
- Wire into Commonplace.Presence.Reaper scan loop: when state_vector size > threshold (default 256), compact.
- Optional: teach DocBuilder.reconstruct_doc/2 to stop at the first commit with metadata.kind == :snapshot.

Tests: single-client state vector post-compaction, >100x apply_update speedup, two-node replication convergence, idempotency.

Dependencies: CX-6g6 (stable client_id) should land first so new bloat stops accumulating — otherwise compaction is chasing its tail.

Out of scope: content-addressed concurrent-snapshot dedup (file separately when general-doc compaction rollout happens); ephemeral-epoch presence subdoc (separate design doc).
close_reason: Implemented in commit 0b0303c on branch worktree-agent-a4811abe. Adds Yelixer.Doc.snapshot_update/1, CommitStore.create_snapshot_commit/4 (+ client pass-through), DocBuilder.reconstruct_doc/2 short-circuit on snapshot commits, and Commonplace.Presence.Compactor.{compact,state_vector_size}/2. Full test coverage (yelixer + commit_store + doc_builder + integration) — 1089 tests passing. Does not wire into Reaper; filed separately.

title: Snapshot/compaction pass for presence docs (Yelixer state vector reduction)
description: Presence docs accumulate one client_id per heartbeat-issuing node forever. claude-code-2ca.bot has 14,360 distinct clients in its state vector and a 398KB latest commit. apply_update is O(clients) — pages that load such docs take 30s. Even with the reaper wired up, surviving long-lived bots will still bloat. Need a compaction step: when a presence doc's state vector exceeds a threshold (or on a schedule), build a fresh Yelixer.Doc with current values and replace the chain. Open question: do we replace the chain (rewrite head with parent=nil) or append a 'snapshot' commit and have apply use it? Talk to commonplace-plan IRC bot before implementing — touches CRDT semantics. Could also generalise to all docs, not just presence.
design: probably need a new CommitStore.compact(uuid, snapshot_doc) primitive that writes a parent=nil commit and either prunes prior commits or marks them tombstoned. Yelixer compaction itself is just Doc.new() + Encoding.apply_update(latest_doc) which produces a fresh state vector with one client.
acceptance_criteria: compaction reduces a presence doc's apply_update time by >100x without losing observable content; design discussed in IRC #loom before merge
close_reason: Design doc at docs/superpowers/specs/2026-04-16-presence-compaction-design.md. IRC consensus (#loom 2026-04-16) on approach B (snapshot-append + reader short-circuit). Root cause is writer-side client_id instability — filed as CX-6g6 (P1, blocks compaction rollout). Compaction implementation filed as CX-u7p (P2, depends on CX-6g6).

title: Doc reconstruction cache: per-uuid, keyed on latest commit_id, invalidate on PubSub :commit
description: Currently every wiki page render rebuilds the Yelixer.Doc from scratch via DocBuilder.reconstruct_snapshot/2 — apply_update is the dominant cost (43ms for a normal bot, 28000ms for a 398KB-state-vector one). Add a cache (ETS or GenServer) keyed by {uuid, latest_commit_id} → %Yelixer.Doc{}, invalidated when CPPubSub broadcasts a :commit for that uuid. Repeat views of an unchanged doc become free. Note this is read-side caching — write path (CommitStore.create_chained_commit) already broadcasts via Dataflow.PubSub blue topic so invalidation hook is straightforward. Keep cache scoped to a single BEAM (no distributed cache yet). Should also benefit LiveView's double-mount (HTTP static + WebSocket) which currently does each reconstruct twice.
acceptance_criteria: second consecutive load of the same /wiki/<page> measurably skips apply_update; cache entry invalidated when a new commit lands on that uuid (verified by test)
close_reason: DocCache module (Commonplace.Tree.DocCache) — GenServer+ETS, {uuid, commit_id} keys, LRU bounded (max_size 256), invalidated by blue:UUID :commit broadcasts. WikiLive's two snapshot call sites migrated. Pass-through when unstarted. 10 tests added.

title: Commonplace.Document.TextMerge: shared text-diff CRDT merge utility
description:
Shared utility used by both MCP 'write' tool and SmartDoc 'push_cyan' rewrite to safely merge new text content into an existing YText without silently clobbering concurrent edits.

API:
  Commonplace.Document.TextMerge.merge_into(doc, target_text) -> {updated_doc, crdt_update_binary}
  Commonplace.Document.TextMerge.ops_for(current_text, target_text) -> [{:insert, offset, text} | {:delete, offset, length}]

Implementation: use String.myers_difference/2 to compute edit script, convert to YText insert/delete ops, apply to the passed Y.Doc.

Why: computed views (views.md section on View computation) explicitly depend on this being the write path for SmartDoc output, otherwise every recompute silently overwrites concurrent edits. MCP write has the same bug class. Doing it once avoids two near-identical implementations.

Not blocking the Views first pass (which ships static views only), but required before any computed-view work or before MCP write can claim correctness. File tracked here; implementation deferred to when it becomes critical path.
notes: Discovery: the utility already exists as Commonplace.Document.Diff at apps/commonplace/lib/commonplace/document/diff.ex. It implements Myers-diff on graphemes via List.myers_difference/2 and exposes diff/2 + apply_diff/3. Already wired into Commonplace.CommandRouter.write/3 (line 140) and used by the MCP write tool. Remaining scope for this ticket is NOT a new module — it's wiring Commonplace.SmartDoc.push_cyan/3 to use Diff.apply_diff instead of the current create-new-Yelixer.Doc-and-text-insert pattern. That's the phase-2 blocker for computed views per docs/views.md. commonplace-plan and I both missed this in the initial audit.
