title: Per-call signing context for CommitStore (fix MCP/CLI cross-contamination)
description:
PROBLEM: CommitStore.maybe_sign_commit/1 reads signing_key:default, signing_pub:default, signing_identity from a global SecretStore. If an MCP agent session loads an ephemeral keypair into those slots to sign its commits, any concurrent CLI commit from the human user will also sign with the agent's key. The audit log would claim the human's commits came from the agent — worse than unsigned.

DISCOVERED: During CX-rmk MVP scoping, decided to punt agent-commit signing for MCP MVP (agents commit with signer_id=nil until this is fixed).

FIX (option b from scoping): Extend CommitStore.create_commit / create_chained_commit to accept an optional signing_context parameter (identity_uuid + keypair ref). Thread it through all call sites including CommandRouter (CX-rmk). maybe_sign_commit becomes a function of the passed context instead of global SecretStore lookup. Legacy/default path still falls back to the global slots for backwards compat. Every writer has a well-defined identity, no cross-contamination.

NOT BLOCKING MCP MVP — agent commits ship unsigned until this lands.
design: Approach: add signing_opts keyword to CommitStore.create_commit and create_chained_commit. maybe_sign_commit inspects opts first, falls back to SecretStore. CommandRouter (CX-rmk) accepts signing_context in its state (set by MCP on init from session keypair, or by CLI from whatever the user configured) and threads it into every commit call. LiveView / sync / bursar writers that don't set a context fall through to the current default slot behavior.
close_reason: Shipped Commonplace.Crypto.SigningContext + opts threading on CommitStore.create_commit/6 and CommitStore.create_chained_commit/5. Per-call signing_context overrides the global SecretStore lookup; :unsigned sentinel skips signing entirely (MCP-MVP path); nil/absent falls through to legacy global behavior so every existing caller stays correct without changes. Backward-compat handle_call clauses preserve the original 4-tuple message shape. 3 new tests prove no cross-contamination between concurrent human/agent writes (each verifies only under its own key).

title: Layer 2 MCP server for commonplace channels
description:
Build an MCP server that makes an AI agent a participant in the commonplace document graph. Exposes the L2 channel surface (magenta commands, red event logs, blue docs) and CLI verbs as tools.

Per commonplace-plan design and boss-clod scope:

Tools:
- send_magenta(path, type, payload)
- append_red(path, event)
- subscribe_magenta(path_glob) / tail_red(path) as MCP notifications
- CLI verbs as tools: checkout, branch_create, fork, merge, commit, gc

Resources:
- Blue docs readable as structured data
- Red chains as event lists with provenance
- Agent's own identity doc + .bot presence file

MVP per boss-clod: send_magenta + tail_red + a handful of CLI verbs. Enough to make an agent a graph participant.
design: Smoke test (2026-04-09) found CommitStoreClient.set_remote_node uses Process.put — per-process. MCP main sets it, but Presence.Server is a NEW GenServer process whose dict is empty, so its CommitStoreClient calls fall through to :local and write to a phantom local CubDB instead of the serve node's. Schema on serve never sees the .bot file. Fix: switch set_remote_node/remote_node to :persistent_term so the routing is node-wide. Tests/CLI unaffected.
notes: Mechanicalness check (2026-04-09): fork/merge/gc are clean single-line drop-in replacements. branch activate/deactivate is 3-line wrap. checkout needs CheckoutRegistry to become a supervised singleton (currently started per-call). checkout 'reroot workspace' legacy path stays CLI-only (not a regular verb). branch_create doesn't exist today — needs scope clarification (mkdir+sync or fork+activate?). Signing flag: SecretStore signing_key:default is single-slot, auto-sign would race with concurrent CLI commits if MCP loads an ephemeral keypair. Options: punt+follow-up, OR extend CommitStore to accept per-call signing context via CommandRouter (leaning this — not expensive if we're already building the router). Awaiting response from boss-clod/plan on signing + branch_create semantics before coding.

title: Integrate flock advisory locks into SyncAgent write path

The Elixir FileLock module exists but is not wired into SyncAgent. Key pieces: wire flock into Export.atomic_write, add shared locks around reads in SyncAgent, coordinate with SandboxExecRunner processes. Reference: commonplace-rs/crates/commonplace-watcher/src/flock.rs and shadow.rs

title: Yelixer CRDT: full-chain replay gives inconsistent results for schema docs
description: When schema docs have multiple commits that each contain full-state snapshots (as fork creates), replaying the full commit chain via Enum.reduce(commits, {:ok, doc}, fn c, {:ok, d} -> Encoding.apply_update(d, c.update) end) gives inconsistent CRDT state. This is because YMap.to_map iterates store.clients in non-deterministic Erlang map order, and applying full snapshots on top of each other creates duplicate items with conflicting ordering. Workaround in merge.ex: reconstruct_snapshot/2 applies only the latest commit to a fresh doc, which works because fork always stores full snapshots. This is fragile — if any code path creates incremental schema commits, reconstruct_snapshot will lose earlier entries. Should investigate root cause in Yelixer's apply_update or document the constraint that schema commits must always be full snapshots.
close_reason: Root cause identified and fixed in CX-sew: YMap.to_map used non-deterministic Erlang map iteration. Now uses YATA sequence order.

title: Schema merge fallback when parent_id=nil breaks DAG ancestry
description: Writers (presence, cell, sync watcher) create commits with parent_id=nil which breaks commit chain ancestry. After such an edit, find_common_ancestor returns :none and merge skips that subtree. Need either: (a) fix writers to properly chain commits, or (b) add schema-level merge-point fallback in merge_tree for directory nodes. Discovered during CX-9zu codex review.

title: Track target fork-point separately for collision detection on repeated merges
description: After first merge, root entry's fork_point_commit is set to a source-chain commit for incremental schema diffing. But collision detection needs the target's fork-point to identify target additions since fork. On repeated merges, reconstruct_doc_at(target, source_commit) returns :none and falls back to current target, disabling collision detection. ForkManifest needs a separate target_fork_point_commit field.
close_reason: Resolved by CX-9zu — common ancestor is unambiguous in shared DAG

title: Recursive schema diff for nested directory merges
description: Current merge only diffs root schema entries. Structural changes inside subdirectories (adds/removes/renames in nested dirs) are excluded from content merge (correctly, to avoid node_id contamination) but also not captured by the schema diff. Need to recursively walk and diff subdirectory schemas. This requires extending the merge algorithm to recurse into dir-type entries.

title: Fork schema as edit in merkle tree, not new document
description: Currently fork creates brand-new documents with new UUIDs. Instead, a forked schema should be an edit (commit) in the existing merkle tree with metadata indicating it's a schema fork. This would simplify merge — the fork-point state vector would be directly available from the commit chain rather than needing to reconstruct from the source's oldest commit or target's fork-point. Would also make the provenance relationship explicit in the commit DAG itself rather than only in the ForkManifest sidecar.
design: See docs/superpowers/specs/2026-03-23-fork-as-dag-branch-design.md. UUID = branch name into shared commit DAG. Fork creates branch points + schema edit commits. Eliminates ForkManifest. Provenance embedded in DAG.

title: MCP server using commonplace docs for tool definitions
description: Run an MCP server backed by commonplace docs — tool and resource definitions stored as CRDT documents. From Rust CP-z7t. Would let commonplace act as an AI tool provider.
notes:
Design constraint from prior nodejs commonplace (jes, 2026-04-23): most MCP-capable agents don't dynamically reload the tool list at runtime. Design implications:
(1) First-class MCP tools defined from CRDT docs are fine, but calls to renamed/removed tools must fail gracefully (not crash the session).
(2) Need a dynamic escape hatch: e.g. call_tool(tool_name, params) so agents with stale tool lists can reach newly-created tools.
(3) Need runtime reflection: e.g. list_tools, describe_tool so agents can discover tools added after their session started.
These three constraints shape the interface surface, not the storage surface — the CRDT-backed tool-definition layer remains the same either way.
close_reason: Shipped. Two-doc pair (interface @ __system/tools/<name> + handler @ target_path). MCP server merges static system tools (cataloged + meta) with CRDT tools at runtime; system wins on collision. Magenta-orchestrating dispatcher with full template rendering, server-injected correlation_id (handlers can't forge), success_type/error_type discrimination, in-band MCP tool errors for timeout/missing-handler/missing-var. Late-bind via call_tool meta-tool with recursion guard, list_tools for runtime catalog reflection. 21 new tests. Suite 1648/0. title: Green channel: exclusive lock manager (bursar)

title: Fork with ForkManifest (deep-copy with new UUIDs)
description:
Deep-copy a directory subtree with new UUIDs, tracking fork provenance via a ForkManifest.

## ForkManifest
Stores the mapping from new UUID → {original_uuid, fork_point_commit} for every document in the forked subtree. Enables future diff/merge operations.

## Fork-safety for __processes.json
Each process entry has a fork behavior (explicit or inferred):
- copy: safe to duplicate (sandbox-exec → stateless, runs independently per fork)
- skip: must NOT be duplicated (command, log-listener → singletons)

When forking encounters a __processes.json, it must apply filter_for_fork to strip skip-marked entries before writing to the forked tree. Prevents accidentally spawning duplicate singleton processes.

Defaults: sandbox-exec → copy, command → skip. Explicit fork field in __processes.json overrides.

## Implementation
1. ForkManifest struct (map of new_uuid → ForkEntry)
2. Config.filter_for_fork/1 — strips skip entries from process configs  
3. fork_directory/2 — recursive deep-copy: walk schema, create new UUIDs, replay commits, filter __processes.json
4. CLI: commonplace fork <path> [--branch <name>]

## From commonplace-rs
Port of: crates/commonplace-types/src/fs/fork.rs, src/orchestrator/discovery.rs (ForkBehavior), src/bin/branch.rs (fork-safety filtering)
close_reason: Fork with ForkManifest: recursive deep-copy with new UUIDs, fork-safety filtering for __processes.json (sandbox-exec→copy, command→skip, explicit override). CLI: commonplace fork. Ported from commonplace-rs. 9 tests.

title: Trust hardening: always node-sign system-kind commits (robust zero-config strict)
description: Phase 2.5 ships maybe_sign_commit with global-SecretStore-key BEFORE the node-identity fallback. So a workspace with a global signing_key:default signs system commits (snapshot/merge) with the GLOBAL identity, which is NOT auto-trusted — meaning "zero-config single-node strict" is literally true only for node-key-only workspaces; a keygen'd workspace must pin its own identity (acceptable, since it needs that pin for user commits anyway). Cleaner/robust option: ALWAYS node-sign system-kind commits (metadata.kind ∈ {:snapshot,:merge}) regardless of the global key — decouples "system commits = node-accountable, zero-config" from "user commits = user-pinned," and gives system commits correct node attribution (a snapshot is a system action, not a human one). Small change (reorder/guard in maybe_sign_commit). Non-blocking robustness improvement.
design: Federation move-#1 Phase-A prereq, folds in with CX-tdkq.26. Reorder maybe_sign_commit (commit_store.ex ~1544-1549) so system kinds (:snapshot/:merge/translation) node-sign BEFORE the global-SecretStore-key fallback — else keygen'd workspaces mis-attribute snapshots to the human key and zero-config strict holds only for node-key-only workspaces.

title: Outliner follow-up: per-viewer collapse state
description: Refinement (epic CX-dqjs). Ref: docs/outliner.md §2,§6. MVP stores 'collapsed' as a SHARED attribute (everyone sees the same fold state). Move it to per-session/per-user state (a small overlay — per-user doc or session assigns) so my fold state doesn't change yours. The shared 'collapsed' attribute can remain as the default/seed.
design: Per-user view-state overlay rather than a substrate fact: collapse is a viewer preference, not a property of the bullet. Keep the shared attr as initial/default; layer per-session overrides on top in OutlineLive.
acceptance_criteria: Two users viewing the same outline can collapse/expand independently; reload preserves a user's own fold state; no cross-user interference.

title: Outliner follow-up: zoom into subtree
description: Workflowy-style zoom (epic CX-dqjs). Ref: docs/outliner.md §6. Render a chosen item id as the temporary ROOT: route /outline/:name/:id renders only that subtree, with breadcrumb back to ancestors. Mostly a render-root filter on MVP ii's reconstruction + OutlineLive routing — no data-model change, no mutation.
design: Pure presentation: pick a render root, filter the reconstructed tree to that node's descendants, show a breadcrumb. Reuses MVP ii unchanged.
acceptance_criteria: Clicking a bullet (or visiting /outline/:name/:id) zooms to that subtree as root; breadcrumb navigates back up; editing/keybinds still work within the zoomed view.

title: Outliner follow-up: node-id transclusion -> mirrors
description:
The one genuinely NET-NEW substrate piece for the outliner (epic CX-dqjs), with value beyond it. Ref: docs/outliner.md §7. Enables Workflowy-style MIRRORS: the same node shown live in multiple places.

VERIFIED BLOCKER: ViewTransclusion today targets only WHOLE documents (resolve_docref walks schema to a uuid, splices entire content; 'from' accepts path/uuid only; no fragment/#node-id/selector syntax exists anywhere — searched exhaustively).

FIX: extend ViewTransclusion so 'from' can carry a node-id suffix selecting an <item> (and its reconstructed subtree) within the target outline doc, e.g. <include from="outline/groceries#b7"/>. Resolution gains one step: if a #id suffix is present, reconstruct the subtree rooted at that id (same parent/order walk as MVP ii) instead of splicing the whole <view>. Extend cycle detection to (uuid, node-id) pairs.
design: This is why multidoc is strictly dominated: mirrors are needed anyway, and once node-id transclusion exists the single-doc model gets mirrors with no per-bullet-doc tax. Benefits any future block-reference use case (Roam/org transclusion), not just outliner. Bounded, additive extension to ViewTransclusion + the renderer.
acceptance_criteria: <include from="<outline>#<item-id>"/> renders the subtree rooted at that item; edits to the source item reflect live in the mirror; (uuid,node-id) cycle detection prevents infinite/self transclusion. Whole-doc include behavior unchanged. Tests for node-id resolve, subtree splice, cycle guard.

title: Outliner follow-up: full Kleppmann cycle-safe move
description:
Additive upgrade on the flat-bag model (epic CX-dqjs). Ref: docs/outliner.md §4. Replaces MVP ii's defensive orphan-to-root with academically-correct conflict-free tree move (Kleppmann, 'A highly-available move operation for replicated trees'): record each reparent as a move-OP; on merge, if a move would introduce a cycle, UNDO the move that loses the tiebreak.

Refines how 'parent' writes are APPLIED — it does NOT change how the tree is stored (still the flat <item> bag). No migration.
design: The flat-bag model was chosen precisely so this is additive: parent is already an LWW register; Kleppmann adds cycle-aware application + undo-on-conflict on top. MVP ships defensive orphan-to-root (no data loss) so this can land later without blocking the outliner.
acceptance_criteria: Concurrent X->Y & Y->X reparent converges to a single valid tree (one move undone) identically on all replicas, no orphans, no data loss. Property tests over random concurrent move sequences: result is always a valid forest equal on all replicas.

title: mix bots.tail live observability command
description:
Shell-friendly command to watch bot activity from the terminal. Polls or subscribes to the dispatcher's room state and prints decisions + worker outcomes as they arrive.

Suggested shape:

  mix bots.tail --room demo     # one room
  mix bots.tail --since 60      # last 60s + follow

Output format mirrors the proposed __bot_activity schema:
  [ts] room/bot decision [reason: …] [msg: …]

Implementation: connects to botdemo@localhost via :rpc.call (same pattern as bin/bot-demo-{post,read}), reads Activity.list for each room, plus attaches a telemetry handler on the serve node for :trigger_fired / :trigger_suppressed / :worker_finished. Streams updates via send + receive loop until Ctrl-C.

Depends on CX-gptu (worker outcomes in activity) to be fully useful.

description:
Alternative to the thin mud_send/mud_read approach. Package PlayerSession as a first-class MCP-session resource: spawning a session is the bot 'connecting'; the session is reachable by handle; input/output flow as session methods rather than ad-hoc top-level tools.

Cons: needs MCP session-shape tooling (handle lifecycle, reconnection, persistence-of-session-across-MCP-calls) which the thin approach skips. Roughly 3× the LoC of the thin version.

Defer until thin approach surfaces a real gap. Filed as the alternative we explicitly chose against.

title: [bug] call_tool meta-tool drops session context (presence_uuid lands as nil)
description:
meta_tools_test.exs:51 'passes context through to the inner tool' fails on main: structured['presence_uuid'] is nil instead of 'p'. Confirmed pre-existing on stashed-clean main (NOT caused by CX-487i V1+V2 chat work, surfaced during its full-suite run).

Likely regression from the CX-hf71 anubis port — somewhere along the call_tool meta-tool path, session context is being dropped before the inner tool's run/2 receives it.

Trace path:
- AnubisServer.handle_request tools/call → presence_context(frame) extracts {presence_uuid, mailbox_uuid, mailbox_topic} → Tools.call(name, args, ctx)
- For call_tool meta-tool: Tools.call('call_tool', %{name, args}, ctx) → CallTool.run(args, ctx) → Tools.call(name, inner_args, ctx)
- The inner Tools.call SHOULD pass ctx to dispatch_static, and dispatch_static SHOULD invoke run/2 if defined
- presence_info has run/2 defined and reads context[:presence_uuid]
- Test expects ctx to flow through both Tools.call layers and reach presence_info.run/2

Verification:
- Test passes when calling presence_info DIRECTLY via Tools.call (skipping the meta-tool)
- Test fails when going through call_tool meta-tool

Likely causes (in priority order):
1. CallTool.run/2 might be losing the context map between its argument unpacking and the inner Tools.call (verify args destructuring doesn't shadow)
2. Tools.call dispatch_static might fall through to run/1 when the tool DOES define run/2 but only as default-arg (run(args, context \ %{})) — function_exported?(mod, :run, 2) might return false for default-arg-only declarations in some Elixir versions

Doesn't currently block any production path (chat uses invoke_view_action directly, not call_tool). File while context is fresh; fix when someone touches that surface or it becomes load-bearing.
close_reason: Root cause: function_exported?/3 returns false on unloaded modules; dispatch_static fell through to run/1 on first call of a fresh VM, dropping context. Fix: Code.ensure_loaded? before the export check (one line). Order-dependent test reproduction now passes in isolation; full MCP suite 102/102 green. Shipped on main c31031e.

title: tail_red occasional 'Connection closed' transport wobble (per-tool, retry-succeeds)
description:
Workspace MCP smoke testing 2026-04-25 (clod-squad msg #2921, round 10) flagged: tail_red occasionally returns 'Connection closed' / -32000 transport error mid-session, but the SAME call succeeds on retry. Other tool calls within the same session continue to work. So this is NOT the session-wide 'Connection closed' that CX-y6uc fixed (where the whole MCP escript dies); this is a per-call wobble.

**Suspected cause:** tail_red's path is RedLog.load → CommitStoreClient.latest_commit → CommitStoreClient.get_commit. Under serve's still-elevated CPU load (CX-0nkq territory — snapshot + reflog + dispatch fanout), a single GenServer.call to CommitStore may hit the 5s timeout. The :exit propagates up; safe_tool_call (CX-0nkq c-shipped) catches it and returns an in-band error to the agent. But maybe the in-band error here is being mis-encoded as a transport error? Or anubis stdio framing has a hiccup under serve's spike?

**Fixes to consider** (in order of preference):
1. The proper fix is the SnapshotWorker single-flight tracked in CX-0nkq — once CommitStore mailbox isn't starved, individual GenServer.call timeouts disappear.
2. Tail_red could pre-flight commit_onramp on the live onramp pid (if locatable via Registry) to ensure freshness without blocking on long load.
3. Bump tail_red's CommitStore call timeouts above the default 5s — papers over but avoids transport churn.

**Status:** P3 because it's a wobble (retry succeeds), not a hard failure. The session stays alive and other tools work. Proper fix likely lands as part of CX-0nkq's SnapshotWorker.

Filed during workspace smoke round 10 (clod-squad msg #2921).
notes: Probably resolved when CX-0nkq's SnapshotWorker lands. Defer until then.

title: CLI: commonplace process remove <name>
description:
Add a CLI verb to remove a process registration from the workspace's __processes.json CRDT doc.

**Motivation:** During CX-0nkq diagnosis (2026-04-25 workspace MCP smoke test), the only way to remove a problematic process registration was a manual mix run script editing the doc directly. A CLI verb makes this a one-liner and avoids the standalone-script-vs-serve-dist-Erlang debugging trap (Application.put_env timing pitfall — see CX-0nkq notes).

**Surface:**
```
commonplace process remove <name>
commonplace process list                  # alias for ps?
commonplace process add <name> <args...>  # future, not v1
```

v1 scope: just . Walks __processes.json (root-level), Jason-decodes, removes the named key from the 'processes' map, re-encodes, writes a chained commit. Idempotent — removing a non-existent name is a no-op with a friendly message.

**Implementation sketch:**
- New file: apps/commonplace_cli/lib/commonplace/cli/process.ex
- Dispatch in cli.ex's case args
- Walk root → __processes.json schema entry → load doc → mutate JSON → write chained commit. Same shape as the script in clod-squad msg #2872.
- Test: setup with __processes.json containing two processes, run remove, verify only one remains.

**Out of scope for v1:**
- Subdir __processes.json files (orchestrator.ex's collect_processes_recursive walks all dirs; remove from where? add a --dir flag in v2)
- process add (write/edit the doc — plenty of YAGNI traps; agents can use the existing magenta send_magenta path or a future MCP tool)
- Live signal to running serve to re-reconcile (orchestrator polls every interval anyway)

Filed during CX-0nkq diagnosis (clod-squad #2872).
notes: Convenience CLI verb; not blocking anything. P3.
close_reason: Shipped on main 022ee65. Process.run returns exit codes; main() halts on non-zero so in-process tests work. 5/5 new tests + 62/62 CLI suite + 86/86 bots all green.

title: CX-y3q followup: progress notifications forwarding
description:
Per docs/dynamic-mcp-tools.md (Magenta Protocol → Progress section), CRDT-defined tools support progress notifications:

- Handler MAY emit zero or more 'progress' magenta on commands/<target_path>/<send_type>/progress with payload {progress, total?, message?, correlation_id}.
- Dispatcher reads request._meta.progressToken; if set, forwards each matching progress event as MCP notifications/progress with the captured token.
- Handler emits unconditionally; dispatcher silently discards if no progressToken.

**What's NOT implemented in CX-y3q v2.2**:
- Dispatcher does NOT subscribe to the /progress topic
- Request _meta.progressToken is not extracted in the Tools.call → CrdtTools.call → dispatcher path
- Anubis session notification API (send(session_pid, {:send_notification, ...})) is not wired

**Implementation sketch**:
1. Extend Commonplace.MCP.AnubisServer.handle_request for tools/call: extract _meta.progressToken from request, pass into context
2. Extend Commonplace.MCP.Tools.call/3 → CrdtTools.call/3 to accept progress_token + progress_callback opts (skeleton already there in CrdtTools.call — see docstring 'reserved for future progress forwarding')
3. CrdtTools.dispatch subscribes to /progress sub-topic alongside main reply topic
4. await_reply loop: matching progress message → invoke callback (or directly forward via Anubis session API); continue
5. Test: spawn handler, emit progress with correlation_id, verify MCP notifications/progress arrives at the session

Filed as followup to CX-y3q which closed without this. Doc reflects the intended design — code catches up here.
notes: P3 because the static system tools never use progress (none of cat/fork/etc. is long-running). Progress only matters for CRDT-defined tools that take >1s. Land when a real dynamic tool needs it.

title: CX-y3q followup: notifications/tools/list_changed watcher
description:
Per docs/dynamic-mcp-tools.md (Late Binding section), the MCP server should emit notifications/tools/list_changed when the CRDT-defined tool catalog changes (add/remove/edit interface docs under __system/tools/).

**Design** (from the doc, my redirect to plan-bot's draft):
- Dedicated singleton GenServer Commonplace.MCP.ToolsCatalogWatcher in the MCP supervision tree
- Subscribes once to PubSub on the __system/tools/ schema doc UUID
- Maintains a Registry of active session pids (sessions register on init/2)
- On commit + 100ms debounce timer, fans out notifications/tools/list_changed to every registered session via anubis's session notification API (send(session_pid, {:send_notification, method, params}))

**What's already in place** (CX-y3q v2.2):
- CrdtTools.list reads __system/tools/ on every tools/list call (no caching)
- The MCP catalog merges static + CRDT correctly
- Clients just see a stale list mid-session today

**Out of scope for this followup**:
- Catalog caching with PubSub-driven invalidation (separate concern)
- Anubis support for fanout to all sessions — needs verification; might require maintaining our own session registry inside ToolsCatalogWatcher

Filed as followup to CX-y3q which closed without this.
notes: P3 because tools/list at session-init still works for new sessions; this is for mid-session catalog reflection on clients that honor list_changed.

title: Orchestrator reconcile loop hits Schema.get_entry/2 FunctionClauseError on fresh workspace
description:
Even on a freshly-init'd workspace with no entries and no __processes.json, the running serve emits a tight loop of:

  Orchestrator reconcile failed: no function clause matching in Commonplace.Tree.Schema.get_entry/2

~4 occurrences per 12s tick. The error is caught + logged at apps/commonplace/lib/commonplace/process/orchestrator.ex:88-95 (the rescue site), so the system stays alive — reflog checkpoints succeed, CLI works, MCP tools work. Cosmetic / log-noise level today, but indicates a hidden invariant is broken.

**Repro context** (boss-clod, 2026-04-25 00:50 UTC):
- Workspace at /home/jes/commonplace/workspace was wiped + commonplace init'd fresh (root 6fd72a7f-0f4c-4e31-8d2f-3b27312ecf4a)
- /home/jes/commonplace/workspace/__processes.json moved out of cwd before re-init
- Serve restarted via mix run --no-halt -e 'Commonplace.CLI.main(["-d", "...", "serve"])' from /home/jes/commonplace
- Orchestrator's reconcile tick fires ~every 5s, errors immediately each time

**Diagnostic gap:** Logger.error at orchestrator.ex:94 prints only Exception.message/1 — no stacktrace. We don't know which Schema.get_entry caller is the actual culprit. Schema.get_entry has many callers besides orchestrator (sync/watcher.ex:213 with change.name, presence/identity.ex × 5, reflog/snapshot.ex × 4, merge_command/handler.ex:229, green/bursar.ex × 2, tree/walk.ex:66 with segment, tree/merge.ex:446) — any of which could be passing a non-binary that bubbles up to orchestrator's rescue.

**Schema.get_entry/2 signature:**
  def get_entry(doc, name) when is_binary(name) do  # apps/commonplace/lib/commonplace/tree/schema.ex:127

The :is_binary guard is what's failing. Caller is passing nil, an atom, or some other non-binary.

**Next step (when picked up):**
1. Replace Logger.error at orchestrator.ex:94 with Logger.error("... \n\#{Exception.format(:error, e, __STACKTRACE__)}") so the next repro pinpoints the caller in one shot.
2. Then either (a) fix the caller to coerce non-binary to binary, or (b) loosen Schema.get_entry to handle non-binary (probably wrong — guard is the right discipline).

**Out of scope:** Workaround. The error is non-fatal and doesn't block any user-visible functionality. Just spam.

Filed per coordination with boss-clod (msg #2801) during workspace MCP relaunch effort. The relaunch proceeded; this is the followup.
close_reason: Root cause: orchestrator's read_source/2 was called with config.source = nil for processes that declare no source file (e.g. sandbox-exec processes). Schema.get_entry/2's is_binary(name) guard rejected nil, raising FunctionClauseError every reconcile tick. Fixed in 88324f6 with nil-source guard in detect_source_changes/2 and is_binary guard on read_source itself. Also improved error logging at the rescue site to format full stacktrace via Exception.format/3 so any future Schema.get_entry mismatch is diagnosable in one shot.

title: Remove hand-rolled MCP substrate after anubis port
description:
Once CX-hf71 ports the MCP server onto anubis_mcp and the new substrate is confirmed working end-to-end, remove the now-redundant hand-rolled substrate:

**To delete:**
- apps/commonplace_mcp/lib/commonplace_mcp/protocol.ex (JSON-RPC 2.0 codec — anubis has equivalent)
- apps/commonplace_mcp/lib/commonplace_mcp/stdio.ex (line-delimited stdio loop — Anubis.Server.Transport.STDIO replaces)
- apps/commonplace_mcp/lib/commonplace_mcp/server.ex (dispatch struct + handlers — replaced by anubis server callbacks)
- Their tests (test/commonplace_mcp/{protocol,stdio,server}_test.exs)

**Stays:**
- apps/commonplace_mcp/lib/commonplace_mcp.ex (escript entry, presence bootstrap, CheckoutRegistry routing, mailbox onramp)
- apps/commonplace_mcp/lib/commonplace_mcp/anubis.ex (facade)
- apps/commonplace_mcp/lib/commonplace_mcp/tools/* (tools themselves — implementations stay; only the registration surface changes)
- apps/commonplace_mcp/lib/commonplace_mcp/resources.ex

**Gate:** all CX-hf71 acceptance criteria met, anubis-backed server exercised in tests AND manually via Claude Code.

**Why separate from CX-hf71:** removing the fallback while porting means if the port has a subtle bug (tool schema mismatch, client edge case), we can't bisect or pause. Keep both alive until the port is proven, then remove in a separate clean commit.

**Risk:** if anubis misses a capability the hand-rolled path handled (e.g. a specific error shape Claude Code expects), we'd want the fallback back. This bead closes only when a full rotation of Claude-Code sessions, each test, and each real tool invocation have been verified on the anubis path.

**Depends on:** CX-hf71.
notes: Filed per jes instruction in clod-squad msg #2717 — two separate beads (port + remove) so removal is gated on the port proving clean.

title: [bug] Sync.LiveSyncIntegrationTest 'peer-to-peer sync via shared CRDT file modification on one peer propagates to the other' is flaky
description:

title: Yelixer.Doc-level clientID_in_namespace?/3 cache (CX-ch5 follow-up)
description:
CX-ch5 spec called for a Doc-level namespace index — Yelixer.Doc would track 'which namespace introduced each clientID' as new struct state, populated by a namespace-aware apply_update variant, exposed via Yelixer.Doc.clientID_in_namespace?/3.

CX-ch5 deferred this in favor of keeping the existing commit-chain-walk validator (Commonplace.Store.Namespace.validate_commit_from_db/2). The walk-based validator already satisfies CX-ch5's acceptance criteria for namespace rejection.

The Doc-level cache becomes load-bearing once CX-umz lands snapshot ops with derivation maps — at that point the validator needs O(1) lookups against snapshot-introduced clientIDs that aren't reachable by walking parent chains.

Scope when picked up:
- Add :client_namespaces field to Yelixer.Doc struct.
- Yelixer.Encoding.apply_update_in_namespace/3 (or extend apply_update with an opts arg) populates the field when processing an update under a declared namespace.
- Yelixer.Doc.clientID_in_namespace?/3 returns membership at O(1).
- Decide whether to keep the commit-walk validator as a parallel source-of-truth or switch import_commit to Doc-state queries — depends on whether snapshot construction (CX-umz) can populate the Doc-state in time.

Reference: docs/namespace-model.md § Identification: Envelope, Not Prefix.
close_reason: Doc-level namespace index shipped at b7ca995. Yelixer.Doc now has :client_namespaces field (default %{}), populated by new apply_update_in_namespace/3 variant and queried via clientID_in_namespace?/3 at O(1). First-writer-wins semantics: a clientID already recorded under ns_a is NOT overwritten when re-seen under ns_b. Plain apply_update/2 doesn't touch the index — callers opt in via the namespace-aware variant. Default validator NOT swapped to Doc-index per CX-ch5 close-note: the commit-chain-walk remains authoritative since it has full historical context across snapshots; Doc-index is a parallel read optimization. 8 new tests covering empty defaults, single-ns tracking, repeat-apply idempotence, cross-ns isolation, first-writer-wins, multi-clientID populate, and plain-apply no-op. Full suite: yelixer 327/0, commonplace 1071/0, cli 55/0, mcp 44/0, web 41/0.

title: Sync.AgentTest 'bidirectional edits on disk and CRDT both appear after sync' is flaky on CI
description:
apps/commonplace/test/commonplace/sync/agent_test.exs:154 fails intermittently on CI. Pre-existing — confirmed during 2026-04-19 session by reverting all in-flight changes and seeing the failure persist on main.

FAILURE: `File.read!("/tmp/cp_agent_sync_<rand>/crdt_file.txt")` raises File.Error :enoent at line 188.

SCENARIO: test creates a disk file, syncs once (disk → CRDT), then adds a CRDT-side doc + chains it into root schema, edits the disk file, calls Agent.sync_once a second time, asserts disk_file.txt has new content AND crdt_file.txt was written to disk. The second assert fails — the inbound CRDT → disk export didn't write crdt_file.txt.

LIKELY: race between phase-1 outbound (which mutates root via watcher.apply_modify) and phase-2 inbound (which walks root schema for files to export). The Agent's GenServer serializes calls to sync_once but the schema-walk inside one call may be racing with the schema-rewrite from outbound.

REPRO: runs 100% pass on jes's laptop; CI hits ~1/5 cases. Probably filesystem-speed dependent.

Out-of-scope for the CI-recovery sweep that brought CI down to this single failure (commits 9424c48 / 87e6fd4 / 65ec22b / 882272a). File for a focused investigation when bug-squashing time comes back around.
close_reason: Flake root cause: Sync.Agent fired reflog checkpoint via Task.start and returned; checkpoint's load+mutate+create_chained_commit on root_uuid raced with any concurrent writer (test, remote peer, MCP). Each writer encoded its pre-race view, last-writer-wins on :latest, and reconstruct_snapshot (applies only :latest.update) silently dropped earlier writer's mutations. In the failing scenario, crdt_file.txt got dropped from root schema → Phase 2 export skipped it → File.read! :enoent. Fixed by running checkpoint synchronously within sync_once (commit 3368000). Also corrected test's misuse of CommitStore.create_commit(root, _, nil) → create_chained_commit. Repro before: ~80% local. Repro after: 10/10 pass. Full suite: yelixer 319/0, commonplace 1056/0, cli 55/0, mcp 44/0, web 41/0. Trade-off: sync_once now blocks on checkpoint (slower on deep trees); if user-visible, follow-up can add Agent.await_checkpoint/1 and restore async pattern.

title: Leaf-doc merge log: __merge.log placement when {path} resolves to non-schema
description:
Follow-up to CX-3hvu (which scopes the merge-command onramp to schema-target merges only). When a magenta merge command addresses a path that resolves to a non-schema leaf (e.g. a Text doc), CX-3hvu returns :not_a_schema as a deferred failure mode.

Candidate designs to evaluate:
(a) Sibling in parent: log lives in PARENT schema under name "{basename}.__merge.log". Works for any leaf with a schema parent. Analogous to how VCS systems co-locate metadata next to files.
(b) Derived UUID doc: log UUID deterministically derived from target UUID (e.g. UUID5 in a namespace). No schema entry needed. Pro: uniform, no parent-schema dependency. Con: no way to traverse to the log from the tree.
(c) Workspace-root log with path key: single __merge.log at workspace root, events carry {path} field to disambiguate. Pro: simplest storage. Con: not "per-document" in the bead sense.

Scope:
- Pick a design (likely need jes + plan-bot input)
- Update MergeCommand.Handler to handle leaf-doc paths, replacing the :not_a_schema short-circuit shipped in CX-3hvu
- Add test: magenta merge command on a path resolving to a Text leaf → merge succeeds → merge_completed event persists in the appropriate log

Acceptance: the E2E test for merging a leaf doc passes; MergeCommand.Handler no longer returns :not_a_schema for valid leaf-doc paths.

Depends on CX-3hvu (primitive layer).
close_reason: Shipped. MergeCommand.Handler now branches on target shape: schema targets keep traversable __merge.log schema entry; leaf targets use UUID5-derived log_uuid (no schema entry written, leaf chain untouched). Discriminator uses DocBuilder.reconstruct_doc + Doc.has_type? (Schema.version not reliable post-snapshot). Bonus: exposed latent test-isolation bug in CX-1mml cross-peer test — fixed by giving each peer a distinct path in its own root. Suite: 1583/0.

title: Heuristic lull-aware snapshot trigger
description:
Context quotes:

"I think I want it done heuristically, like after enough edits to be interesting, but ideally during a lull, but forcefully at some threshold. Maybe the automatic mandatory threshold is the higher priority, and heuristic is a nice to have." — jes, 2026-04-18

"Deterministic-anyone snapshotting (CX-umz) means multiple hooks can race safely; concurrent snapshots at the same parent dedup via CID. No coordination required."

Scope:
- Extends the producer-side hook with a "interesting enough + lull-aware" layer
- Soft counter: N edits since last snapshot where N < mandatory threshold
- Prefers to wait for quiet period (no edits for X seconds) before firing
- If lull never comes AND mandatory threshold crossed, Bead A's hard check fires anyway — so Bead F is strictly additive

Acceptance: under sustained load → only Bead A's mandatory fires; under bursty load with quiet gaps → fires during first post-interesting lull
close_reason: Heuristic lull-aware layer shipped at 2f3aca2. SnapshotTrigger.maybe_snapshot/3 now takes :soft_chain_length_threshold + :lull_window_ms opts; when both set, fires when chain >= soft threshold AND latest commit older than window. Mandatory threshold always wins. Producer-side wiring in EntryAgent threads :soft_snapshot_chain_threshold + :snapshot_lull_window_ms into the trigger call via the same pattern as CX-tvyb's mandatory opt. :now opt for deterministic test time injection (defaults to System.system_time(:millisecond)). 8 new tests + entry_agent suite preserved. Full suite: yelixer 319/0, commonplace 1071/0, cli 55/0, mcp 44/0, web 41/0. Acceptance met: sustained load → only mandatory fires; bursty load with lull → fires during first post-interesting lull; mandatory always wins; soft-only or lull-only → inert (both required together). CX-1t0t superseded by this work.

title: Heuristic snapshot trigger with lull detection
description:
Soft snapshot trigger preferring to fire during a lull. From jes 2026-04-18: 'I think I want it done heuristically, like after enough edits to be interesting, but ideally during a lull, but forcefully at some threshold. Maybe the automatic mandatory threshold is the higher priority, and heuristic is a nice to have.'

Scope:
- Soft trigger: 'enough edits to be interesting' — something like N edits since last snapshot where N < the mandatory threshold
- Prefers to wait for a lull (period of no edits for X seconds) before firing the snapshot
- Forceful fallback: if the lull never comes AND the mandatory threshold is crossed, the hard trigger from the mandatory-threshold bead fires
- Strictly additive — it just gets the snapshot written earlier when conditions are favorable
- Hook point: same sync agent as the mandatory-threshold bead

Depends on CX-3vc2 (reuses threshold logic as the forceful-fallback floor).

Acceptance: under sustained load, only the hard trigger fires; under bursty load with quiet gaps, snapshot fires during the first post-interesting lull.

title: Snapshot-parents: second Merkle tree linking snapshot commits
description:
Introduce a snapshot-level DAG as a second Merkle tree layered over the
commit DAG. Every snapshot commit carries an additional reference to
its immediate prior snapshot (its snapshot-parent), distinct from its
commit-DAG parent_commit. History can then be navigated at two
granularities: the fine-grained commit chain (today) and the
coarse-grained snapshot chain (new).

## Unlocks

- **Cheap history traversal at time T**: walk snapshot-parent edges
  back to the last snapshot ≤ T, then fast-forward incrementals.
  O(snapshots) instead of O(commits) for long-lived docs.
- **First-class branches**: a branch is a snapshot whose
  snapshot-parent is shared with another snapshot. Fork/merge gets a
  representation at the snapshot layer instead of being inferred from
  Schema tree entries.
- **Tighter concurrent-snapshot detection**: two snapshots with the
  same snapshot-parent but different content = true concurrent
  snapshot. Today this topology is hidden under a flat commit chain.
- **Faster rebase baseline reconstruction**: CX-6a7's positional
  rebase currently calls reconstruct_doc_at(parent_commit) which walks
  the full commit chain. With snapshot-parents, it can walk snapshot
  edges first and apply only the trailing incrementals.

## Cost

- One additional CID reference per snapshot commit's metadata.
- Snapshot creation logic picks the snapshot-parent (latest prior
  snapshot reachable on the chain being snapshotted).
- Migration for existing stores: historical snapshots lack the
  snapshot-parent edge. Either (a) backfill by walking parent_commit
  chains to find prior snapshots, or (b) accept nil for legacy.

## Interaction with CX-6a7

None immediate — positional rebase operates on (old_doc, dirty_doc,
new_doc) and doesn't care how new_doc was reconstructed. But once
snapshot-parents exist, rebase's baseline path can use them as a
shortcut. CX-6a7 ships cleanly without this; this ships cleanly on
top of CX-6a7.

## Recommendation

Pick up after CX-6a7 closes (after Phase 2 CX-9fy ships). Treat as its
own epic; likely decomposes into:
- snapshot-parent metadata field + write path in
  CommitStore.create_snapshot_commit
- read path / traversal API in CommitStore / DocBuilder
- rebase baseline optimization (optional follow-up)
- branch/merge semantics on top of snapshot DAG (larger follow-up)
close_reason: Snapshot-DAG exposure landed at 289be3f. SnapshotAncestry.snapshot_chain/2 returns [genesis_id, s1, s2, ..., current_namespace] by walking metadata.snapshot_parents from the input's namespace back to genesis. The DAG itself was already built: CX-umz stamps snapshot_parents on snapshot commits, CX-bv3 auto-stamps snapshot_parent on regular commits, CX-ntz5 introduced the internal walker. What was missing was public traversal for callers other than LCA (CX-ntz5/Build 7.1) — now shipped. 7 unit tests covering fresh doc, single/multi-snapshot chains, snapshot-as-input, genesis-as-input, unknown-commit, and the merge-snapshot first-parent MVP. Write-path (stamping), LCA, and compose_dms already existed; this bead's deliverable is the public API. Follow-ups (rebase baseline optimization via snapshot-DAG shortcuts, siblings/concurrent-snapshot detection with cross-ref index, full merge-snapshot DAG walk) remain as separate tickets if prioritized.

title: Advance parent_commit on remote-incremental apply (rebase baseline tightening)
description:
Follow-on to CX-dqn Phase 1 positional rebase.

The 2-way diff (pre, dirty) used by Rebase.rebase treats any remote incremental commits applied to state.doc between parent_commit and a snapshot as if they were local dirty edits. If the incoming snapshot already contains those same incrementals, replaying the diff on new_doc will double-apply them.

Fix: advance state.parent_commit when applying a non-snapshot remote commit, so 'pre' tightly reflects 'last incorporated state'. This requires deciding how parent_commit interacts with local commit chaining (we probably want a separate 'last_sync_commit' marker that's used only for the rebase baseline; local commits keep chaining off the actual parent).

Files touched (likely):
  * apps/commonplace/lib/commonplace/document/server.ex — add last_sync_commit to state
  * apps/commonplace/lib/commonplace/document/rebase.ex — update limitation note
  * apps/commonplace/test/commonplace/document/server_sync_test.exs — add regression test: incremental-then-snapshot should not double-apply
close_reason: Shipped: advance :latest + parent_commit on remote-incremental apply. Regression test added. 724/724 commonplace tests pass. Commit 2f72ba2.

title: Positional-rebase phase 4: YArray rebase (LCS + identity function contract)
description:

Per RFC §YArray + §Intent-loss + §YArray item churn:

Scope (~150 LOC):
  * LCS / Myers on item sequence.
  * Scalar items: deep-equal as identity fallback.
  * Structured items: require user-supplied identity function OR accept delete+reinsert churn on reorder.
  * Identity function registration (per RFC §Open Questions — leaning per-doc schema annotation matching CP-o3f4 sync-flag pattern).
  * Tests: YArray of YMaps with identity function → clean diff; without → documented churn (correct but non-minimal history).
